category: AIP – Implementation and Integration
stem: A financial services organization has built a custom machine learning (ML) model designed for real-time fraud detection. The model, which is hosted on the company’s on-premises infrastructure, is less than 5 GB in size and processes up to 50 concurrent requests simultaneously. The company is exploring AWS services to migrate its model to the cloud while minimizing infrastructure management. The development team is familiar with Amazon Rekognition for image-based analysis and Amazon Textract for document analysis, and is now looking for the best service to deploy the fraud detection model. Which of the following will meet the given requirements with the least operational overhead?
correct_text: Create a model configuration within Amazon SageMaker AI, then deploy the custom fraud detection model on a serverless SageMaker endpoint.

candidates.full_text: Hosting - un modelo de fraude near real-time y baja latencia pesa menos de 1 GB, recibe como maximo 10 peticiones concurrentes y hoy corre on-premises. La empresa quiere hostearlo en AWS sin administrar ni optimizar la infraestructura , con el MENOR esfuerzo. Que solucion conviene? A. Configurar el modelo como SageMaker AI Model y servirlo en un endpoint serverless de SageMaker AI B. Configurar el modelo como SageMaker AI Model y usar batch transform para inferencia C. Construir un contenedor del modelo y desplegarlo con Amazon ECS sobre AWS Fargate D. Importar el modelo a Amazon Comprehend Custom Classification y usar su API en tiempo real

A media company has hybrid architecture with Direct Connect. 50TB+ digital videos on on-premises tape library used by Media Asset Management (MAM) system. Want automated catalog with facial recognition, minimal disruption, least management overhead . Eventually migrate to AWS. Which solution uses LEAST ongoing management overhead with MINIMAL disruption? A. Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to set up video ingestion stream with Amazon Rekognition, build face collection. Stream media files from MAM into Kinesis, configure Rekognition to process streamed files. Launch stream consumer for metadata, push to MAM, store files in S3. B. Set up tape gateway on-premises connected to AWS Storage Gateway. Configure MAM to fetch files from archive, push to tape gateway for Glacier storage. Use Rekognition with Lambda function to process video from tape gateway in real-time. C. Integrate local data center file system to AWS Storage Gateway via file gateway on-premises. MAM extracts files and sends to file gateway. Build Rekognition collection, use Lambda to process files from S3 bucket backing file gateway. D. Request AWS Snowball to migrate files to S3. Provision large EC2 instance, install open-source facial recognition tools like OpenFace/OpenCV. Process files for metadata, push to MAM, copy files to another S3 bucket. ✅ C File Gateway with Rekognition 🎯 File Gateway provides seamless integration with existing MAM system while enabling real-time processing with Rekognition. Tape Gateway can't process files in real-time from Glacier. ⚠️ A Kinesis Video Streams — Requires major MAM changes, designed for streaming not archived files ⚠️ B Tape Gateway — Can't process files real-time from Glacier archive ⚠️ D Snowball + EC2 — High management overhead with open-source tools vs managed Rekognition 📖 Full Explanation Amazon Rekognition can store information about detected faces in server-side containers known as collections. You can use the facial information that's stored in a collection to search for known faces in images, stored videos, and streaming videos. Amazon Rekognition supports the IndexFaces operation. You can use this operation to detect faces in an image and persist information about facial features that are detected in a collection. This is an example of a storage-based API operation because the service persists information on the server. To store facial information, you must first create (CreateCollection) a face collection in one of the AWS Regions in your account. You specify this face collection when you call the IndexFaces operation. After you create a face collection and store facial feature information for all faces, you can search the collection for face matches. To search for faces in an image, call SearchFacesByImage. To search for faces in a stored video, call StartFaceSearch. To search for faces in a streaming video, call CreateStreamProcessor. AWS Storage Gateway offers file-based, volume-based, and tape-based storage solutions. With a tape gateway, you can cost-effectively and durably archive backup data in GLACIER or DEEP_ARCHIVE. A tape gateway provides a virtual tape infrastructure that scales seamlessly with your business needs and eliminates the operational burden of provisioning, scaling, and maintaining a physical tape infrastructure. You can run AWS Storage Gateway either on-premises as a VM appliance, as a hardware appliance, or in AWS as an Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance. You deploy your gateway on an EC2 instance to provision iSCSI storage volumes in AWS. You can use gateways hosted on EC2 instances for disaster recovery, data mirroring, and providing storage for applications hosted on Amazon EC2. Hence, the correct answer is: Integrate the file system of your local data center to AWS Storage Gateway by setting up a file gateway appliance on-premises. Utilize the MAM solution to extract the media files from the current data store and send them into the file gateway. Build a collection using Amazon Rekognition by populating a catalog of faces from the processed media files. Use an AWS Lambda function to invoke Amazon Rekognition Javascript SDK to have it fetch the media file from the S3 bucket which is backing the file gateway, retrieve the needed metadata, and finally, persist the information into the MAM solution. The option that says: Request for an AWS Snowball Storage Optimized device to migrate all of the media files from the on-premises library into Amazon S3. Provision a large EC2 instance and allow it to access the S3 bucket. Install an open-source facial recognition tool on the instance like OpenFace or OpenCV. Process the media files to retrieve the metadata and push this information into the MAM solution. Lastly, copy the media files to another S3 bucket is incorrect. This entails a lot of ongoing management overhead instead of just using Amazon Rekognition. Moreover, it is more suitable to use the AWS Storage Gateway service rather than an EBS Volume. The option that says: Set up a tape gateway appliance on-premises and connect it to your AWS Storage Gateway. Configure the MAM solution to fetch the media files from the current archive and push them into the tape gateway to be stored in Amazon Glacier. Using Amazon Rekognition, build a collection from the catalog of faces. Utilize a Lambda function which invokes the Rekognition Javascript SDK to have Amazon Rekognition process the video directly from the tape gateway in real-time, retrieve the required metadata, and push the metadata into the MAM solution is incorrect. Although this solution uses the right combination of AWS Storage Gateway and Amazon Rekognition, take note that you can't directly fetch the media files from your tape gateway in real time since this is backed up using Glacier. Although the on-premises data center is using a tape gateway, you can still set up a solution to use a file gateway in order to properly process the videos using Amazon Rekognition. Keep in mind that the tape gateway in the AWS Storage Gateway service is primarily used as an archive solution. The option that says: Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to set up a video ingestion stream and with Amazon Rekognition, build a collection of faces. Stream the media files from the MAM solution into Kinesis Video Streams and configure the Amazon Rekognition to process the streamed files. Launch a stream consumer to retrieve the required metadata, and push the metadata into the MAM solution. Finally, configure the stream to store the files in an S3 bucket is incorrect. This approach requires significant changes to the existing MAM solution to stream media files directly into Kinesis Video Streams, potentially causing more disruption to the current workflow. Additionally, Kinesis Video Streams is designed for real-time video streaming and processing, which may not be the most efficient approach for processing pre-existing media files stored in a tape library. Lastly, setting up and managing Kinesis Video Streams, configuring Amazon Rekognition integration, implementing a stream consumer, and storing files in S3 introduces additional complexity and management overhead compared to the File Gateway approach.

A media company with a hybrid architecture has 50+ TB of digital videos stored on on-premises tape library. They want to implement automated facial recognition catalog with minimal disruption to existing MAM system and least management overhead . Eventually migrate to AWS. Which solution provides the least ongoing management overhead with minimal disruption? A. Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams for ingestion and Amazon Rekognition for facial recognition processing B. Set up tape gateway appliance and process videos directly from tape gateway using Lambda and Rekognition C. Set up file gateway appliance, use MAM to send files to gateway, process with Lambda and Rekognition from S3 D. Use AWS Snowball to migrate files to S3, install open-source facial recognition on EC2 instance ✅ C. File Gateway with Lambda and Rekognition processing 🎯 Why correct: File Gateway provides seamless integration with existing MAM system while automatically backing files to S3. Rekognition can directly process files from S3 with minimal architectural changes. ⚠️ A. Kinesis Video Streams Requires significant changes to MAM solution to stream files into Kinesis. Designed for real-time streaming, not processing pre-existing archived files from tape library. ⚠️ B. Tape Gateway processing Cannot process videos directly from tape gateway in real-time since it's backed by Glacier storage. Files must be retrieved from archive before processing, adding latency. ⚠️ D. Snowball + open-source tools Requires significant management overhead to maintain open-source facial recognition on EC2. Less accurate than managed Rekognition service and requires custom development.

A company receives sensor data every millisecond from manufacturing equipment and needs to detect anomalies in real-time to prevent equipment failure. Which AWS service is best suited for this use case? A. Amazon SQS with Lambda processing B. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Analytics C. Amazon S3 with scheduled EMR jobs D. Amazon RDS with stored procedures ✅ B. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Analytics 🎯 Trigger keywords: "every millisecond" + "real-time anomaly detection" = streaming analytics requirement. Kinesis Data Streams ingests high-frequency sensor data, while Kinesis Analytics runs SQL queries for real-time anomaly detection using sliding windows and statistical functions. SQS + Lambda: SQS has throughput limits and Lambda has execution time limits - not suitable for continuous millisecond data streams requiring real-time processing.

The department of education is building a learning portal in AWS to supplement their on-premises network . They need a highly available cloud infrastructure with multiple Availability Zones . Requirements: aggregate logs , automate log analysis for errors , and immediately notify IT Operations when errors breach thresholds . Which solution BEST meets these requirements? A. Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus on-premises → AWS Lambda for metrics → CloudWatch Alarm B. Amazon Kinesis agent on-premises → CloudWatch Logs → metric filter → QuickSight monitoring C. CloudWatch agent on-premises → EventBridge → metric filter → Athena monitoring D. CloudWatch agent on-premises → CloudWatch Logs → metric filter → CloudWatch Alarm ✅ D. CloudWatch agent → CloudWatch Logs → metric filter → CloudWatch Alarm 🎯 Why correct: CloudWatch agent is the proper service for collecting on-premises logs and sending to CloudWatch Logs. Metric filters convert log data to numerical metrics, and CloudWatch Alarms provide immediate notifications when thresholds are breached. ⚠️ A. Prometheus + Lambda approach Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is designed for container metrics, not general log processing. Creating custom Lambda functions for log processing is unnecessary complexity when CloudWatch already provides this functionality natively. ⚠️ B. Kinesis agent approach Kinesis agent is for streaming data ingestion, not log collection from on-premises servers. QuickSight is a business intelligence tool, not designed for real-time alerting and monitoring compared to CloudWatch Alarms. ⚠️ C. EventBridge destination Logs should go to CloudWatch Logs, not EventBridge which is for event routing. Athena is for querying data, not real-time monitoring and alerting like CloudWatch Alarms.

category: AIP – Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
stem: A financial analytics company is building a customer-facing chatbot that uses a large language model (LLM) to answer domain-specific questions about investment products and compliance policies. The company has thousands of PDF documents stored in an Amazon S3 bucket that contain detailed policy explanations and financial regulations. The AI engineering team wants the chatbot to retrieve precise answers from these documents instead of relying solely on the LLM’s pre-trained knowledge. The goal is to implement a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach to ground the model’s responses with proprietary data. The team is evaluating whether to use Amazon Kendra or Amazon Bedrock to manage this retrieval pipeline efficiently while maintaining scalability and minimal infrastructure overhead. Which solution provides the most effective and AWS-managed way to integrate proprietary document retrieval with an LLM for this RAG-based chatbot?
correct_text: Configure a knowledge base in Bedrock. Add the S3 bucket as the connected data source, and utilize the Bedrock API to perform RAG queries that dynamically combine document retrieval with LLM generation.

candidates.full_text: Chatbot RAG sobre PDFs en S3 con LLMs. Que par de soluciones hace buscables las guias operativas para el chatbot? A. Convertir los PDFs a texto y guardarlos en Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, y transformarlos con AWS Glue hacia Amazon RDS B. Guardar los PDFs convertidos en Aurora PostgreSQL, y extraer entidades con Comprehend hacia DynamoDB C. Extraer entidades y frases clave con Amazon Comprehend hacia DynamoDB, y transformar los PDFs con AWS Glue hacia RDS D. Ingerir los PDFs en una base vectorial de Amazon OpenSearch Service, y crear una knowledge base en Bedrock con Titan Embeddings G1 usando los PDFs en S3

RAG - un chatbot RAG de salud debe seguir mejorando y dar respuestas precisas y oportunas con el tiempo. Como asegurar la mejora continua? A. Usar Amazon Comprehend para analizar las consultas de los usuarios y las respuestas del chatbot e identificar areas de mejora continua B. Actualizar periodicamente la base de conocimiento con documentos nuevos y reentrenar el modelo de embeddings por completo desde cero C. Implementar un sistema basado en reglas para curar manualmente y actualizar la base de conocimiento con la informacion nueva D. Implementar un bucle de retroalimentacion donde los usuarios califican las respuestas y ese feedback afina el LLM y el prompt

RAG (PDFs) - hay que hacer que documentos PDF sean consultables por un chatbot LLM usando RAG. Que almacen es apto para guardar la informacion y recuperarla por similitud? A. Una base de datos Amazon Redshift (data warehouse relacional) B. Un volumen de Amazon EFS (file storage) donde ingestar los documentos C. Una base de datos vectorial de Amazon OpenSearch Service (o Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases) D. Un bucket de Amazon S3 (object storage) donde ingestar los documentos

A company has thousands of scanned PDF invoices and needs to automatically extract vendor names, amounts, and line items for processing in their accounting system. Which AWS service best addresses this requirement? A. Amazon Rekognition B. Amazon Textract C. Amazon Comprehend D. Amazon Kendra ✅ B. Amazon Textract 🎯 Key trigger: "Extract structured data from scanned documents" maps directly to Textract's AnalyzeExpense API, which is specifically designed for invoice and receipt processing to extract vendor names, amounts, and line items. ⚠️ A. Rekognition - General computer vision, not optimized for structured document data extraction ⚠️ C. Comprehend - Natural language processing for sentiment/entity analysis, not document structure extraction ⚠️ D. Kendra - Enterprise search service, not document data extraction

Chatbot RAG con Amazon Bedrock. Los registros sanitizados todavia no estan en la nube (aun no existe el bucket de almacenamiento) y hay que armar la knowledge base desde cero. Ordenando el flujo real, cual es el primer paso ? A. Crear una instancia de Amazon RDS para alojar las transacciones B. Cargar la informacion dentro de la knowledge base ya creada C. Crear el bucket de Amazon S3 que alojara los registros sanitizados D. Configurar una knowledge base en Bedrock enlazada al bucket S3

category: AIP – Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
stem: A global wildlife research organization is developing an automated monitoring system to track endangered species using camera trap images collected from remote conservation areas. Image data is uploaded to Amazon S3, and Amazon Rekognition performs an initial scan to identify frames that likely contain animals instead of empty backgrounds. Filtered images are then passed to a custom deep learning model, built using an Amazon SageMaker AI algorithm, to detect and count individual animals within each image accurately. The project requires distinguishing between multiple species, such as elephants, tigers, and rhinos, while also determining the exact position of each animal in the frame. Bounding boxes must be generated for every detected animal to analyze population density and movement patterns over time. The final model will be integrated into an automated analytics pipeline that updates a conservation dashboard used by field researchers and policy teams. Which modeling approach should be implemented in SageMaker AI to both identify animal species and locate each one precisely within the images?
correct_text: Use a SageMaker AI object detection algorithm to accurately identify and localize multiple animal species by generating bounding boxes and associated class labels.

candidates.full_text: SageMaker - se necesita identificar un articulo en una imagen y dar su ubicacion (bounding box) en estanterias en tiempo real. Que algoritmo integrado conviene? A. Random Cut Forest (detecta anomalias en series de tiempo y datos tabulares) B. Object Detection - MXNet (detecta y localiza objetos con bounding boxes) C. K-Means Clustering (agrupa vectores numericos por similitud, no supervisado) D. Object2Vec (aprende embeddings vectoriales de objetos discretos para similitud)

A company receives sensor data every millisecond from manufacturing equipment and needs to detect anomalies in real-time to prevent equipment failure. Which AWS service is best suited for this use case? A. Amazon SQS with Lambda processing B. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Analytics C. Amazon S3 with scheduled EMR jobs D. Amazon RDS with stored procedures ✅ B. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Analytics 🎯 Trigger keywords: "every millisecond" + "real-time anomaly detection" = streaming analytics requirement. Kinesis Data Streams ingests high-frequency sensor data, while Kinesis Analytics runs SQL queries for real-time anomaly detection using sliding windows and statistical functions. SQS + Lambda: SQS has throughput limits and Lambda has execution time limits - not suitable for continuous millisecond data streams requiring real-time processing.

A startup develops IoT pet collars that collect biometric data every second and send it via POST API to a web portal. The portal must provide real-time analytics , trends, and health reports to global pet owners with high durability, availability, and scalability . Which architecture best meets these requirements? A. Use Kinesis Data Streams → Kinesis analytics → S3 → Redshift with backups B. SQS queue → Kinesis analytics → RDS MySQL C. S3 bucket → Data Pipeline daily analysis → Redshift OLAP D. EMR instance → Kinesis analytics → DynamoDB ✅ A. Kinesis Data Streams → analytics → S3 → Redshift 🎯 Kinesis Data Streams handles high-frequency streaming data and enables real-time analytics, perfect for second-by-second biometric collection. ⚠️ B. SQS — Not designed for high-frequency streaming data analytics ⚠️ C. Data Pipeline — Daily batch processing, not real-time ⚠️ D. EMR — Not appropriate for data collection, only processing 📖 Full Explanation Amazon Kinesis Data Streams enable you to build custom applications that process or analyze streaming data for specialized needs. Kinesis Data Streams can continuously capture and store terabytes of data per hour from hundreds of thousands of sources. With the Kinesis Client Library (KCL), you can build applications for real-time dashboards, generate alerts, and emit data to other AWS services like S3, Redshift, EMR, and Lambda. The correct architecture uses Kinesis for streaming collection, real-time analytics, S3 for storage, and Redshift for complex analytics with automated backups. Option B is wrong because SQS queues aren't appropriate for high-frequency streaming data. Option C is wrong because Data Pipeline runs daily batch jobs, not real-time processing. Option D is wrong because EMR instances aren't designed for data collection, only processing.

A data analytics startup will develop a FIFA World Cup statistics system for global access. The system must track game statistics, allow voting for best players/coaches, and handle 10-30 million queries on game days . Requirements: durable storage , high availability , high scalability , and cost-effective . Which is the most cost-effective solution meeting these requirements? A. Multi-AZ RDS + ElastiCache reports + default expire parameters B. Multi-AZ RDS + DynamoDB storage + daily table deletion C. Multi-AZ RDS with Read Replicas + query replicas + daily cleanup D. Multi-AZ RDS with Read Replicas + S3 batch reports + CloudFront CDN with daily TTL ✅ D. Multi-AZ RDS with Read Replicas + S3 batch reports + CloudFront CDN with daily TTL 🎯 Combines scalable database (RDS Multi-AZ + Read Replicas), durable storage (S3), and global distribution (CloudFront) for cost-effective handling of millions of global queries. ⚠️ A. ElastiCache — lacks durable storage and CDN for global distribution ⚠️ B. RDS + DynamoDB — maintaining both databases is not cost-effective ⚠️ C. Read Replicas only — missing durable storage and CDN components 📖 Full Explanation In this scenario, you are required to have the following: A durable storage for the generated reports. A database that is highly available and can scale to handle millions of queries. A Content Delivery Network that can distribute the report files to users all over the world. Amazon S3 is object storage built to store and retrieve any amount of data from anywhere. It's a simple storage service that offers industry leading durability, availability, performance, security, and virtually unlimited scalability at very low costs. Amazon RDS provides high availability and failover support for DB instances using Multi-AZ deployments. In a Multi-AZ deployment, Amazon RDS automatically provisions and maintains a synchronous standby replica in a different Availability Zone. The primary DB instance is synchronously replicated across Availability Zones to a standby replica to provide data redundancy, eliminate I/O freezes, and minimize latency spikes during system backups. Amazon RDS uses the MariaDB, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle, and PostgreSQL DB engines' built-in replication functionality to create a special type of DB instance called a read replica from a source DB instance. The source DB instance becomes the primary DB instance. Updates made to the primary DB instance are asynchronously copied to the read replica. Amazon CloudFront is a web service that speeds up distribution of your static and dynamic web content, such as .html, .css, .js, and image files, to your users. CloudFront delivers your content through a worldwide network of data centers called edge locations. When a user requests content that you're serving with CloudFront, the request is routed to the edge location that provides the lowest latency (time delay), so that content is delivered with the best possible performance. Hence, the following option is the best solution that satisfies all of these requirements: 1. Generate the FIFA reports from MySQL database in Multi-AZ RDS deployments configuration with Read Replicas. 2. Set up a batch job that puts reports in an S3 bucket. 3. Launch a CloudFront distribution to cache the content with a TTL set to expire objects daily. In the above, S3 provides durable storage; Multi-AZ RDS with Read Replicas provide a scalable and highly available database and CloudFront provides the CDN.

A company runs a sports web portal with resources in multiple AWS regions (EC2, RDS, IAM). The IT Security Compliance Officer requires a reliable and durable logging solution to track changes to all resources across all regions. The solution must ensure integrity and confidentiality of log data. Which solution would be the best option? A. Create a new trail in AWS CloudTrail with the global services option selected, and create one new Amazon S3 bucket to store the logs. Create IAM roles, S3 bucket policies, and enable Multi Factor Authentication (MFA) Delete on the S3 bucket storing your logs. B. Create three new CloudTrail trails, each with its own S3 bucket to store the logs: one for the AWS Management console, one for AWS SDKs, and one for command line tools. Then create IAM roles and S3 bucket policies for the S3 buckets storing your logs. C. Create a new trail in AWS CloudTrail with the global services option selected, and assign it an existing S3 bucket to store the logs. Create S3 ACLs and enable Multi Factor Authentication (MFA) delete on the S3 bucket storing your logs. D. Create a new trail in CloudTrail and assign it a new S3 bucket to store the logs. Configure AWS SNS to send delivery notifications to your management system. Secure the S3 bucket that stores your logs using IAM roles and S3 bucket policies. ✅ A. CloudTrail with global services + new S3 bucket + IAM roles + MFA Delete 🎯 Global services flag captures IAM events across regions, new S3 bucket ensures confidentiality, MFA Delete provides integrity protection. ⚠️ B — Creates unnecessary multiple trails without global services flag ⚠️ C — Uses existing S3 bucket (compromises confidentiality) and S3 ACLs instead of IAM roles ⚠️ D — Missing global services flag, won't capture IAM events 📖 Full Explanation For most services, events are recorded in the region where the action occurred to its respective AWS CloudTrail. For global services such as AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), AWS STS, Amazon CloudFront, and Route 53, events are delivered to any trail that includes global services (IncludeGlobalServiceEvents flag). AWS CloudTrail service should be your top choice for the scenarios where the application is tracking the changes made by any AWS service, resource, or API. AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) is integrated with AWS CloudTrail, a service that logs AWS events made by or on behalf of your AWS account. CloudTrail logs authenticate AWS API calls and also AWS sign-in events, and collects this event information in files that are delivered to Amazon S3 buckets. Therefore, the correct answer is: Create a new trail in AWS CloudTrail with the global services option selected, and create one new Amazon S3 bucket to store the logs. Create IAM roles, S3 bucket policies, and enable Multi Factor Authentication (MFA) Delete on the S3 bucket storing your logs. It uses AWS CloudTrail with (includeGlobalServiceEvents flag) Global Option enabled, a single new S3 bucket and IAM Roles so that it has the confidentiality, and MFA on Delete on S3 bucket so that it maintains the data integrity. The option that says: Create a new trail in AWS CloudTrail with the global services option selected, and assign it an existing S3 bucket to store the logs. Create S3 ACLs and enable Multi Factor Authentication (MFA) delete on the S3 bucket storing your logs is incorrect. As an existing S3 bucket is used, it may already be accessed by the user, hence not maintaining the confidentiality, and it is not using IAM roles. The option that says: Create three new CloudTrail trails, each with its own S3 bucket to store the logs: one for the AWS Management console, one for AWS SDKs, and one for command line tools. Then create IAM roles and S3 bucket policies for the S3 buckets storing your logs is incorrect. Although it uses AWS CloudTrail, the Global Option is not enabled, and three S3 buckets are not needed. The option that says: Create a new trail in CloudTrail and assign it a new S3 bucket to store the logs. Configure AWS SNS to send delivery notifications to your management system. Secure the S3 bucket that stores your logs using IAM roles and S3 bucket policies is incorrect. Although it uses AWS CloudTrail, the Global Option is not enabled.

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A financial services company uses Amazon SageMaker Studio notebooks for data exploration and SageMaker Autopilot to train ML models on customer data stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The dataset contains sensitive financial information, and compliance policies require that all data traffic remain within the AWS private network. During an audit, the security team discovers that SageMaker Studio is accessing S3 over the public internet. The AI developer must reconfigure the environment to ensure that all data transfers between SageMaker and S3 occur securely within AWS’s internal network while maintaining full functionality for Studio notebooks and Autopilot jobs. Which configuration should the developer implement to meet this requirement?
correct_text: Configure SageMaker Studio notebooks to run within a VPC and create a VPC Gateway Endpoint for S3 to ensure all traffic between SageMaker and S3 stays within the AWS private network.

candidates.full_text: MLOps - en un pipeline de despliegue se necesita un paso de aprobacion manual de la version del modelo antes de desplegar. Que enfoque cumple? A. Crear una SageMaker AI pipeline y actualizar el approval status de la version del modelo a Approved con Boto3 tras registrarla B. Configurar una accion de aprobacion manual en AWS CodePipeline que publique a un topic de Amazon SNS C. Usar SageMaker Studio para aprobar los modelos actualizando manualmente sus tags de metadatos en la consola D. Usar notebooks de SageMaker Studio para revisar y aprobar cada version del modelo a mano una por una

Pipelines - hay que construir un pipeline de ingestion que prepare datos crudos de S3 y ademas un pipeline de despliegue para entrenar y desplegar el modelo en tiempo real. Que servicios usar? A. Amazon Data Firehose para entregar los datos a S3 y SageMaker Batch Transform para servir la inferencia B. Amazon QuickSight para preparar los datos y una funcion AWS Lambda para desplegar el modelo C. Amazon Athena para consultar la ingestion y un notebook de SageMaker para desplegar el modelo a produccion D. AWS Glue para los pipelines de ingestion de datos y Amazon SageMaker Studio (Classic) para desplegar el modelo

Entrenamiento con datos sensibles que debe estar aislado de redes externas (sin acceso a internet durante el training). Que solucion cumple el requisito? A. Habilitar el modo network isolation de SageMaker AI en el training job B. Usar el cifrado en reposo y en transito integrado de SageMaker C. Usar SageMaker Canvas con un VPC interface endpoint para bloquear internet D. Guardar los datos de entrenamiento en un bucket S3 cifrado con acceso restringido

Preparaci n de datos - menor overhead: pron stico de demanda diaria con datos hist ricos de ventas que tienen timestamps irregulares y valores faltantes . Qu enfoque cumple con el MENOR esfuerzo operativo? A. Preparar y analizar los datos con Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler (transformaciones visuales listas) B. Visualizar y pronosticar directamente con Amazon QuickSight sin una etapa dedicada de limpieza de datos C. Procesar y pronosticar con Amazon EMR Serverless ejecutando trabajos PySpark personalizados D. Limpiar y pronosticar con un Amazon SageMaker Studio Notebook usando Pandas escrito a mano

Dataset sensible en un bucket de S3 en la region us-east-1 , pero las instancias de entrenamiento de SageMaker corren en una VPC de us-west-2 (otra region). El trafico hacia S3 NO debe exponerse a internet publico en ningun momento, sin duplicar los datos ni cambiar de servicio de transferencia. Que solucion aporta el acceso privado entre regiones ? A. Deshabilitar el acceso directo a internet y crear un gateway endpoint en la VPC de us-west-2, agregando su prefix list a la tabla de rutas para llegar al bucket B. Replicar el bucket con S3 Cross-Region Replication hacia us-west-2 y entrenar el modelo sobre esa copia local dentro de la misma VPC del training job C. Usar AWS Transfer Family con un endpoint SFTP para copiar el dataset a un bucket local en us-west-2 de forma segura antes de lanzar el entrenamiento D. Deshabilitar el acceso directo a internet y usar un interface endpoint (PrivateLink) combinado con VPC peering / Transit Gateway hacia la VPC de la region del bucket

category: AIP – Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
stem: A multinational publishing company is developing an internal AI-powered assistant to help employees retrieve, summarize, and analyze research documents. The company’s data-science team already relies on Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to label training data and improve metadata accuracy. The next development phase involves integrating AI agents in Amazon Bedrock that can autonomously answer questions, summarize lengthy documents, and recommend related content. To achieve this, the team requires a mechanism that can represent both user queries and document content as semantic embeddings that capture contextual relationships between concepts and terms. The solution must be fully managed, scalable, and easily integrated with existing AWS services to support downstream retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflows. Given the large volume of documents, the team also needs to optimize performance by implementing appropriate data distribution and query-handling strategies. Which approach best satisfies these requirements?
correct_text: Leverage Amazon Titan Text Embeddings in Bedrock to convert text into semantic vectors and store them in Amazon OpenSearch Service for context-aware retrieval and reasoning by AI agents. Implement OpenSearch sharding strategies to distribute the vector index across multiple nodes for optimal query performance and horizontal scalability.

Rekognition - General computer vision, not optimized for structured document data extraction ⚠️ C. Requirements: Cloud contact center with automatic speech recognition , natural language understanding , intent recognition , and ability to maintain conversation context across multiple interactions. Which AWS service meets ALL these requirements for conversational AI? A. Amazon Transcribe B. Amazon Polly C. Amazon Lex D. Amazon Comprehend ✅ C. Amazon Lex 🎯 Why: Amazon Lex provides ASR (speech-to-text), NLU (natural language understanding), intent recognition with slot filling, and context management across conversations. It's specifically designed for building conversational interfaces and chatbots. ⚠️ A. Transcribe: Only provides speech-to-text conversion, lacks NLU, intent recognition, and context management. ⚠️ B. Polly: Only provides text-to-speech synthesis, cannot understand or process incoming speech or text. ⚠️ D. Comprehend: Analyzes text for insights but lacks ASR capabilities and real-time conversational context management.

A company wants to build an Interactive Voice Response (IVR) system where customers can speak naturally to check account balances and update personal information without speaking to agents. Which AWS service combination is specifically designed for this use case? A. Amazon Polly + Amazon Transcribe B. Amazon Connect + Amazon Lex C. Amazon Comprehend + Amazon Translate D. AWS Alexa for Business + Amazon Rekognition ✅ B. Amazon Connect + Amazon Lex 🎯 This is the exact use case Amazon Connect and Lex were designed for. Amazon Connect handles the contact center infrastructure, while Amazon Lex provides the conversational AI with built-in ASR and NLU to understand natural speech and execute self-service tasks. ⚠️ A. Polly + Transcribe: Polly only does text-to-speech, Transcribe only does speech-to-text. Neither provides intent understanding or dialogue management needed for IVR interactions. ⚠️ C. Comprehend + Translate: These are for text analysis and translation, not real-time voice interactions or contact center operations. ⚠️ D. Alexa for Business + Rekognition: Alexa for Business is for workplace productivity, Rekognition is for image analysis - neither addresses contact center or IVR requirements.

stem: A startup is training an autonomous vehicle detection model using Amazon SageMaker AI with labeled image data stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The dataset is annotated using SageMaker Ground Truth, which contains thousands of high-resolution images. During model training, the team observes slow startup times and low GPU utilization because the training job downloads data sequentially from S3. The company wants to keep the S3 bucket as the primary data repository, but improve data access performance and training throughput for SageMaker AI without duplicating data or significantly altering the training script. The team reviewed AWS Cost Explorer and observed rising GPU costs due to idle compute time. Which solution should be implemented to optimize SageMaker AI training performance while maintaining the existing S3-based workflow?
correct_text: Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system and connect it to the existing S3 bucket. Update the SageMaker AI training job to access the dataset directly from the FSx mount.

stem: A social media platform is developing an ML model to moderate user-generated content. The platform stores large volumes of textual and document data in Amazon S3. It uses Amazon Textract to extract text from uploaded PDFs or images, and Amazon SageMaker AI to train custom language models that classify comments based on sentiment, context, and topic relevance. The moderation team aims to enhance safety by detecting toxic or harmful language in real-time, including hate speech, harassment, and explicit threats. The solution must integrate seamlessly with the existing SageMaker AI inference pipeline, handle high throughput, and provide confidence scores for each classification, allowing content flagged as toxic to be reviewed or blocked automatically. Which of the solutions provides a managed solution for detecting toxicity in text to support this ML pipeline with safety classifiers?

A media company has hybrid architecture with Direct Connect. 50TB+ digital videos on on-premises tape library used by Media Asset Management (MAM) system. Want automated catalog with facial recognition, minimal disruption, least management overhead . Eventually migrate to AWS. Which solution uses LEAST ongoing management overhead with MINIMAL disruption? A. Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to set up video ingestion stream with Amazon Rekognition, build face collection. Stream media files from MAM into Kinesis, configure Rekognition to process streamed files. Launch stream consumer for metadata, push to MAM, store files in S3. B. Set up tape gateway on-premises connected to AWS Storage Gateway. Configure MAM to fetch files from archive, push to tape gateway for Glacier storage. Use Rekognition with Lambda function to process video from tape gateway in real-time. C. Integrate local data center file system to AWS Storage Gateway via file gateway on-premises. MAM extracts files and sends to file gateway. Build Rekognition collection, use Lambda to process files from S3 bucket backing file gateway. D. Request AWS Snowball to migrate files to S3. Provision large EC2 instance, install open-source facial recognition tools like OpenFace/OpenCV. Process files for metadata, push to MAM, copy files to another S3 bucket. ✅ C File Gateway with Rekognition 🎯 File Gateway provides seamless integration with existing MAM system while enabling real-time processing with Rekognition. Tape Gateway can't process files in real-time from Glacier. ⚠️ A Kinesis Video Streams — Requires major MAM changes, designed for streaming not archived files ⚠️ B Tape Gateway — Can't process files real-time from Glacier archive ⚠️ D Snowball + EC2 — High management overhead with open-source tools vs managed Rekognition 📖 Full Explanation Amazon Rekognition can store information about detected faces in server-side containers known as collections. You can use the facial information that's stored in a collection to search for known faces in images, stored videos, and streaming videos. Amazon Rekognition supports the IndexFaces operation. You can use this operation to detect faces in an image and persist information about facial features that are detected in a collection. This is an example of a storage-based API operation because the service persists information on the server. To store facial information, you must first create (CreateCollection) a face collection in one of the AWS Regions in your account. You specify this face collection when you call the IndexFaces operation. After you create a face collection and store facial feature information for all faces, you can search the collection for face matches. To search for faces in an image, call SearchFacesByImage. To search for faces in a stored video, call StartFaceSearch. To search for faces in a streaming video, call CreateStreamProcessor. AWS Storage Gateway offers file-based, volume-based, and tape-based storage solutions. With a tape gateway, you can cost-effectively and durably archive backup data in GLACIER or DEEP_ARCHIVE. A tape gateway provides a virtual tape infrastructure that scales seamlessly with your business needs and eliminates the operational burden of provisioning, scaling, and maintaining a physical tape infrastructure. You can run AWS Storage Gateway either on-premises as a VM appliance, as a hardware appliance, or in AWS as an Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance. You deploy your gateway on an EC2 instance to provision iSCSI storage volumes in AWS. You can use gateways hosted on EC2 instances for disaster recovery, data mirroring, and providing storage for applications hosted on Amazon EC2. Hence, the correct answer is: Integrate the file system of your local data center to AWS Storage Gateway by setting up a file gateway appliance on-premises. Utilize the MAM solution to extract the media files from the current data store and send them into the file gateway. Build a collection using Amazon Rekognition by populating a catalog of faces from the processed media files. Use an AWS Lambda function to invoke Amazon Rekognition Javascript SDK to have it fetch the media file from the S3 bucket which is backing the file gateway, retrieve the needed metadata, and finally, persist the information into the MAM solution. The option that says: Request for an AWS Snowball Storage Optimized device to migrate all of the media files from the on-premises library into Amazon S3. Provision a large EC2 instance and allow it to access the S3 bucket. Install an open-source facial recognition tool on the instance like OpenFace or OpenCV. Process the media files to retrieve the metadata and push this information into the MAM solution. Lastly, copy the media files to another S3 bucket is incorrect. This entails a lot of ongoing management overhead instead of just using Amazon Rekognition. Moreover, it is more suitable to use the AWS Storage Gateway service rather than an EBS Volume. The option that says: Set up a tape gateway appliance on-premises and connect it to your AWS Storage Gateway. Configure the MAM solution to fetch the media files from the current archive and push them into the tape gateway to be stored in Amazon Glacier. Using Amazon Rekognition, build a collection from the catalog of faces. Utilize a Lambda function which invokes the Rekognition Javascript SDK to have Amazon Rekognition process the video directly from the tape gateway in real-time, retrieve the required metadata, and push the metadata into the MAM solution is incorrect. Although this solution uses the right combination of AWS Storage Gateway and Amazon Rekognition, take note that you can't directly fetch the media files from your tape gateway in real time since this is backed up using Glacier. Although the on-premises data center is using a tape gateway, you can still set up a solution to use a file gateway in order to properly process the videos using Amazon Rekognition. Keep in mind that the tape gateway in the AWS Storage Gateway service is primarily used as an archive solution. The option that says: Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to set up a video ingestion stream and with Amazon Rekognition, build a collection of faces. Stream the media files from the MAM solution into Kinesis Video Streams and configure the Amazon Rekognition to process the streamed files. Launch a stream consumer to retrieve the required metadata, and push the metadata into the MAM solution. Finally, configure the stream to store the files in an S3 bucket is incorrect. This approach requires significant changes to the existing MAM solution to stream media files directly into Kinesis Video Streams, potentially causing more disruption to the current workflow. Additionally, Kinesis Video Streams is designed for real-time video streaming and processing, which may not be the most efficient approach for processing pre-existing media files stored in a tape library. Lastly, setting up and managing Kinesis Video Streams, configuring Amazon Rekognition integration, implementing a stream consumer, and storing files in S3 introduces additional complexity and management overhead compared to the File Gateway approach.

A government agency has multiple VPCs in various AWS regions across the United States that need to be linked up to an on-premises central office network in Washington, D.C. The central office requires inter-region VPC access over a private network that is dedicated to each region for enhanced security and more predictable data transfer performance. Your team needs to quickly build this network mesh and minimize management overhead. Which option provides the most secure, highly available, and durable solution for this interconnectivity? A. Utilize AWS Direct Connect Gateway for inter-region VPC access. Create a virtual private gateway in each VPC, then create a private virtual interface for each AWS Direct Connect connection to the Direct Connect gateway. B. Enable inter-region VPC peering which allows peering relationships to be established between VPCs across different AWS regions. C. Implement a hub-and-spoke network topology in each region using AWS Transit Gateway. Route traffic between VPCs and the on-premise network over AWS Site-to-Site VPN. D. Create a link aggregation group (LAG) with AWS Direct Connect Gateway and create public virtual interfaces for each connection. ✅ A. AWS Direct Connect Gateway with private virtual interfaces 🎯 Why correct: Direct Connect Gateway provides dedicated network connections with predictable performance across multiple regions while minimizing management overhead. Private virtual interfaces ensure traffic stays within AWS backbone without traversing public internet, meeting the security and performance requirements. ⚠️ B. Inter-region VPC peering While VPC peering keeps traffic on AWS backbone, it requires extensive manual setup and management overhead to create a functional multi-region network mesh. The connections are not dedicated and don't provide the enhanced performance guarantees required by the government agency. ⚠️ C. Transit Gateway with Site-to-Site VPN Site-to-Site VPN uses internet-based connections rather than dedicated private network connections. This doesn't meet the requirement for dedicated network connectivity and enhanced security that the government agency specifically needs. ⚠️ D. LAG with public virtual interfaces Public virtual interfaces are used for accessing AWS public services, not VPC resources. The scenario requires private connectivity to VPC resources. Additionally, LAG is unnecessary complexity for this use case and doesn't address the core connectivity requirements.

stem: A leading technology company has developed a powerful Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) application that enhances user interactions by providing relevant responses through advanced search techniques. The application uses a vector database to store embeddings of documents, understanding the meaning behind user queries rather than relying on keyword matches. As part of the cloud migration, the text repository has been moved to Amazon S3, containing terabytes of unstructured documents such as technical manuals and customer support logs. To support the data processing pipeline, Amazon SageMaker AI is used for building and training custom machine learning models that analyze and classify documents, and Amazon Comprehend is utilized for natural language processing tasks such as sentiment analysis and entity recognition. The company needs a solution that integrates smoothly with the S3 bucket, scales effectively, and ensures high performance when retrieving relevant, context-aware results from the vast repository. The goal is to provide users with accurate and contextually relevant results based on the deeper meaning of queries, offering a more dynamic and engaging user experience. Which AWS solution will optimize the company’s RAG application and enable semantic search?
correct_text: Ingest documents from S3 into Amazon Kendra using the Kendra S3 connector, then perform semantic search queries with Kendra's built-in search engine.

A company uses AWS Organizations for multi-account infrastructure. They need to automate sharing AWS resources between accounts using AWS RAM. A service needs to perform tasks on organization accounts on behalf of a previous account moderator who maintained specific configurations. What is the simplest solution to allow the service to perform tasks on organization accounts on the moderator's behalf? A. Enable cross-account access with AWS Organizations in the Resource Access Manager Console. Mirror the configuration changes that was performed by the account that previously managed this service. B. Configure a service-linked role for AWS RAM and modify the permissions policy to specify what the role can and cannot do. Lastly, modify the trust policy of the role so that other processes can utilize AWS RAM. C. Use trusted access by running the enable-sharing-with-aws-organization command in the AWS RAM CLI. Mirror the configuration changes that was performed by the account that previously managed this service. D. Attach an IAM role on the service detailing all the allowed actions that it will be able to perform. Install an SSM agent in each of the worker VMs. Use AWS Systems Manager to build automation workflows that involve the daily key processes. ✅ C. Use trusted access by running the enable-sharing-with-aws-organization command 🎯 Trusted access allows AWS RAM to create service-linked roles across all organization accounts automatically, enabling centralized resource sharing management. ⚠️ A. Cross-account access — Should enable trusted access, not cross-account access ⚠️ B. Manual service-linked role — Trust policies of service-linked roles cannot be modified ⚠️ D. SSM automation — Overly complex solution that doesn't address RAM-Organizations integration 📖 Full Explanation AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) enables you to share specified AWS resources that you own with other AWS accounts. To enable trusted access with AWS Organizations: From the AWS RAM CLI, use the enable-sharing-with-aws-organizations command. Name of the IAM service-linked role that can be created in accounts when trusted access is enabled: AWSResourceAccessManagerServiceRolePolicy. You can use trusted access to enable an AWS service that you specify, called the trusted service, to perform tasks in your organization and its accounts on your behalf. This involves granting permissions to the trusted service but does not otherwise affect the permissions for IAM users or roles. When you enable access, the trusted service can create an IAM role called a service-linked role in every account in the organization. That role has a permissions policy that allows the trusted service to do the tasks that are described in that service's documentation.

When building conversational AI interfaces, when should you choose Amazon Lex over Amazon Comprehend? A. When you need to analyze sentiment in customer reviews B. When you need real-time speech recognition and intent understanding C. When you need to extract entities from documents D. When you need to classify text into categories ✅ B. When you need real-time speech recognition and intent understanding Amazon Lex • Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) • Natural Language Understanding (NLU) • Intent recognition and slot filling • Conversational chatbots and voice interfaces • Real-time dialogue management Amazon Comprehend • Text analysis and insights • Sentiment analysis • Entity extraction • Document classification • Batch processing of text documents 🎯 Decision rule: Choose Lex when building interactive conversational interfaces that need to understand spoken or typed user input in real-time. Choose Comprehend when analyzing existing text content for insights, sentiment, or classification.

The company also needs to ensure that this process does not disrupt the production system. Which of the following should be implemented with the LEAST operational overhead?

stem: A software development team is building a customer support chatbot for a large e-commerce platform. The chatbot needs to provide real-time, contextually accurate answers to customer inquiries based on product documentation, frequently asked questions, and order history. The team decides to implement a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architecture to enhance the chatbot’s ability to understand customer queries and generate precise, context-aware responses. The chatbot must query a vector database to retrieve relevant documents based on the user’s query, analyze the retrieved context for important entities and sentiments using Amazon Comprehend, and then feed this refined context to a foundation model deployed to an Amazon SageMaker AI real-time inference endpoint for response generation. The solution should enable the chatbot to operate in real-time and provide accurate answers based on the user’s query context. Which solution will best integrate Pinecone into this RAG-based system to provide context for the Llama 2 model?
correct_text: Use Pinecone to index product documentation, retrieve pertinent information based on the query, analyze the context with Comprehend, and provide the refined context to a Llama 2 model deployed to a SageMaker AI real-time inference endpoint for response generation.

Comprehend: Analyzes text for insights but lacks ASR capabilities and real-time conversational context management.

A BPO startup needs a scalable call center system on AWS that can handle thousands of inbound calls with self-service capabilities (password changes, balance checks) without agents. Requirements: automatic speech recognition (ASR) , natural language understanding , and integration with business applications . Which solution should the Solutions Architect implement? A. AWS Ground Station + Amazon Alexa for Business + Lambda B. Amazon Connect + Amazon Comprehend + Lambda C. Amazon Connect + Amazon Lex + Lambda D. AWS Elemental MediaConnect + Amazon Polly + Lambda ✅ C. Amazon Connect + Amazon Lex + Lambda 🎯 Amazon Connect provides cloud contact center functionality, while Amazon Lex offers both ASR and NLU for conversational chatbots that can handle self-service tasks. ⚠️ A. Ground Station is for satellite communications, not contact centers ⚠️ B. Comprehend analyzes text but lacks ASR/NLU for voice interactions ⚠️ D. MediaConnect is for live video transport, Polly only does text-to-speech 📖 Full Explanation Amazon Connect provides a seamless omnichannel experience through a single unified contact center for voice and chat. Amazon Lex is a service for building conversational interfaces into any application using voice and text. Amazon Lex provides the advanced deep learning functionalities of automatic speech recognition (ASR) for converting speech to text and natural language understanding (NLU) to recognize the intent of the text, enabling you to build applications with highly engaging user experiences and lifelike conversational interactions. By using an Amazon Lex chatbot in your Amazon Connect call center, callers can perform tasks such as changing a password, requesting a balance on an account, or scheduling an appointment without needing to speak to an agent. Amazon Lex uses AWS Lambda functions to query your business applications, provide information back to callers, and make updates as requested.

A company wants to build an Interactive Voice Response (IVR) system where customers can speak naturally to check account balances and update personal information without speaking to agents. Which AWS service combination is specifically designed for this use case? A. Amazon Polly + Amazon Transcribe B. Amazon Connect + Amazon Lex C. Amazon Comprehend + Amazon Translate D. AWS Alexa for Business + Amazon Rekognition ✅ B. Amazon Connect + Amazon Lex 🎯 This is the exact use case Amazon Connect and Lex were designed for. Amazon Connect handles the contact center infrastructure, while Amazon Lex provides the conversational AI with built-in ASR and NLU to understand natural speech and execute self-service tasks. ⚠️ A. Polly + Transcribe: Polly only does text-to-speech, Transcribe only does speech-to-text. Neither provides intent understanding or dialogue management needed for IVR interactions. ⚠️ C. Comprehend + Translate: These are for text analysis and translation, not real-time voice interactions or contact center operations. ⚠️ D. Alexa for Business + Rekognition: Alexa for Business is for workplace productivity, Rekognition is for image analysis - neither addresses contact center or IVR requirements.

stem: A global economic research organization is developing an AI-driven financial insights engine that generates analytical summaries from earnings disclosures, market indicators, and corporate filings. The system uses Amazon SageMaker Processing for large-scale data preparation and Amazon Textract to extract structured financial data. From the outset, the architecture team evaluates the solution using the Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix to classify risk categories, determine validation requirements, and outline controls needed to manage accuracy-related concerns. Early testing reveals statements affected by hallucinations regarding projected revenue and risk exposure, prompting the engineering team to design an automated verification layer that ensures generated insights consistently align with authoritative financial documents. To meet compliance and audit requirements, the organization mandates a verification mechanism capable of detecting unsupported claims, performing document-level cross-checking, and producing traceable metadata for downstream auditing. The solution must validate each generated response against trusted enterprise sources while maintaining consistent governance as defined in the scoping matrix. Which solution best satisfies these requirements?

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A financial services company needs to build a predictive model to identify fraudulent transactions using historical customer data, which includes sensitive information such as credit card numbers. The company plans to use Amazon SageMaker AI to train the model and Amazon Comprehend to extract features from the text-based data in the dataset. The company must ensure that all customer data is securely encrypted and that any personally identifiable information (PII), including credit card numbers, is redacted before the data is used for model training. Which solution will meet this requirement?
correct_text: Encrypt customer data with AWS KMS in Amazon S3 before importing it into SageMaker AI. Use AWS Glue to redact credit card numbers from the customer data before using it for model training.

candidates.full_text: A financial services company stores customer transaction data in S3 and needs to automatically identify credit card numbers, social security numbers, and other PII across terabytes of documents. Which service best addresses this requirement? A. AWS Config B. Amazon Macie C. AWS CloudTrail D. Amazon Inspector ✅ B. Amazon Macie 🎯 Perfect match: Macie uses machine learning to automatically scan S3 buckets and identify sensitive data patterns like credit card numbers, SSNs, and PII. It provides continuous monitoring, classification, and alerting for data security compliance. Config tracks resource configuration changes, CloudTrail logs API calls, and Inspector assesses application security - none perform content-based PII discovery.

A telecommunications company is hosting a WordPress website on Amazon ECS Cluster using Fargate launch type . Database credentials must be provided via environment variables , kept secure and not viewable on the cluster. Requirements: dedicated storage with lifecycle management and key rotation . Which solution provides secure credential storage with the least effort? A. Store credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, encrypt with KMS, create IAM role for ECS task execution, reference secrets in container definition B. Migrate to Amazon EKS, use Kubernetes Secrets objects, reference with secretKeyRef, configure automatic rotation C. Store credentials in ECS task definition file encrypted with KMS, store in private S3 bucket with HTTPS, use --cli-input-json parameter D. Store credentials in AWS Secrets Manager, encrypt with KMS, create IAM role for ECS task execution, reference secrets in container definition ✅ D. AWS Secrets Manager with KMS encryption 🎯 Why correct: Secrets Manager provides dedicated secrets storage with built-in lifecycle management and automatic key rotation capabilities, exactly matching the requirement for "dedicated storage with lifecycle management and key rotation." ⚠️ A. Systems Manager Parameter Store While Parameter Store can store encrypted credentials and works with ECS secrets, it doesn't provide dedicated storage with lifecycle management and key rotation features like Secrets Manager does. ⚠️ B. Migrate to Amazon EKS This requires significant migration effort from ECS to EKS, violating the "least effort" requirement. Additionally, Kubernetes doesn't natively support automatic rotation of secrets. ⚠️ C. Store in ECS task definition in S3 Storing sensitive credentials in S3, even encrypted, is not a recommended practice and requires extensive manual configuration. This approach has more overhead than using purpose-built secrets management services.

A company requires: encrypted credential storage , cost optimization , hierarchical organization , and no automatic rotation for their application configuration. Which service meets ALL requirements? A. AWS Secrets Manager B. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store C. Amazon S3 with KMS encryption D. AWS Config ✅ B. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 🎯 Why: Parameter Store provides KMS encryption (security), free tier pricing (cost optimization), hierarchical parameter organization (/app/database/password), and no built-in rotation (meeting the no automatic rotation requirement). It's purpose-built for configuration management. ⚠️ A. Secrets Manager - More expensive and includes automatic rotation features not needed ⚠️ C. S3 with KMS - Lacks hierarchical organization and configuration management features ⚠️ D. AWS Config - Configuration compliance service, not credential storage

Which option satisfies the requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

Company runs weather simulations generating terabytes of data stored in MySQL 8.0 on EC2. Ruby on Rails app on separate EC2 processes data. Current DB: 16 TiB, growing continuously . Need highly scalable, highly available, 24x7 reliability, cost-effective solution. Which is the MOST cost-effective solution? A. Auto Scaling EC2 + ALB + Reserved instances + Aurora + read-replica in another AZ B. Lambda@Edge functions + RDS MySQL Multi-AZ + storage autoscaling C. Auto Scaling EC2 + ALB + Reserved instances + RDS MySQL Multi-AZ + manual storage adjustment D. Reserved EC2 for app/DB + Auto Scaling Multi-AZ + source-replica setup + LVM for storage ✅ A. Auto Scaling EC2 + ALB + Reserved instances + Aurora + read-replica 🎯 Aurora auto-scales storage to 128 TiB (vs RDS 64 TiB limit) and offers better performance/cost for large datasets. Read replica provides HA across AZs. ⚠️ B. Lambda@Edge — designed for CloudFront edge computing, not heavy data processing applications ⚠️ C. RDS MySQL — limited to 64 TiB max storage, manual adjustment unnecessary when autoscaling available ⚠️ D. Self-managed MySQL — high operational overhead, manual scaling, not cost-effective vs managed Aurora 📖 Full Explanation You can launch and automatically scale a fleet of On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances within a single Auto Scaling group. In addition to receiving discounts for using Spot Instances, you can use Reserved Instances or a Savings Plan to receive discounted rates of the regular On-Demand Instance pricing. All of these factors combined help you to optimize your cost savings for Amazon EC2 instances, while making sure that you obtain the desired scale and performance for your application. Amazon Aurora storage automatically scales with the data in your cluster volume. As your data grows, your cluster volume storage expands up to a maximum of 128 tebibytes (TiB). Even though an Aurora cluster volume can scale up in size to many tebibytes, you are only charged for the space that you use in the volume. The mechanism for determining billed storage space depends on the version of your Aurora cluster. Aurora stores copies of the data in a DB cluster across multiple Availability Zones in a single AWS Region. Aurora stores these copies regardless of whether the instances in the DB cluster span multiple Availability Zones. However, you still need to create a read-replica for the high availability of the Aurora DB instance. A single read-replica is enough to quickly recover the database in case the primary instance fails.

A clinic runs its medical record system using Windows-based EC2 instances with confidential health files. Requirements: latest security patches must be installed and there should be a system that checks all EC2 instances for approved AMIs . The solution must not impede developers from launching instances with unapproved AMIs, but you must be notified of non-compliant instances . Which TWO solutions should the architect implement? (Select TWO.) A. Set up a patch baseline using AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager B. Set up Amazon GuardDuty to monitor patches and AMI compliance C. Use AWS Shield Advanced to automatically patch instances D. Create an IAM policy restricting unapproved AMI launches E. Use AWS Config Managed Rule to check approved AMIs with CloudWatch Alarms ✅ A & E. AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager + AWS Config Managed Rule 🎯 Why correct: Patch Manager handles automated patching with customizable baselines, while Config Managed Rules continuously monitor AMI compliance without blocking developer actions. CloudWatch Alarms provide the required notifications for non-compliance. ⚠️ B. Amazon GuardDuty GuardDuty is a threat detection service that monitors for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior. It does not check security patch status or AMI compliance - it focuses on detecting threats like unusual API calls or potential account compromises. ⚠️ C. AWS Shield Advanced Shield Advanced is specifically designed for DDoS protection and mitigation. It has no capabilities for patching EC2 instances or monitoring AMI compliance - it's purely a network-level protection service. ⚠️ D. IAM Policy Restriction While technically possible, creating an IAM policy that blocks unapproved AMI launches would directly violate the requirement that the solution "should not impede developers from launching instances using an unapproved AMI."

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A company has developed a machine learning-based recommendation system designed to personalize content for users. The model has been trained using Amazon SageMaker AI built-in algorithms and a custom dataset, with real-time inference being performed within SageMaker AI. As part of the system, the company also intends to leverage Amazon Comprehend for natural language processing to analyze customer reviews and sentiment, which will further enhance the recommendation engine. To meet strict security and compliance requirements, the company must ensure that both the training and inference environments, as well as all associated services, are deployed within a secure Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). Furthermore, the solution must completely block all access to the internet or any external resources to protect sensitive user data and ensure compliance with regulatory standards. Which of the following will satisfy the given requirements with the LEAST development effort?
correct_text: Activate SageMaker AI network isolation mode to block all external access and establish a VPC endpoint for Comprehend within the same VPC.

When you need real-time speech recognition and intent understanding Amazon Lex • Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) • Natural Language Understanding (NLU) • Intent recognition and slot filling • Conversational chatbots and voice interfaces • Real-time dialogue management Amazon Comprehend • Text analysis and insights • Sentiment analysis • Entity extraction • Document classification • Batch processing of text documents 🎯 Decision rule: Choose Lex when building interactive conversational interfaces that need to understand spoken or typed user input in real-time. Choose Comprehend when analyzing existing text content for insights, sentiment, or classification.

Requirements: DNS resolution for internal services , cross-VPC accessibility , no internet exposure , custom domain names , integration with existing VPC peering . Route 53 Resolver endpoints with conditional forwarding D. CloudFront distribution with origin access identity ✅ B. Private hosted zone associated with all relevant VPCs 🎯 Requirement mapping: Private hosted zones provide custom domain DNS (✓), work within VPCs only (✓), support cross-VPC resolution through peering (✓), ensure no internet exposure (✓), and integrate seamlessly with existing VPC infrastructure (✓). Public zones expose to internet, Resolver endpoints are for hybrid connectivity, CloudFront is for content delivery not internal DNS resolution.

category: AIP – Testing, Validation, and Troubleshooting
stem: A global e-commerce company is developing a product return prediction model using the Amazon SageMaker XGBoost algorithm to identify which orders are most likely to result in customer returns. Transactional and behavioral data are stored in Amazon Redshift, and the data engineering team utilizes SageMaker Data Wrangler to clean and prepare training features, including product category, customer sentiment, and delivery delays. After deploying the model, the team observes that while the training Area Under the Curve (AUC) is exceptionally high, the validation performance drops significantly. Model explainability reports from SageMaker Clarify reveal that the model is overly sensitive to a few dominant features like product price and region, suggesting overfitting to patterns in the training set. The team decides to tune the model’s hyperparameters to reduce model complexity and improve its ability to generalize to new data. Which hyperparameter modification would best help reduce overfitting and improve validation performance for this XGBoost model?
correct_text: Decrease the value of the max_depth hyperparameter to limit tree complexity and prevent overfitting on dominant patterns in the training data.

category: AIP – Implementation and Integration
stem: A multinational company is gathering a diverse set of multimedia data in various languages, including Spanish, from customer interactions, video recordings, and written documents. The company operates in multiple countries and needs to extract valuable insights by converting audio and video content into text, translating it into English, and summarizing it efficiently. The company already uses Amazon Kendra for indexing and searching large volumes of documents and Amazon Textract to extract text from scanned documents. These services help the company manage and process content in different languages, but an efficient solution is still needed to translate and summarize the content for a global audience. The company is now looking for a solution that can process audio and video data, translate it into English, and summarize it quickly using a large language model (LLM). The solution should minimize deployment time, ensuring that it can scale efficiently to meet the company’s global needs. Which option will best fulfill these requirements in the shortest time possible?
correct_text: Utilize Amazon Transcribe for audio and video-to-text conversion, Amazon Translate for translating the content into English, and Amazon Bedrock with the Jamba model for summarizing the text.

A print media company has a web application for searching newspaper archives. They scanned old newspapers to PNG images and used OCR software to convert to text. The OCR license expires soon and they want to move to AWS with a scalable, durable, highly available architecture. Which is the best option to achieve this requirement? A. Store images in S3, use Amazon Kendra for search, lifecycle policy to Glacier after 3 months with Glacier Select B. CloudFormation with EBS-backed EC2 instances, ALB, NGINX web server, open source search, EBS volumes with Data Lifecycle Manager C. S3 bucket with CloudFront, Elastic Beanstalk multi-AZ website, Amazon OpenSearch Service for queries, Amazon Textract for OCR D. S3 Intelligent-Tiering, migrate existing OCR software to Auto Scaling Spot instances with ALB, use Amazon Rekognition for text ✅ C. S3 + CloudFront + Elastic Beanstalk + OpenSearch + Textract 🎯 Amazon Textract replaces expiring OCR software, OpenSearch provides scalable search, multi-AZ ensures high availability. ⚠️ A. Kendra can't extract text from scanned images, Glacier affects retrieval performance ⚠️ B. EBS volumes less scalable/durable than S3, more maintenance overhead ⚠️ D. Still uses expiring OCR software, Rekognition not optimized for document text extraction 📖 Full Explanation Amazon OpenSearch Service simplifies deployment and scaling of search capabilities without hardware management. Amazon Textract is specifically designed for OCR from documents, going beyond simple text recognition to extract structured data. S3 provides durable storage, CloudFront improves global performance, and Elastic Beanstalk offers managed multi-AZ hosting. Option A fails because Kendra doesn't perform OCR and Glacier impacts performance. Option B uses less scalable EBS storage with maintenance overhead. Option D keeps the expiring OCR software and uses Rekognition incorrectly for document text extraction.

A print media company wants to migrate their on-premises web application to AWS. The app allows global users to search and retrieve newspaper pages stored as PNG images with OCR-converted text files . Their OCR license expires soon and they need a scalable, durable, highly available AWS architecture. Which is the best option to achieve this requirement? A. Store images in S3, use Amazon Kendra for search, lifecycle policy to Glacier after 3 months with Glacier Select for queries B. CloudFormation with EBS-backed EC2 instances, ALB, NGINX, open source search, EBS volumes with Data Lifecycle Manager C. S3 bucket with CloudFront distribution, Elastic Beanstalk multi-AZ environment, Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Textract for OCR D. S3 Intelligent-Tiering, migrate OCR software to Auto Scaling Spot instances with ALB, Amazon Rekognition for text recognition ✅ C. S3 bucket with CloudFront distribution, Elastic Beanstalk multi-AZ environment, Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Textract for OCR 🎯 Why correct: This solution replaces the expiring OCR license with managed AWS services (Textract), provides scalable storage (S3), high availability (multi-AZ Beanstalk), and robust search capabilities (OpenSearch Service). CloudFront ensures global content delivery performance. ⚠️ A. Amazon Kendra approach Kendra is an enterprise search service for existing content repositories, not designed for OCR text recognition from scanned documents. Moving frequently accessed images to Glacier would severely impact retrieval performance for a global web application. ⚠️ B. EBS-based solution EBS volumes are neither scalable nor durable compared to S3, requiring manual management and creating single points of failure. This approach lacks the cost-effectiveness and automated scaling of managed services. ⚠️ D. Rekognition with existing OCR This solution still relies on the expiring OCR software that needs replacement. Amazon Rekognition is optimized for general image recognition, while Textract is specifically designed for document text extraction.

stem: A global e-commerce company is building a multilingual product description generator using Amazon Titan Text on Amazon Bedrock. The team plans to enhance the model’s domain understanding by fine-tuning it with proprietary product data in Amazon SageMaker AI before deploying it to production through Bedrock’s managed API. For compliance reasons, all model artifacts must be encrypted using AWS KMS, and API calls to the Bedrock endpoint must be logged and auditable. The company also wants to continuously monitor model latency and throughput across different regions to ensure consistent performance. Which solution provides a secure, compliant, and observable architecture for deploying and monitoring the Titan-based generative AI model?
correct_text: Fine-tune the Titan model in SageMaker AI using training data stored in Amazon S3 with KMS encryption, deploy the model through Bedrock with a customer-managed KMS key, enable AWS CloudTrail for API auditing, and use Amazon CloudWatch metrics for Bedrock such as InvocationLatency to continuously monitor latency and throughput across regions.
