stem: A global e-commerce company is preparing to train a generative AI model to generate realistic customer reviews for its products. The company collects vast amounts of user-generated content, including reviews, but some of this data contains personally identifiable information (PII). To ensure compliance with privacy regulations, the data scientist must redact any sensitive information while retaining the overall structure and integrity of the content for training the model. The solution must also scale to handle large datasets and automate the process efficiently, allowing for continuous model training without manual intervention. The company utilizes Amazon SageMaker AI for model training and Amazon Comprehend to analyze product reviews. The solution must also ensure that no PII is used during model training. Which of the following solutions is the most efficient and scalable option to meet these requirements?
correct_text: Apply Comprehend DetectPiiEntities API to automatically identify and redact PII from the dataset, and store the cleansed data in an Amazon S3 bucket. SageMaker AI can then access the S3 bucket for training the generative AI model.

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A financial services company is developing a machine learning (ML) model in Amazon SageMaker AI to detect real-time fraudulent transactions. The company plans to integrate this model with Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for continuous transaction data ingestion and Amazon DynamoDB for storing transaction metadata. The model must be trained on an extensive historical dataset stored in Amazon S3. The company must ensure that all data is encrypted in transit and at rest, and that access to sensitive data and model results is strictly controlled. AWS Encryption SDK is being considered for additional client-side encryption of sensitive data before uploading it to S3. There’s also a need to track model performance over time to ensure it remains effective and predictions align with business rules. Which solution will secure the ML workflow, control access, and allow for continuous monitoring of model performance?
correct_text: Use SageMaker AI to train the model with data from S3, enable S3 server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) for data at rest, configure IAM roles to control access to the model and data, and use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor model performance metrics and logging.

candidates.full_text: A company receives sensor data every millisecond from manufacturing equipment and needs to detect anomalies in real-time to prevent equipment failure. Which AWS service is best suited for this use case? A. Amazon SQS with Lambda processing B. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Analytics C. Amazon S3 with scheduled EMR jobs D. Amazon RDS with stored procedures ✅ B. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Analytics 🎯 Trigger keywords: "every millisecond" + "real-time anomaly detection" = streaming analytics requirement. Kinesis Data Streams ingests high-frequency sensor data, while Kinesis Analytics runs SQL queries for real-time anomaly detection using sliding windows and statistical functions. SQS + Lambda: SQS has throughput limits and Lambda has execution time limits - not suitable for continuous millisecond data streams requiring real-time processing.

A financial services company stores customer transaction data in S3 and needs to automatically identify credit card numbers, social security numbers, and other PII across terabytes of documents. Which service best addresses this requirement? A. AWS Config B. Amazon Macie C. AWS CloudTrail D. Amazon Inspector ✅ B. Amazon Macie 🎯 Perfect match: Macie uses machine learning to automatically scan S3 buckets and identify sensitive data patterns like credit card numbers, SSNs, and PII. It provides continuous monitoring, classification, and alerting for data security compliance. Config tracks resource configuration changes, CloudTrail logs API calls, and Inspector assesses application security - none perform content-based PII discovery.

A company needs to store and replicate financial transaction data across multiple AWS regions with ACID properties , sub-millisecond latency , and automatic failover capabilities. Which service best addresses this requirement? A. Amazon RDS with Cross-Region Read Replicas B. DynamoDB Global Tables C. Amazon S3 with Cross-Region Replication D. Amazon ElastiCache Global Datastore ✅ B. DynamoDB Global Tables 🎯 Key insight: DynamoDB Global Tables provides single-digit millisecond latency, automatic multi-region replication, and built-in ACID properties for transactions. It's specifically designed for financial and transactional workloads requiring global distribution. ⚠️ A. RDS Cross-Region Replicas only provide read replicas, not multi-master writes, and have higher latency than DynamoDB. ⚠️ C. S3 is object storage, not suitable for transactional data requiring ACID properties. ⚠️ D. ElastiCache is for caching, not persistent transactional storage with ACID guarantees.

Amazon Bedrock, la empresa YA tiene el dataset etiquetado en JSONL y el rol IAM listo. Dado esto, cual es el primer paso RESTANTE del proceso de personalizacion (fine-tuning) del modelo? A. A company needs to ensure log file integrity for compliance audits, prevent accidental deletion of critical audit logs, and maintain confidentiality of sensitive API call data stored in S3. Which combination of S3 security features best meets ALL requirements? A. S3 Object Lock with Legal Hold and bucket-level public read blocking B. MFA Delete, IAM roles with least privilege, and S3 bucket policies C. S3 versioning with Cross-Region Replication and KMS encryption D. S3 Access Control Lists (ACLs) and CloudWatch monitoring ✅ B. MFA Delete, IAM roles with least privilege, and S3 bucket policies 🎯 MFA Delete prevents accidental deletion (integrity), IAM roles provide fine-grained access control (confidentiality), and bucket policies add an additional layer of access restrictions. Object Lock is overkill for this scenario and doesn't address confidentiality. Versioning alone doesn't prevent deletion. ACLs are less secure than IAM-based controls.

Which tuning strategy should be employed to enhance optimization efficiency and expedite hyperparameter search?

stem: A telecommunications company is developing a generative AI troubleshooting assistant that uses RAG to answer questions from network manuals, incident reports, and engineering runbooks indexed in Amazon OpenSearch Service. The application currently relies on vector similarity search to retrieve relevant documents. Engineers report that searches often return documents with similar meaning but miss records containing exact device codes, protocol names, product identifiers, and technical acronyms. The company needs to improve retrieval accuracy by preserving semantic relevance while also matching precise terminology. The solution must continue to provide low end-user latency as the knowledge repository grows. Which solution will best meet these requirements?
correct_text: Use hybrid search to combine vector similarity search with keyword-based retrieval, improving semantic relevance while accurately matching exact terms and acronyms.

candidates.full_text: A company has thousands of scanned PDF invoices and needs to automatically extract vendor names, amounts, and line items for processing in their accounting system. Which AWS service best addresses this requirement? A. Amazon Rekognition B. Amazon Textract C. Amazon Comprehend D. Amazon Kendra ✅ B. Amazon Textract 🎯 Key trigger: "Extract structured data from scanned documents" maps directly to Textract's AnalyzeExpense API, which is specifically designed for invoice and receipt processing to extract vendor names, amounts, and line items. ⚠️ A. Rekognition - General computer vision, not optimized for structured document data extraction ⚠️ C. Comprehend - Natural language processing for sentiment/entity analysis, not document structure extraction ⚠️ D. Kendra - Enterprise search service, not document data extraction

Embeder la pregunta con un modelo de embeddings, consultar la knowledge base con ese vector y devolver los EMBEDDINGS de los N vecinos mas cercanos C. Which statement about Amazon OpenSearch Service is correct? A. It can only be deployed in a single Availability Zone for cost optimization B. It automatically provisions resources and deploys highly-tuned search indexes C. It requires manual installation and configuration of the OpenSearch engine D. It only supports basic keyword searching without analytics capabilities ✅ B. It automatically provisions resources and deploys highly-tuned search indexes 🎯 Why correct: OpenSearch Service is a fully managed service that handles provisioning, scaling, and optimization automatically. You simply upload data and it creates optimized search indexes. The other options are incorrect because: A) It supports multi-AZ deployments for high availability, C) It's fully managed requiring no manual installation, D) It provides comprehensive search and analytics capabilities beyond basic keyword search.

stem: A global e-commerce enterprise is preparing a major product launch and requires a large-scale system for continuous monitoring of customer feedback across multiple social media platforms. Social media posts are already collected and stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. Amazon Rekognition will extract visual sentiment indicators from images and videos within the collected posts, and Amazon Kendra will retrieve contextually relevant posts from a broad corpus of unstructured text, with semantic retrieval supported by an Inverted File with Flat Compression (IVFFlat) vector index. The analytics group must perform sentiment scoring across all retrieved content and must generate long-term trend visualizations for leadership teams that track sentiment changes across product categories, geographic regions, and marketing campaigns. Automated alarms based on predefined sentiment thresholds must also be configured to support rapid incident response for negative sentiment spikes during critical launch periods. Which combination of AWS services best meets these requirements?
correct_text: Trigger an AWS Lambda function whenever S3 receives a new post, and use Amazon Comprehend for sentiment detection. Save the analysis results back into S3 and publish the sentiment scores as corresponding Amazon CloudWatch metrics. Enable CloudWatch alarms to alert analysts based on configured sentiment thresholds automatically.

Which AWS service best addresses this requirement? A. Amazon Rekognition B. Amazon Textract C. Amazon Comprehend D. Amazon Kendra ✅ B. Amazon Textract 🎯 Key trigger: "Extract structured data from scanned documents" maps directly to Textract's AnalyzeExpense API, which is specifically designed for invoice and receipt processing to extract vendor names, amounts, and line items. ⚠️ A. Rekognition - General computer vision, not optimized for structured document data extraction ⚠️ C. Comprehend - Natural language processing for sentiment/entity analysis, not document structure extraction ⚠️ D. Kendra - Enterprise search service, not document data extraction

A company runs a sports web portal with resources in multiple AWS regions (EC2, RDS, IAM). The IT Security Compliance Officer requires a reliable and durable logging solution to track changes to all resources across all regions. The solution must ensure integrity and confidentiality of log data. Which solution would be the best option? A. Create a new trail in AWS CloudTrail with the global services option selected, and create one new Amazon S3 bucket to store the logs. Create IAM roles, S3 bucket policies, and enable Multi Factor Authentication (MFA) Delete on the S3 bucket storing your logs. B. Create three new CloudTrail trails, each with its own S3 bucket to store the logs: one for the AWS Management console, one for AWS SDKs, and one for command line tools. Then create IAM roles and S3 bucket policies for the S3 buckets storing your logs. C. Create a new trail in AWS CloudTrail with the global services option selected, and assign it an existing S3 bucket to store the logs. Create S3 ACLs and enable Multi Factor Authentication (MFA) delete on the S3 bucket storing your logs. D. Create a new trail in CloudTrail and assign it a new S3 bucket to store the logs. Configure AWS SNS to send delivery notifications to your management system. Secure the S3 bucket that stores your logs using IAM roles and S3 bucket policies. ✅ A. CloudTrail with global services + new S3 bucket + IAM roles + MFA Delete 🎯 Global services flag captures IAM events across regions, new S3 bucket ensures confidentiality, MFA Delete provides integrity protection. ⚠️ B — Creates unnecessary multiple trails without global services flag ⚠️ C — Uses existing S3 bucket (compromises confidentiality) and S3 ACLs instead of IAM roles ⚠️ D — Missing global services flag, won't capture IAM events 📖 Full Explanation For most services, events are recorded in the region where the action occurred to its respective AWS CloudTrail. For global services such as AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), AWS STS, Amazon CloudFront, and Route 53, events are delivered to any trail that includes global services (IncludeGlobalServiceEvents flag). AWS CloudTrail service should be your top choice for the scenarios where the application is tracking the changes made by any AWS service, resource, or API. AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) is integrated with AWS CloudTrail, a service that logs AWS events made by or on behalf of your AWS account. CloudTrail logs authenticate AWS API calls and also AWS sign-in events, and collects this event information in files that are delivered to Amazon S3 buckets. Therefore, the correct answer is: Create a new trail in AWS CloudTrail with the global services option selected, and create one new Amazon S3 bucket to store the logs. Create IAM roles, S3 bucket policies, and enable Multi Factor Authentication (MFA) Delete on the S3 bucket storing your logs. It uses AWS CloudTrail with (includeGlobalServiceEvents flag) Global Option enabled, a single new S3 bucket and IAM Roles so that it has the confidentiality, and MFA on Delete on S3 bucket so that it maintains the data integrity. The option that says: Create a new trail in AWS CloudTrail with the global services option selected, and assign it an existing S3 bucket to store the logs. Create S3 ACLs and enable Multi Factor Authentication (MFA) delete on the S3 bucket storing your logs is incorrect. As an existing S3 bucket is used, it may already be accessed by the user, hence not maintaining the confidentiality, and it is not using IAM roles. The option that says: Create three new CloudTrail trails, each with its own S3 bucket to store the logs: one for the AWS Management console, one for AWS SDKs, and one for command line tools. Then create IAM roles and S3 bucket policies for the S3 buckets storing your logs is incorrect. Although it uses AWS CloudTrail, the Global Option is not enabled, and three S3 buckets are not needed. The option that says: Create a new trail in CloudTrail and assign it a new S3 bucket to store the logs. Configure AWS SNS to send delivery notifications to your management system. Secure the S3 bucket that stores your logs using IAM roles and S3 bucket policies is incorrect. Although it uses AWS CloudTrail, the Global Option is not enabled.

A company needs to track who deleted an S3 bucket and monitor when IAM policies are modified across their multi-region AWS environment for security auditing. Which service best addresses this requirement? A. Amazon CloudWatch Logs with custom log streams B. AWS Config with configuration history tracking C. AWS CloudTrail with multi-region trail and global service events D. Amazon EventBridge with custom event patterns ✅ C. AWS CloudTrail with multi-region trail and global service events 🎯 Why CloudTrail: The trigger phrases "who deleted" and "when policies are modified" indicate the need for API call auditing . CloudTrail captures the identity (who), timestamp (when), and action details. Multi-region captures S3 deletions across regions, while global service events capture IAM policy changes. ⚠️ AWS Config tracks resource configuration changes but doesn't provide the "who" information (user identity) that performed the action.

A media company with a hybrid architecture has 50+ TB of digital videos stored on on-premises tape library. They want to implement automated facial recognition catalog with minimal disruption to existing MAM system and least management overhead . Eventually migrate to AWS. Which solution provides the least ongoing management overhead with minimal disruption? A. Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams for ingestion and Amazon Rekognition for facial recognition processing B. Set up tape gateway appliance and process videos directly from tape gateway using Lambda and Rekognition C. Set up file gateway appliance, use MAM to send files to gateway, process with Lambda and Rekognition from S3 D. Use AWS Snowball to migrate files to S3, install open-source facial recognition on EC2 instance ✅ C. File Gateway with Lambda and Rekognition processing 🎯 Why correct: File Gateway provides seamless integration with existing MAM system while automatically backing files to S3. Rekognition can directly process files from S3 with minimal architectural changes. ⚠️ A. Kinesis Video Streams Requires significant changes to MAM solution to stream files into Kinesis. Designed for real-time streaming, not processing pre-existing archived files from tape library. ⚠️ B. Tape Gateway processing Cannot process videos directly from tape gateway in real-time since it's backed by Glacier storage. Files must be retrieved from archive before processing, adding latency. ⚠️ D. Snowball + open-source tools Requires significant management overhead to maintain open-source facial recognition on EC2. Less accurate than managed Rekognition service and requires custom development.

A sports web portal company runs resources across multiple AWS regions including EC2 instances and RDS databases. The IT Security Compliance Officer requires a reliable and durable logging solution to track changes to all EC2, IAM, and RDS resources in all regions. The solution must ensure integrity and confidentiality of log data. Which solution best meets these requirements? A. Create a new trail in AWS CloudTrail with the global services option selected, and create one new Amazon S3 bucket to store the logs. Create IAM roles, S3 bucket policies, and enable Multi Factor Authentication (MFA) Delete on the S3 bucket storing your logs. B. Create three new CloudTrail trails, each with its own S3 bucket to store the logs: one for the AWS Management console, one for AWS SDKs, and one for command line tools. Then create IAM roles and S3 bucket policies for the S3 buckets storing your logs. C. Create a new trail in AWS CloudTrail with the global services option selected, and assign it an existing S3 bucket to store the logs. Create S3 ACLs and enable Multi Factor Authentication (MFA) delete on the S3 bucket storing your logs. D. Create a new trail in CloudTrail and assign it a new S3 bucket to store the logs. Configure AWS SNS to send delivery notifications to your management system. Secure the S3 bucket that stores your logs using IAM roles and S3 bucket policies. ✅ A. CloudTrail with global services, new S3 bucket, IAM roles, and MFA Delete 🎯 Why correct: The IncludeGlobalServiceEvents flag captures IAM events across all regions. A new S3 bucket ensures confidentiality, while MFA Delete protects log integrity and IAM roles provide proper access control. ⚠️ B. Three separate trails Creates unnecessary complexity with three S3 buckets when one trail can capture all API calls regardless of source (console, SDK, CLI). Missing the global services option means IAM events won't be captured properly. ⚠️ C. Existing S3 bucket with ACLs Using an existing bucket compromises confidentiality since it may already have other access permissions. S3 ACLs are less secure than IAM roles and bucket policies for this use case. ⚠️ D. No global services option Without the global services flag, IAM events won't be captured. SNS notifications are nice-to-have but don't address the core logging requirements for multi-region resource tracking.

category: AIP – Implementation and Integration
stem: A transportation company is building an Amazon Bedrock agent that provides dispatch recommendations based on live vehicle data. The agent uses Amazon SageMaker AI to generate ETA predictions and Amazon Comprehend to interpret driver feedback. The system must also integrate a custom telemetry tool that maintains a long-lived WebSocket connection to stream continuous GPS events into the agent. The development team tested serverless options but encountered connection timeouts due to execution limits. A deployment approach is needed that supports persistent network sessions without requiring server management. Which solution will meet these requirements?
correct_text: Deploy the telemetry tool as a containerized application on Amazon ECS using the AWS Fargate launch type to support long-lived WebSocket connections.

The department of education is building a learning portal in AWS to supplement their on-premises network . They need a highly available cloud infrastructure with multiple Availability Zones . Requirements: aggregate logs , automate log analysis for errors , and immediately notify IT Operations when errors breach thresholds . Which solution BEST meets these requirements? A. Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus on-premises → AWS Lambda for metrics → CloudWatch Alarm B. Amazon Kinesis agent on-premises → CloudWatch Logs → metric filter → QuickSight monitoring C. CloudWatch agent on-premises → EventBridge → metric filter → Athena monitoring D. CloudWatch agent on-premises → CloudWatch Logs → metric filter → CloudWatch Alarm ✅ D. CloudWatch agent → CloudWatch Logs → metric filter → CloudWatch Alarm 🎯 Why correct: CloudWatch agent is the proper service for collecting on-premises logs and sending to CloudWatch Logs. Metric filters convert log data to numerical metrics, and CloudWatch Alarms provide immediate notifications when thresholds are breached. ⚠️ A. Prometheus + Lambda approach Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is designed for container metrics, not general log processing. Creating custom Lambda functions for log processing is unnecessary complexity when CloudWatch already provides this functionality natively. ⚠️ B. Kinesis agent approach Kinesis agent is for streaming data ingestion, not log collection from on-premises servers. QuickSight is a business intelligence tool, not designed for real-time alerting and monitoring compared to CloudWatch Alarms. ⚠️ C. EventBridge destination Logs should go to CloudWatch Logs, not EventBridge which is for event routing. Athena is for querying data, not real-time monitoring and alerting like CloudWatch Alarms.

When should you choose Amazon ECS over AWS Lambda for containerized applications? A. When you need event-driven, stateless functions with automatic scaling B. When you have long-running processes, persistent connections, or need full container control C. When you want to avoid managing any infrastructure whatsoever D. When you need sub-second response times for simple compute tasks ✅ B. When you have long-running processes, persistent connections, or need full container control Amazon ECS • Long-running applications • Persistent connections/state • Full container orchestration • Custom networking/security • Existing Docker workflows AWS Lambda • Event-driven functions • Stateless processing • 15-minute execution limit • Automatic scaling • Pay-per-invocation 🎯 Decision rule: Choose ECS when you need container orchestration for traditional applications. Choose Lambda when you can refactor to stateless, event-driven functions under 15 minutes.

Polly: Only provides text-to-speech synthesis, cannot understand or process incoming speech or text. ⚠️ D. category: AIP – Implementation and Integration
stem: A company is building an AI-powered customer support platform that uses AWS Amplify AI Kit on the front end to integrate with Amazon Bedrock for generating human-like responses. The platform’s front end is connected to Amazon API Gateway, which triggers an AWS Lambda function. This function then calls the Bedrock API to construct responses to customer queries. During load testing, the team notices intermittent latency issues and ThrottlingException errors when the Lambda function makes requests to the Bedrock API. These issues arise primarily during peak usage hours when there is a high volume of concurrent requests, impacting the system’s ability to generate real-time responses efficiently. The team needs to ensure that the platform can handle peak traffic while reducing the frequency of ThrottlingException errors and maintaining fast response times. Which of the following should be implemented?
correct_text: Initialize the exponential backoff with jitter in the AWS SDK for retry management, and set up per-client throttling limits in API Gateway to control the request rate during high-traffic periods.

A company is decommissioning its legacy web application (Auto Scaling EC2 + ALB) and building a new serverless architecture using AWS Lambda , API Gateway , and DynamoDB . The solution requires a CI/CD pipeline to automate builds and support gradual deployments . Which is the most suitable way to build, test, and deploy the new architecture? A. Use AWS Serverless Application Repository to organize components and deploy as versioned entities B. Use AWS SAM and set up CodeBuild, CodeDeploy, and CodePipeline for CI/CD C. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to deploy the application D. Use CodeBuild, CodeDeploy, CodePipeline with Systems Manager Automation ✅ B. Use AWS SAM and set up CodeBuild, CodeDeploy, and CodePipeline for CI/CD 🎯 Why correct: AWS SAM is specifically designed for building, testing, and deploying serverless applications with Lambda, API Gateway, and DynamoDB. Combined with the AWS Code services, it provides native support for gradual deployments and automated CI/CD workflows for serverless architectures. ⚠️ A. Serverless Application Repository This is just a managed repository for discovering and sharing serverless applications. It doesn't provide the build, test, and CI/CD pipeline capabilities needed for development workflows - it's only for deployment of pre-built applications. ⚠️ C. AWS Elastic Beanstalk Elastic Beanstalk is designed for deploying traditional applications on EC2 instances, not serverless architectures. It cannot manage Lambda functions, API Gateway, or DynamoDB in a serverless context. ⚠️ D. Systems Manager Automation Systems Manager Automation is primarily for managing and configuring EC2 instances through runbooks, not for building and deploying serverless applications. It lacks the serverless-specific deployment capabilities that SAM provides.

A tech startup is launching a global mobile marketplace using AWS Amplify . Backend APIs will be deployed to multiple AWS regions to process sales and financial transactions in the region closest to users. Transactions made in one region must be automatically replicated to other regions. Expected to have millions of users across North America, South America, Europe, and Asia. Which is the most scalable, cost-effective, and highly available architecture? A. Create a Global DynamoDB table with replica tables across several AWS regions. Store transactions to a DynamoDB replica table in each local region. B. Use AWS Control Tower and Amazon Connect to launch and centrally manage multiple DynamoDB tables in various AWS Regions. C. Store transactions to a DynamoDB table in each local region. Set up AWS Lambda function to read recent writes and replay data to DynamoDB tables in all other regions. D. Create Amazon S3 buckets in all required regions. Store transactions in local S3 bucket and replicate using S3 Cross-Region Replication. ✅ A. Create a Global DynamoDB table with replica tables across several AWS regions 🎯 Why correct: DynamoDB Global Tables provides fully managed, multi-region, multi-master database with automatic replication. It eliminates the complexity of manual replication and conflict resolution while providing fast local read/write performance for global applications. ⚠️ B. AWS Control Tower and Amazon Connect AWS Control Tower is for multi-account governance and Amazon Connect is a contact center service. Neither service can set up Global DynamoDB tables or handle database replication across regions. ⚠️ C. Lambda function for replication Using Lambda to manually replicate millions of transactions across multiple regions is not scalable. This approach would require significant compute capacity, custom conflict resolution logic, and complex error handling that Global Tables handles automatically. ⚠️ D. S3 Cross-Region Replication Amazon S3 is designed for object storage, not transactional workloads. While S3 Cross-Region Replication works for objects, it's not suitable for real-time transactional data that requires ACID properties and low-latency access.

category: AIP – Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
stem: A legal research company is preparing large volumes of unstructured data, including case files, deposition transcripts, regulatory documents, and legal opinions stored in Amazon S3. The organization is building an Amazon Bedrock application that will help attorneys search, summarize, and analyze this content. Before the documents are supplied to the foundation model, the company needs to automatically discover and catalog the source files, generate auditable metadata, and apply custom transformation and text chunking logic. The solution must also validate the processed datasets and continuously track data metrics to identify quality issues before the content is used by the application. The company wants to minimize custom development and infrastructure management. Which solution will satisfy these requirements while minimizing development effort?
correct_text: Use an AWS Glue crawler to discover the source data and register its metadata in the Glue Data Catalog. Configure Glue ETL jobs to apply the required custom transformations and text-chunking logic, then use Glue Data Quality to evaluate the processed data and track quality metrics. After validation, make the transformed content available to the Bedrock application.

A company needs to process variable workloads with unpredictable timing , wants to minimize management overhead , and requires automatic scaling for containerized batch jobs. Which service best addresses this requirement? A. Amazon ECS with manual scaling B. AWS Batch with Managed Compute Environments C. Amazon EKS with Cluster Autoscaler D. It requires zero infrastructure management while handling unpredictable job timing through dynamic compute resource allocation. ECS requires manual scaling configuration and cluster management. EKS adds Kubernetes complexity. EC2 Auto Scaling requires custom job scheduling logic.

A company needs to migrate an Oracle database to PostgreSQL in AWS. This is a heterogeneous migration requiring schema and code transformation before data migration can begin. Which approach is most suitable for this database migration? A. Use AWS SAM to transform database to PostgreSQL using Lambda functions, then migrate with DMS B. Use AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) to convert source schema, then migrate data using DMS to RDS PostgreSQL C. Use AWS Application Migration Service, then use DMS to convert and migrate to RDS PostgreSQL D. Use AWS Glue to convert schema and code, then use AWS Batch with Spot instances for data migration ✅ B. Use AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) to convert source schema, then migrate data using DMS to RDS PostgreSQL 🎯 Why correct: Heterogeneous migrations require a two-step process: first convert schema/code with AWS SCT , then migrate data with AWS DMS . SCT is specifically designed for Oracle-to-PostgreSQL conversions. ⚠️ A. AWS SAM + Lambda approach AWS SAM is for building serverless applications, not database schema conversion. Lambda functions are not designed for complex Oracle-to-PostgreSQL schema transformations that require understanding database-specific syntax and data types. ⚠️ C. AWS Application Migration Service Application Migration Service migrates entire applications and infrastructure, not individual databases. While DMS is correct for data migration, this skips the critical schema conversion step that SCT provides. ⚠️ D. AWS Glue + Batch approach AWS Glue is an ETL service for data preparation and analytics, not for Oracle-to-PostgreSQL schema conversion. AWS Batch with Spot instances doesn't handle the database-specific migration complexities that DMS manages.

A print media company wants to migrate their on-premises web application to AWS. The app allows global users to search and retrieve newspaper pages stored as PNG images with OCR-converted text files . Their OCR license expires soon and they need a scalable, durable, highly available AWS architecture. Which is the best option to achieve this requirement? A. Store images in S3, use Amazon Kendra for search, lifecycle policy to Glacier after 3 months with Glacier Select for queries B. CloudFormation with EBS-backed EC2 instances, ALB, NGINX, open source search, EBS volumes with Data Lifecycle Manager C. S3 bucket with CloudFront distribution, Elastic Beanstalk multi-AZ environment, Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Textract for OCR D. S3 Intelligent-Tiering, migrate OCR software to Auto Scaling Spot instances with ALB, Amazon Rekognition for text recognition ✅ C. S3 bucket with CloudFront distribution, Elastic Beanstalk multi-AZ environment, Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Textract for OCR 🎯 Why correct: This solution replaces the expiring OCR license with managed AWS services (Textract), provides scalable storage (S3), high availability (multi-AZ Beanstalk), and robust search capabilities (OpenSearch Service). CloudFront ensures global content delivery performance. ⚠️ A. Amazon Kendra approach Kendra is an enterprise search service for existing content repositories, not designed for OCR text recognition from scanned documents. Moving frequently accessed images to Glacier would severely impact retrieval performance for a global web application. ⚠️ B. EBS-based solution EBS volumes are neither scalable nor durable compared to S3, requiring manual management and creating single points of failure. This approach lacks the cost-effectiveness and automated scaling of managed services. ⚠️ D. Rekognition with existing OCR This solution still relies on the expiring OCR software that needs replacement. Amazon Rekognition is optimized for general image recognition, while Textract is specifically designed for document text extraction.

category: AIP – Implementation and Integration
stem: A financial technology company operates a customer-facing loan eligibility platform that uses an Amazon SageMaker AI model to generate real-time premium estimates. The model’s training data is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket and continuously grows as new customer records are collected. The company wants to eliminate manual retraining cycles by building an automated pipeline that triggers retraining and redeploys the updated model to the application whenever an analyst uploads a new dataset file to the S3 bucket. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
correct_text: Create an AWS Step Functions Standard workflow. Configure the first state to invoke an AWS Lambda function with webhook handlers to respond when an analyst uploads a new file to the S3 bucket. Use SageMaker AI Pipelines to retrain and redeploy the updated model to the application. Use the next state in the workflow to execute the pipeline after the first state receives a response.

category: AIP – Testing, Validation, and Troubleshooting
stem: A company is developing a generative AI assistant that delivers personalized product recommendations, promotional messages, and customer support summaries. The assistant leverages structured purchase history, behavioral data, and unstructured customer reviews to generate customized content in real time. To ensure outputs are accurate, relevant, and unbiased, the team plans to conduct systematic model evaluation across multiple AI model versions before deploying to the full customer base. The solution integrates Amazon Comprehend to extract sentiment, entities, and key themes from reviews and messages, and Amazon SageMaker AI to train predictive models that score engagement likelihood and product interest. The team requires a deployment strategy that enables safe testing of multiple AI model versions while collecting performance and evaluation metrics to inform decision-making. Which deployment strategy is most appropriate for this scenario?
correct_text: Utilize an A/B testing strategy to route different user segments to multiple AI model versions simultaneously, collect metrics such as sentiment, entity recognition, and predicted engagement using Comprehend and SageMaker AI, and select the best-performing model based on the comparison.

category: AIP – Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications
stem: A retail enterprise utilizes a generative AI (GenAI) foundation model (FM) to automatically write product catalog descriptions. The DevOps group uses Amazon CloudWatch to monitor technical metrics, including token consumption, inference latency, and fault rates. Concurrently, the sales department measures commercial metrics, such as click-through rates and total revenue impact, in separate external systems. The enterprise requires a unified observability framework to correlate system performance directly with commercial results. This framework must provide holistic visibility across both domains and automatically alert key personnel whenever operational metrics indicate abnormal degradation. Which of the following solutions satisfies the enterprise’s requirements?
correct_text: Build custom CloudWatch dashboards that aggregate both the operational data and the imported commercial metrics to achieve unified observability. Establish CloudWatch composite alarms enhanced with anomaly detection to evaluate the correlated data. Utilize Amazon SNS to dispatch alerts to relevant personnel when performance anomalies occur.

candidates.full_text: An accounting firm runs 200+ EC2 instances (Windows and Linux) in production. They need monthly performance checks collecting system details like memory usage, disk space , and other metrics. System logs must be analyzed with AWS Analytics tools and results stored in S3 . Which is the most efficient way to collect and analyze logs with minimal effort? A. Set up unified CloudWatch Logs agent on each instance, analyze with CloudWatch Logs Insights B. Enable Traffic Mirroring, install AWS CDK, create custom daemon script for CloudWatch Logs C. Install AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) on each instance for CloudWatch Logs D. Install AWS Inspector Agent on each instance, use CloudWatch dashboard for analysis ✅ A. Set up unified CloudWatch Logs agent on each instance, analyze with CloudWatch Logs Insights 🎯 Why correct: The unified CloudWatch agent collects both logs and metrics with one installation, supports Windows/Linux, provides better performance, and CloudWatch Logs Insights enables interactive log analysis with purpose-built query language. ⚠️ B. Traffic Mirroring + AWS CDK + custom daemon Requires significant development effort to create custom monitoring solution. Traffic Mirroring only copies network traffic from ENIs, not system metrics. This violates the "minimal effort" requirement and is unnecessarily complex. ⚠️ C. AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) While valid, SSM Agent requires manual connection to instances for log troubleshooting, making it time-consuming. CloudWatch Agent is more efficient for monitoring and automatically sends data to CloudWatch Logs. ⚠️ D. AWS Inspector Agent + CloudWatch dashboard Inspector is a security assessment service for vulnerability scanning, not system performance monitoring. CloudWatch dashboards are for resource monitoring across regions, not interactive log analysis like the scenario requires.

A company needs to immediately notify operations teams when application error rates exceed 5% based on log analysis. Which AWS service best provides this immediate notification capability? A. Amazon SNS with manual monitoring B. CloudWatch Alarms with automated thresholds C. QuickSight dashboards with scheduled reports D. EventBridge rules with batch processing ✅ B. CloudWatch Alarms with automated thresholds 🎯 Perfect match: CloudWatch Alarms automatically monitor metrics in real-time and trigger immediate notifications when thresholds are breached. They integrate seamlessly with metric filters from log data. A. SNS alone requires manual triggering. C. QuickSight is for visualization, not real-time alerting. D. EventBridge with batch processing introduces delays, not immediate response.

A web application is experiencing sudden traffic spikes that overwhelm individual EC2 instances, causing application timeouts and poor user experience during peak periods. Which AWS service best addresses this scaling challenge? A. Amazon CloudWatch with custom metrics B. Application Load Balancer (ALB) with Auto Scaling C. Amazon ElastiCache for session management D. AWS Lambda for serverless processing ✅ B. Application Load Balancer with Auto Scaling 🎯 Perfect match: ALB distributes incoming traffic across multiple healthy instances while Auto Scaling automatically adds/removes instances based on demand. This combination prevents any single instance from being overwhelmed and ensures consistent performance during traffic spikes. CloudWatch provides monitoring but doesn't solve the traffic distribution problem. ElastiCache helps with data access but doesn't address instance overload. Lambda is serverless but may not be suitable for existing web application architecture.
