Visualizar y pronosticar directamente con Amazon QuickSight sin una etapa dedicada de limpieza de datos C. Procesar y pronosticar con Amazon EMR Serverless ejecutando trabajos PySpark personalizados D. Limpiar y pronosticar con un Amazon SageMaker Studio Notebook usando Pandas escrito a mano

An accounting firm has 200+ mixed Windows/Linux EC2 instances in production. Need to conduct monthly performance checks collecting system details like memory usage, disk space, and metrics . Logs will be analyzed using AWS Analytics tools and stored in S3. Must implement with minimal effort . Which is the most efficient way to collect and analyze logs from instances with minimal effort? A. Set up and configure a unified CloudWatch Logs agent in each On-Demand EC2 instance which will automatically collect and push data to CloudWatch Logs. Analyze the log data with CloudWatch Logs Insights. B. Enable Traffic Mirroring and install AWS CDK on each instance. Create custom daemon script to collect data to CloudWatch Logs. Use CloudWatch detailed monitoring and Logs Insights. C. Set up and install AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) on each instance to collect and push data to CloudWatch Logs. Analyze with CloudWatch Logs Insights. D. Set up AWS Inspector Agent on each instance to collect data to CloudWatch Logs. Use CloudWatch dashboard to analyze log data. ✅ A. Unified CloudWatch Logs agent + CloudWatch Logs Insights 🎯 Unified CloudWatch agent is AWS's recommended solution - works on both Windows/Linux, collects logs AND metrics with one agent, provides better performance than alternatives. ⚠️ B. Traffic Mirroring + CDK — Overcomplicated custom solution, Traffic Mirroring is for network traffic not system logs ⚠️ C. SSM Agent — Not designed for log collection, requires manual connection to instances ⚠️ D. Inspector Agent — Security assessment tool only, not for performance monitoring 📖 Full Explanation To collect logs from your Amazon EC2 instances and on-premises servers into CloudWatch Logs, AWS offers both a new unified CloudWatch agent, and an older CloudWatch Logs agent. It is recommended to use the unified CloudWatch agent which has the following advantages: – You can collect both logs and advanced metrics with the installation and configuration of just one agent. – The unified agent enables the collection of logs from servers running Windows Server. – If you are using the agent to collect CloudWatch metrics, the unified agent also enables the collection of additional system metrics, for in-guest visibility. – The unified agent provides better performance. CloudWatch Logs Insights enables you to interactively search and analyze your log data in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. You can perform queries to help you quickly and effectively respond to operational issues. If an issue occurs, you can use CloudWatch Logs Insights to identify potential causes and validate deployed fixes.

category: AIP – Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications
stem: A media streaming company runs a personalized content recommendation engine on Amazon EC2 instances. Each instance mounts an Amazon EBS volume that stores a local cache of pre-computed customer preference vectors, which the application reads at query time to enrich prompts before calling Amazon Bedrock foundation models for final recommendation scoring. The engineering team has observed intermittent periods in which recommendation quality degrades, and customers receive off-target suggestions, but the team cannot determine whether the root cause is EBS I/O latency starving the feature retrieval pipeline or FM behavioral drift in the Bedrock model responses. The company needs an observability solution that automatically discovers and monitors both the EC2 compute layer and the attached EBS volumes as a unified application stack, detects performance deviations from established baselines using historical patterns rather than static thresholds, and generates correlated alerts within 10 minutes when anomalies are detected across any layer of the stack. The solution must minimize the effort required for manual monitoring configuration. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
correct_text: Enable Amazon CloudWatch Application Insights on the resource group containing the EC2 instances and attached EBS volumes. Configure custom recommendation quality metrics using the embedded metric format with dimensions for customer segment and FM model ID. Use Application Insights' ML-powered anomaly detection to automatically baseline performance patterns across the EC2, EBS, and FM metric layers and generate correlated alerts when deviations are detected.

candidates.full_text: Requirements: 500GB shared dataset , multiple EC2 instances in Auto Scaling group, cost optimization , immediate access at boot , file-level operations . Which storage solution meets ALL requirements? A. Amazon S3 with download via user data script B. Amazon EFS mounted at instance launch C. Amazon EBS volumes attached to each instance D. Instance store volumes with data replication ✅ B. Amazon EFS mounted at instance launch 🎯 Why EFS wins: Shared access (one dataset, multiple instances), immediate availability (no download time), cost-effective (pay for one copy vs multiple), file-level operations (NFS protocol), and Auto Scaling compatible (automatic mounting). ⚠️ A. S3 requires downloading 500GB to each instance's local storage, increasing costs and boot time ⚠️ C. EBS requires separate 500GB volumes per instance, multiplying storage costs unnecessarily ⚠️ D. Instance store is ephemeral and requires complex replication logic for data persistence

An online media streaming startup has deployed hundreds of containerized microservices using Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate . As new features roll out, the number of running ECS tasks steadily increases. The engineering team needs to be alerted when the number of concurrently running Fargate vCPUs exceeds 75% of the service quota's maximum limit . Which solution most efficiently monitors and alerts when Fargate vCPU usage reaches 75% of the service quota? A. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor service quotas published in the AWS/Usage metric namespace. Set up an alarm when the math expression metricId/SERVICE_QUOTA(metricId)*100 is greater than 75. Configure Amazon SNS to send notifications to the operations team. B. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the sample count metric for each service in the ECS cluster. Create an alarm based on the math expression sample count/SERVICE_QUOTA(service)*100 when it exceeds 75. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to notify the operations team. C. Use AWS Service Quotas to request an increase in the Fargate task limit to 200% of the current limit. Configure AWS Health Dashboard to monitor for quota-related issues and use Amazon EventBridge to trigger an AWS Lambda function that sends notifications via Amazon SNS when the usage reaches 75% of the new limit. D. Use Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights to monitor ECS clusters and tasks. Create a custom CloudWatch dashboard that displays the current Fargate task count and the account limit. Set up a CloudWatch alarm based on a custom metric that calculates the percentage of tasks used. ✅ A. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor service quotas published in the AWS/Usage metric namespace with SERVICE_QUOTA() math expression 🎯 Why correct: AWS publishes service quota metrics in the AWS/Usage namespace, and the SERVICE_QUOTA() function retrieves the actual quota limit for calculations. This provides real-time monitoring without custom metrics or complex configurations. ⚠️ B. Sample count metric monitoring Sample count measures the number of requests or invocations, not the actual resource usage against quotas. This metric doesn't directly correlate to vCPU consumption or service quota utilization for Fargate tasks. ⚠️ C. Quota increase with AWS Health Dashboard This approach focuses on increasing quotas rather than monitoring them. AWS Health Dashboard is reactive and designed for service health notifications, not proactive quota monitoring against percentage thresholds. ⚠️ D. Custom metrics with Container Insights While Container Insights provides valuable monitoring, creating custom metrics requires additional development and maintenance effort. This is less operationally efficient than using built-in AWS/Usage namespace metrics.

A media streaming startup runs hundreds of containerized microservices on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate . They need to be alerted when Fargate vCPUs exceed 75% of service quota limits to prevent disruptions. The company plans to use ECS Anywhere for on-premises workloads. Which solution is MOST operationally efficient? A. Use CloudWatch to monitor AWS/Usage metrics. Set alarm when metricId/SERVICE_QUOTA(metricId)*100 > 75. Use SNS for notifications. B. Monitor sample count metric for each ECS service. Create alarm based on sample count/SERVICE_QUOTA(service)*100 > 75. Use SNS. C. Use Service Quotas to increase Fargate limit to 200%. Configure Health Dashboard and EventBridge/Lambda/SNS for 75% alerts. D. Use Container Insights to monitor clusters. Create custom dashboard and alarm based on custom metric for task percentage. ✅ A. CloudWatch AWS/Usage metrics with SERVICE_QUOTA() function 🎯 AWS/Usage namespace provides built-in service quota monitoring, and SERVICE_QUOTA() function automatically retrieves current limits for efficient threshold calculations. ⚠️ B — Sample count tracks requests/invocations, not actual vCPU quota usage ⚠️ C — Focuses on increasing quotas rather than monitoring; Health Dashboard is reactive, not proactive ⚠️ D — Requires custom metrics and manual configuration when native AWS/Usage metrics already exist 📖 Full Explanation Amazon CloudWatch provides metrics on service quota usage through the AWS/Usage namespace, including Fargate vCPU utilization. A CloudWatch alarm can be created using metricid/SERVICE_QUOTA(metricid)*100, where SERVICE_QUOTA() is a built-in function that retrieves the service quota for specific resources. This enables proactive monitoring when usage exceeds 75%, triggering SNS notifications to the operations team. This solution is operationally efficient as it uses native AWS services without requiring custom metrics or complex configurations.

A web application is experiencing sudden traffic spikes that overwhelm individual EC2 instances, causing application timeouts and poor user experience during peak periods. Which AWS service best addresses this scaling challenge? A. Amazon CloudWatch with custom metrics B. Application Load Balancer (ALB) with Auto Scaling C. Amazon ElastiCache for session management D. AWS Lambda for serverless processing ✅ B. Application Load Balancer with Auto Scaling 🎯 Perfect match: ALB distributes incoming traffic across multiple healthy instances while Auto Scaling automatically adds/removes instances based on demand. This combination prevents any single instance from being overwhelmed and ensures consistent performance during traffic spikes. CloudWatch provides monitoring but doesn't solve the traffic distribution problem. ElastiCache helps with data access but doesn't address instance overload. Lambda is serverless but may not be suitable for existing web application architecture.

A company hosts its online immigration system on one large EC2 instance with attached EBS volumes . The system accepts documents and photos, performs automated verification, but becomes unavailable during surges . Processing takes too long and EBS storage is insufficient for growing data uploads. Which option provides high availability and scalable storage? A. Upgrade to EBS with Provisioned IOPS and use SQS queue with Auto Scaling EC2 instances B. Use SNS to distribute tasks to EC2 instances with Auto Scaling based on SQS queue length C. Use EBS with Provisioned IOPS, SNS for task distribution, Auto Scaling based on SNS notifications D. Use S3 with cross-region replication, SQS queue, Auto Scaling EC2 instances, CloudFormation for multi-region deployment ✅ D. S3 with cross-region replication, SQS queue, Auto Scaling EC2 instances, CloudFormation for multi-region deployment 🎯 Why correct: S3 provides unlimited scalable storage for documents/photos, SQS enables reliable task distribution to multiple EC2 instances, Auto Scaling handles surge capacity, and cross-region replication ensures high availability. ⚠️ A. EBS with Provisioned IOPS and SQS EBS volumes have size limits and don't scale automatically like S3. Each EC2 instance would need its own EBS volume, making data synchronization complex and expensive compared to centralized S3 storage. ⚠️ B. SNS for task distribution SNS is for notifications, not task queuing. It doesn't provide message persistence or retry logic needed for processing tasks. SQS is designed for reliable task distribution with dead letter queues and visibility timeouts. ⚠️ C. EBS storage with SNS Combines two problems: EBS lacks scalability for growing file storage, and SNS isn't appropriate for task queuing. This doesn't solve the core storage scalability issue or provide proper task distribution.

category: AIP – Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications
stem: An AI engineer trains a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)–based computer vision model to generate detailed object representations for a custom dataset. The dataset consists of millions of high-resolution labeled images stored in Amazon S3. The engineer uses Amazon Rekognition for feature extraction on raw images before feeding it into an Amazon SageMaker training job for model fine-tuning. During training, the engineer observed that model training took significantly longer than expected due to slow data reads from S3. The training job uses an Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instance and currently accesses data using File mode. The engineer wants to improve I/O performance during training without modifying the model architecture, data preprocessing scripts, or the training infrastructure. Which action should the engineer take to optimize training performance most efficiently?
correct_text: Change the SageMaker training job’s data input configuration to FastFile mode to stream data directly from S3 without other changes.

candidates.full_text: SageMaker AI - un job de entrenamiento de k-means usa un dataset de 100 GB en S3 (10 archivos de 10 GB) y tarda demasiado. Hay que reducir el tiempo de entrenamiento con el MENOR esfuerzo operativo . Que opcion conviene? A. Comprimir el dataset en el bucket de S3 y asegurar almacenamiento para la version comprimida y la descomprimida B. Fijar el input mode a fast file mode y asegurar que la instancia tenga almacenamiento suficiente para todo el dataset C. Copiar el dataset a un sistema de archivos EFS del dominio de SageMaker y usarlo como fuente de datos del modelo D. Crear un sistema de archivos FSx for Lustre, copiar el dataset desde S3 y usarlo como fuente de datos del modelo

Acceso a datos - se hace fine-tuning de un modelo BERT en SageMaker con 150 GB de texto en S3. El entrenamiento es lento y hay que optimizar el acceso a datos para acelerarlo sin aumentar la complejidad operativa . Que solucion requiere el MENOR overhead? A. Configurar fast file mode en el training job y asegurar suficiente almacenamiento en la instancia B. Usar AWS Glue para preprocesar el dataset y guardarlo en Amazon EFS C. Habilitar pipe mode para transmitir datos directamente desde S3 a la instancia D. Configurar file mode y asegurar suficiente almacenamiento para todo el dataset

GenAI - se quiere hacer fine-tuning de un LLM para un chatbot de soporte con un enfoque low-code / no-code que automatice el entrenamiento y aproveche modelos preconstruidos. Que combinacion usar? A. SageMaker Processing jobs con scripts propios de Python y SageMaker Debugger para depurar el entrenamiento B. Amazon SageMaker Autopilot para automatizar el entrenamiento y SageMaker JumpStart para partir de modelos preconstruidos y ajustarlos C. Amazon EC2 con contenedores de Hugging Face gestionados y configurados manualmente por el equipo D. SageMaker Training Jobs para el entrenamiento y SageMaker Experiments para rastrear y gestionar las iteraciones

Privacidad - la empresa no quiere que SageMaker AI recolecte metadata sobre el uso de las librerias provistas por AWS durante los training jobs. Que debe hacer en la API CreateTrainingJob? A. Fijar la variable de entorno OPT_OUT_TRACKING en 1 B. Configurar como privada la subnet usada por SageMaker AI mediante la opcion VpcConfig C. Fijar la variable de entorno OPT_OUT_TRACKING en 0 D. Deshabilitar el uso de VPC en SageMaker AI mediante la opcion VpcConfig

A media company with a hybrid architecture has 50+ TB of digital videos stored on on-premises tape library. They want to implement automated facial recognition catalog with minimal disruption to existing MAM system and least management overhead . Eventually migrate to AWS. Which solution provides the least ongoing management overhead with minimal disruption? A. Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams for ingestion and Amazon Rekognition for facial recognition processing B. Set up tape gateway appliance and process videos directly from tape gateway using Lambda and Rekognition C. Set up file gateway appliance, use MAM to send files to gateway, process with Lambda and Rekognition from S3 D. Use AWS Snowball to migrate files to S3, install open-source facial recognition on EC2 instance ✅ C. File Gateway with Lambda and Rekognition processing 🎯 Why correct: File Gateway provides seamless integration with existing MAM system while automatically backing files to S3. Rekognition can directly process files from S3 with minimal architectural changes. ⚠️ A. Kinesis Video Streams Requires significant changes to MAM solution to stream files into Kinesis. Designed for real-time streaming, not processing pre-existing archived files from tape library. ⚠️ B. Tape Gateway processing Cannot process videos directly from tape gateway in real-time since it's backed by Glacier storage. Files must be retrieved from archive before processing, adding latency. ⚠️ D. Snowball + open-source tools Requires significant management overhead to maintain open-source facial recognition on EC2. Less accurate than managed Rekognition service and requires custom development.

category: AIP – Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications
stem: A global retail company is transforming its customer support system with a conversational AI chatbot built using Amazon Lex for natural language understanding and automated conversation flows. Amazon Transcribe is integrated for speech-to-text conversion, allowing customers to voice inquiries and interact naturally with the system. This setup improves the customer experience by enabling spoken communication, but the company now aims to automate the chatbot’s responses by leveraging its vast knowledge base of product documentation, FAQs, and support articles. The solution must quickly and accurately retrieve relevant information from the company’s documentation library. It should seamlessly integrate with existing AWS tools to provide real-time, dynamic responses to customer queries, reducing the need for manual updates or custom model training. What approach will provide the desired result with the least amount of development work?
correct_text: Utilize Amazon Kendra for indexing company documents and integrate it with the chatbot through the Kendra Query API for dynamic response generation.

candidates.full_text: A company wants to build an Interactive Voice Response (IVR) system where customers can speak naturally to check account balances and update personal information without speaking to agents. Which AWS service combination is specifically designed for this use case? A. Amazon Polly + Amazon Transcribe B. Amazon Connect + Amazon Lex C. Amazon Comprehend + Amazon Translate D. AWS Alexa for Business + Amazon Rekognition ✅ B. Amazon Connect + Amazon Lex 🎯 This is the exact use case Amazon Connect and Lex were designed for. Amazon Connect handles the contact center infrastructure, while Amazon Lex provides the conversational AI with built-in ASR and NLU to understand natural speech and execute self-service tasks. ⚠️ A. Polly + Transcribe: Polly only does text-to-speech, Transcribe only does speech-to-text. Neither provides intent understanding or dialogue management needed for IVR interactions. ⚠️ C. Comprehend + Translate: These are for text analysis and translation, not real-time voice interactions or contact center operations. ⚠️ D. Alexa for Business + Rekognition: Alexa for Business is for workplace productivity, Rekognition is for image analysis - neither addresses contact center or IVR requirements.

When building conversational AI interfaces, when should you choose Amazon Lex over Amazon Comprehend? A. When you need to analyze sentiment in customer reviews B. When you need real-time speech recognition and intent understanding C. When you need to extract entities from documents D. When you need to classify text into categories ✅ B. When you need real-time speech recognition and intent understanding Amazon Lex • Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) • Natural Language Understanding (NLU) • Intent recognition and slot filling • Conversational chatbots and voice interfaces • Real-time dialogue management Amazon Comprehend • Text analysis and insights • Sentiment analysis • Entity extraction • Document classification • Batch processing of text documents 🎯 Decision rule: Choose Lex when building interactive conversational interfaces that need to understand spoken or typed user input in real-time. Choose Comprehend when analyzing existing text content for insights, sentiment, or classification.

Requirements: Cloud contact center with automatic speech recognition , natural language understanding , intent recognition , and ability to maintain conversation context across multiple interactions. Which AWS service meets ALL these requirements for conversational AI? A. Amazon Transcribe B. Amazon Polly C. Amazon Lex D. Amazon Comprehend ✅ C. Amazon Lex 🎯 Why: Amazon Lex provides ASR (speech-to-text), NLU (natural language understanding), intent recognition with slot filling, and context management across conversations. It's specifically designed for building conversational interfaces and chatbots. ⚠️ A. Transcribe: Only provides speech-to-text conversion, lacks NLU, intent recognition, and context management. ⚠️ B. Polly: Only provides text-to-speech synthesis, cannot understand or process incoming speech or text. ⚠️ D. Comprehend: Analyzes text for insights but lacks ASR capabilities and real-time conversational context management.

A BPO startup needs a scalable call center system on AWS that can handle thousands of inbound calls with self-service capabilities (password changes, balance checks) without agents. Requirements: automatic speech recognition (ASR) , natural language understanding , and integration with business applications . Which solution should the Solutions Architect implement? A. AWS Ground Station + Amazon Alexa for Business + Lambda B. Amazon Connect + Amazon Comprehend + Lambda C. Amazon Connect + Amazon Lex + Lambda D. AWS Elemental MediaConnect + Amazon Polly + Lambda ✅ C. Amazon Connect + Amazon Lex + Lambda 🎯 Amazon Connect provides cloud contact center functionality, while Amazon Lex offers both ASR and NLU for conversational chatbots that can handle self-service tasks. ⚠️ A. Ground Station is for satellite communications, not contact centers ⚠️ B. Comprehend analyzes text but lacks ASR/NLU for voice interactions ⚠️ D. MediaConnect is for live video transport, Polly only does text-to-speech 📖 Full Explanation Amazon Connect provides a seamless omnichannel experience through a single unified contact center for voice and chat. Amazon Lex is a service for building conversational interfaces into any application using voice and text. Amazon Lex provides the advanced deep learning functionalities of automatic speech recognition (ASR) for converting speech to text and natural language understanding (NLU) to recognize the intent of the text, enabling you to build applications with highly engaging user experiences and lifelike conversational interactions. By using an Amazon Lex chatbot in your Amazon Connect call center, callers can perform tasks such as changing a password, requesting a balance on an account, or scheduling an appointment without needing to speak to an agent. Amazon Lex uses AWS Lambda functions to query your business applications, provide information back to callers, and make updates as requested.

Which statement about Amazon Connect contact flows is correct? A. Contact flows can only handle voice calls, not chat or text interactions B. Contact flows are comprised of blocks that define customer interaction steps and can invoke Lambda functions or Lex bots C. Contact flows must be programmed using AWS SDK and cannot use visual interfaces D. Contact flows are limited to simple menu options and cannot integrate with external systems ✅ B. Contact flows are comprised of blocks that define customer interaction steps and can invoke Lambda functions or Lex bots 🎯 Amazon Connect contact flows are visual workflows similar to IVR systems. Each block represents an interaction step (play prompt, get input, branch logic). They can invoke Lambda functions for business logic and Amazon Lex bots for conversational AI, enabling sophisticated customer experiences with external system integration. ⚠️ A: Connect supports omnichannel experiences including voice, web chat, and mobile chat through the same contact flows. ⚠️ C: Contact flows use a visual, drag-and-drop interface in the Connect console, not SDK programming. ⚠️ D: Contact flows extensively integrate with external systems via Lambda functions and can create complex, dynamic interactions.

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A healthcare organization is implementing a generative AI solution to process and analyze sensitive medical records, including patient histories and diagnostic images. The solution uses Amazon Rekognition for image analysis to extract features from diagnostic images and Amazon Textract for extracting text from scanned medical forms. The organization must ensure that only authorized users and services have access to specific subsets of sensitive medical data stored in Amazon S3, with the ability to classify sensitive datasets (e.g., patient health information, diagnostic images, billing records) using metadata. The team requires a solution that provides granular control over data access, ensuring that only authorized users and services can access specific portions of sensitive data for processing and inference. The solution must allow secure data access management, with the ability to monitor and audit all data access events to maintain privacy and security. Which solution best achieves these requirements?
correct_text: Leverage AWS Lake Formation with LF-Tag-based to apply fine-grained access control policies, enabling comprehensive data governance with built-in auditing and encryption for compliance.

candidates.full_text: A company has thousands of scanned PDF invoices and needs to automatically extract vendor names, amounts, and line items for processing in their accounting system. Which AWS service best addresses this requirement? A. Amazon Rekognition B. Amazon Textract C. Amazon Comprehend D. Amazon Kendra ✅ B. Amazon Textract 🎯 Key trigger: "Extract structured data from scanned documents" maps directly to Textract's AnalyzeExpense API, which is specifically designed for invoice and receipt processing to extract vendor names, amounts, and line items. ⚠️ A. Rekognition - General computer vision, not optimized for structured document data extraction ⚠️ C. Comprehend - Natural language processing for sentiment/entity analysis, not document structure extraction ⚠️ D. Kendra - Enterprise search service, not document data extraction

An IT consulting company uses AWS Organizations with multiple accounts grouped into OUs. Security team discovered an unauthorized third-party account was added to the organization with high-level access privileges . No damage occurred yet, but they need to implement monitoring for organizational changes . Which actions should be taken to set up proper monitoring? (Select TWO.) A. Create a trail in Amazon CloudTrail to capture all API calls to AWS Organizations. Use Amazon EventBridge and SNS to raise events when administrator-specified actions occur. B. Monitor all changes using Systems Manager and use Amazon EventBridge to notify of any new activity. C. Use AWS Config to monitor compliance of AWS Organizations. Set up SNS Topic or Amazon EventBridge for change alerts. D. Configure AWS Control Tower to manage child accounts. Use Amazon Inspector to analyze breaches and notify via SNS. ✅ A and C. CloudTrail + EventBridge/SNS and AWS Config aggregation 🎯 Why correct: CloudTrail captures all Organizations API calls (including unauthorized account additions) while EventBridge can trigger on specific organizational events. AWS Config's multi-account aggregation enables centralized compliance monitoring across the entire organization. ⚠️ B. Systems Manager monitoring Systems Manager is designed for EC2 instances, on-premises servers, and AWS resource configuration management - not for monitoring AWS Organizations structural changes like account additions or OU modifications. ⚠️ D. Control Tower + Inspector While Control Tower can manage accounts, Amazon Inspector is a vulnerability assessment service for workloads and applications, not an organizational event monitoring tool for detecting unauthorized account additions.

An IT consulting company uses AWS Organizations with multiple accounts grouped into OUs. Security team discovered an unauthorized third-party AWS account was added to the organization with high-level access privileges. No detrimental actions occurred yet. Which actions should the solutions architect take to set up monitoring for changes to AWS accounts ? (Select TWO.) A. Create a trail in Amazon CloudTrail to capture all API calls to your AWS Organizations, including calls from the AWS Organizations console and from code calls to the AWS Organizations APIs. Use Amazon EventBridge and SNS to raise events when administrator-specified actions occur in an organization and send a notification to you. B. Monitor all changes to your organization using Systems Manager and use Amazon EventBridge to notify you of any new activity to your account. C. Use AWS Config to monitor the compliance of your AWS Organizations. Set up an SNS Topic or Amazon EventBridge that will send alerts to you for any changes. D. Configure AWS Control Tower to manage and monitor all child accounts under the organization. Use Amazon Inspector to analyze any possible breach and notify the administrators using AWS SNS. E. Set up a CloudWatch Dashboard to monitor any changes to your organizations and create an SNS topic that would send you a notification. ✅ A & C: CloudTrail + EventBridge/SNS for API calls, AWS Config for compliance monitoring 🎯 CloudTrail captures Organizations API calls, Config aggregates compliance data across accounts - both can trigger EventBridge/SNS for real-time alerts. ⚠️ B: Systems Manager manages EC2/servers, not Organizations structure ⚠️ D: Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, not account changes ⚠️ E: CloudWatch Dashboard visualizes metrics, doesn't monitor Organizations configuration 📖 Full Explanation AWS Organizations can work with CloudWatch Events to raise events when administrator-specified actions occur in an organization. For example, because of the sensitivity of such actions, most administrators would want to be warned every time someone creates a new account in the organization or when an administrator of a member account attempts to leave the organization. You can configure CloudWatch Events rules that look for these actions and then send the generated events to administrator-defined targets. Targets can be an Amazon SNS topic that emails or text messages its subscribers. Combining this with Amazon CloudTrail, you can set an event to trigger whenever a matching API call is received. Multi-account, multi-region data aggregation in AWS Config enables you to aggregate AWS Config data from multiple accounts and regions into a single account. Multi-account, multi-region data aggregation is useful for central IT administrators to monitor compliance for multiple AWS accounts in the enterprise. An aggregator is a new resource type in AWS Config that collects AWS Config data from multiple source accounts and regions.

Elegir servicio de IA generativa: una empresa de salud quiere probar y comparar distintos foundation models , adaptarlos a sus datos clinicos manteniendo esos datos privados, y consumirlos pagando por uso, sin aprovisionar ni operar servidores ni endpoints . Qu servicio encaja mejor? A. Amazon SageMaker Canvas: interfaz no-code con modelos administrados para construir y personalizar modelos sin escribir codigo B. Amazon SageMaker Studio: IDE administrado para elegir, entrenar y ajustar modelos gestionando el computo desde un solo lugar C. Amazon SageMaker JumpStart: catalogo de foundation models con fine-tuning privado que despliegas en endpoints en tu cuenta D. Amazon Bedrock: acceso por API a varios foundation models, con fine-tuning privado y consumo serverless pagando por uso

A company needs to ensure log file integrity for compliance audits, prevent accidental deletion of critical audit logs, and maintain confidentiality of sensitive API call data stored in S3. Which combination of S3 security features best meets ALL requirements? A. S3 Object Lock with Legal Hold and bucket-level public read blocking B. MFA Delete, IAM roles with least privilege, and S3 bucket policies C. S3 versioning with Cross-Region Replication and KMS encryption D. S3 Access Control Lists (ACLs) and CloudWatch monitoring ✅ B. MFA Delete, IAM roles with least privilege, and S3 bucket policies 🎯 MFA Delete prevents accidental deletion (integrity), IAM roles provide fine-grained access control (confidentiality), and bucket policies add an additional layer of access restrictions. Object Lock is overkill for this scenario and doesn't address confidentiality. Versioning alone doesn't prevent deletion. ACLs are less secure than IAM-based controls.

category: AIP – Implementation and Integration
stem: A company manages a large-scale analytics platform that stores high-volume transaction data in a PostgreSQL database. The dataset includes hundreds of millions of records with customer details, purchase amounts, product categories, and regions. The analytics team wants to use Amazon SageMaker AI to predict which customers are likely to churn in the next 90 days and improve retention strategies. The company needs a solution that automates data extraction and preparation from the PostgreSQL database for scheduled cleaning, normalization, and handling of missing values. After refining the data, the team considers using SageMaker Feature Store to store and manage customer features for consistent inputs in machine learning workflows. Analysts should then be able to build and deploy a no-code churn-prediction model and easily generate predictions on new customer data without support from data scientists. Some architects also evaluated Amazon DocumentDB for the future modernization of application workloads. Which is the best option to achieve this requirement?
correct_text: Use AWS Glue DataBrew to extract the data from PostgreSQL, clean and normalize the dataset, and write the prepared data back into Amazon S3. Import the cleaned dataset into SageMaker Canvas to build a no-code churn-prediction model and generate predictions for business analysts.

candidates.full_text: A company needs to migrate an Oracle database to PostgreSQL in AWS. This is a heterogeneous migration requiring schema and code transformation before data migration can begin. Which approach is most suitable for this database migration? A. Use AWS SAM to transform database to PostgreSQL using Lambda functions, then migrate with DMS B. Use AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) to convert source schema, then migrate data using DMS to RDS PostgreSQL C. Use AWS Application Migration Service, then use DMS to convert and migrate to RDS PostgreSQL D. Use AWS Glue to convert schema and code, then use AWS Batch with Spot instances for data migration ✅ B. Use AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) to convert source schema, then migrate data using DMS to RDS PostgreSQL 🎯 Why correct: Heterogeneous migrations require a two-step process: first convert schema/code with AWS SCT , then migrate data with AWS DMS . SCT is specifically designed for Oracle-to-PostgreSQL conversions. ⚠️ A. AWS SAM + Lambda approach AWS SAM is for building serverless applications, not database schema conversion. Lambda functions are not designed for complex Oracle-to-PostgreSQL schema transformations that require understanding database-specific syntax and data types. ⚠️ C. AWS Application Migration Service Application Migration Service migrates entire applications and infrastructure, not individual databases. While DMS is correct for data migration, this skips the critical schema conversion step that SCT provides. ⚠️ D. AWS Glue + Batch approach AWS Glue is an ETL service for data preparation and analytics, not for Oracle-to-PostgreSQL schema conversion. AWS Batch with Spot instances doesn't handle the database-specific migration complexities that DMS manages.

A company migrating from on-premises Oracle to PostgreSQL on AWS requires heterogeneous database migration with schema and code transformation prior to data migration. Which approach is most suitable? A. Use AWS SAM with Lambda functions to transform database to PostgreSQL. Migrate using DMS to RDS. B. Use AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) to convert source schema. Migrate data using DMS to RDS for PostgreSQL. C. Migrate using AWS Application Migration Service, then use DMS to convert and migrate to RDS PostgreSQL. D. Use AWS Glue to convert schema/code. Use AWS Batch with Spot instances to migrate data. ✅ B. Use AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) to convert source schema. Migrate data using DMS to RDS for PostgreSQL. 🎯 Heterogeneous migrations require SCT for schema conversion first, then DMS for data migration. This is the standard two-step AWS process. ⚠️ A. SAM — Framework for serverless apps, not database migration ⚠️ C. Application Migration Service — For entire applications, not database schema conversion ⚠️ D. Glue — ETL service, not designed for Oracle to PostgreSQL schema conversion 📖 Full Explanation AWS Database Migration Service helps you migrate databases to AWS quickly and securely. The source database remains fully operational during the migration, minimizing downtime to applications that rely on the database. The AWS Database Migration Service can migrate your data to and from the most widely used commercial and open-source databases. AWS Database Migration Service can migrate your data to and from most of the widely used commercial and open-source databases. It supports homogeneous migrations, such as Oracle to Oracle, as well as heterogeneous migrations between different database platforms, such as Oracle to Amazon Aurora. Migrations can be from on-premises databases to Amazon RDS or Amazon EC2, databases running on EC2 to RDS, or vice versa, as well as from one RDS database to another RDS database. It can also move data between SQL, NoSQL, and text-based targets. In heterogeneous database migrations, the source and target databases engines are different, like in the case of Oracle to Amazon Aurora, Oracle to PostgreSQL, or Microsoft SQL Server to MySQL migrations. In this case, the schema structure, data types, and database code of source and target databases can be quite different, requiring a schema and code transformation before the data migration starts. That makes heterogeneous migrations a two-step process. Hence, the correct answer is: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool to convert the source schema and code to match that of the target database, and then use the AWS Database Migration Service to migrate data from the source database to the target database. All the required data type conversions will automatically be done by the AWS Database Migration Service during the migration. The source database can be located in your own premises outside of AWS, running on an Amazon EC2 instance, or it can be an Amazon RDS database. The target can be a database in Amazon EC2 or Amazon RDS.

A company needs to migrate MySQL databases from on-premises to AWS with minimal downtime and wants to maintain the same database engine for compatibility . Which combination of services best addresses this requirement? A. AWS SCT + Amazon DynamoDB B. AWS DMS + Amazon RDS MySQL C. AWS DataSync + Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL D. AWS Backup + Amazon DocumentDB ✅ B. AWS DMS + Amazon RDS MySQL 🎯 Perfect match: DMS provides continuous data replication for minimal downtime migration. RDS MySQL maintains the same engine for full compatibility. This is a homogeneous migration requiring no schema changes. ⚠️ A: SCT + DynamoDB changes from relational to NoSQL, breaking compatibility. ⚠️ C: DataSync is for file migration, and PostgreSQL changes the database engine. ⚠️ D: Backup doesn't provide continuous replication, and DocumentDB is for MongoDB workloads.

Requirements: Migrate Oracle database to PostgreSQL with minimal downtime , preserve all stored procedures , and maintain data consistency during migration. Which combination of services meets ALL requirements? A. AWS Application Migration Service + RDS B. AWS SCT + DMS + RDS PostgreSQL C. AWS Glue + Lambda + RDS PostgreSQL D. AWS DataSync + EC2 + PostgreSQL ✅ B. AWS SCT + DMS + RDS PostgreSQL 🎯 Requirements mapping: • Preserve stored procedures: SCT converts Oracle PL/SQL to PostgreSQL functions • Minimal downtime: DMS keeps source database operational during migration • Data consistency: DMS handles ongoing replication and validation • Target platform: RDS PostgreSQL provides managed database service

category: AIP – Testing, Validation, and Troubleshooting
stem: A financial services company has deployed a binary classification model to an Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoint to predict loan default risk. After operating in production for several months, the data science team suspects the model’s accuracy has degraded due to changes in applicant demographics and economic conditions. The team needs a solution that automatically detects when the statistical distribution of incoming inference data deviates from the training data baseline. The solution must also schedule periodic monitoring jobs without manual intervention and publish drift-violation metrics to Amazon CloudWatch for automated alerting. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?
correct_text: Enable data capture on the SageMaker real-time endpoint and use SageMaker Model Monitor to create a statistical baseline from the training dataset. Configure a monitoring schedule to automatically compare incoming inference data against the baseline constraints and publish drift violation metrics to CloudWatch.

They integrate seamlessly with metric filters from log data. A. SNS alone requires manual triggering. C. QuickSight is for visualization, not real-time alerting. D. EventBridge with batch processing introduces delays, not immediate response.

A company receives sensor data every millisecond from manufacturing equipment and needs to detect anomalies in real-time to prevent equipment failure. Which AWS service is best suited for this use case? A. Amazon SQS with Lambda processing B. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Analytics C. Amazon S3 with scheduled EMR jobs D. Amazon RDS with stored procedures ✅ B. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Analytics 🎯 Trigger keywords: "every millisecond" + "real-time anomaly detection" = streaming analytics requirement. Kinesis Data Streams ingests high-frequency sensor data, while Kinesis Analytics runs SQL queries for real-time anomaly detection using sliding windows and statistical functions. SQS + Lambda: SQS has throughput limits and Lambda has execution time limits - not suitable for continuous millisecond data streams requiring real-time processing.

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A healthcare organization is building an enterprise search tool using Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases. The underlying corporate data resides in an Amazon S3 data lake, which is cataloged using AWS Glue. The organization must enforce strict access controls to ensure that different departments can only query documents that correspond to specific departmental data. The security team wants to implement fine-grained access control at the database, table, and column level using a scalable, attribute-based approach rather than managing complex AWS IAM policies for every individual user and resource combination. Which solution will securely meet these requirements with the least operational overhead?
correct_text: Implement AWS Lake Formation and assign an LF-Tag to the databases, tables, and columns representing the departmental data. Grant IAM principals access to the data lake resources based on the matching LF-Tag expressions.

candidates.full_text: A company has multiple AWS accounts for different departments (finance, HR, engineering). Each account has a Systems Administrator with root access . The company needs to centrally manage policies to allow or deny AWS services for individual accounts or groups of accounts. Which is the most suitable solution with the LEAST complexity? A. Connect all departments by setting up cross-account access to each AWS account. Create and attach IAM policies to resources based on departments. B. Use AWS Organizations and Service Control Policies to control the list of AWS services that can be used by each member account. C. Set up AWS Organizations and Organizational Units (OU) to connect all AWS accounts. Create a custom IAM Policy to allow or deny certain AWS services for each account. D. Provide access to externally authenticated users via Identity Federation. Set up an IAM role to specify permissions for users from each department. ✅ B. Use AWS Organizations and Service Control Policies 🎯 Why correct: Service Control Policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations are specifically designed for centrally managing permissions across multiple AWS accounts. Unlike IAM policies which only affect users/groups/roles within an account, SCPs can restrict even the root user and affect all identities in member accounts. ⚠️ A. Cross-account access with IAM policies This approach creates significant complexity with multiple cross-account trust relationships and doesn't provide centralized policy management. Each account would need individual IAM policy configuration, defeating the purpose of centralized control. ⚠️ C. AWS Organizations with custom IAM Policy While AWS Organizations is correct, IAM policies cannot restrict services across accounts or affect the root user. Only Service Control Policies (SCPs) can centrally control AWS service access across multiple accounts in an organization. ⚠️ D. Identity Federation with IAM roles This solution addresses user authentication but doesn't solve the core requirement of centrally managing service permissions across multiple AWS accounts. It focuses on federated access rather than service control.

A company has multiple AWS accounts for different departments (finance, HR, engineering). Each account is managed by Systems Administrators with root access. Requirement: centrally manage policies across multiple AWS accounts to allow/deny specific AWS services for individual accounts or groups of accounts. Which is the most suitable solution with the LEAST complexity? A. Connect all departments by setting up cross-account access to each of the AWS accounts of the company. Create and attach IAM policies to your resources based on their respective departments to control access. B. Use AWS Organizations and Service Control Policies to control the list of AWS services that can be used by each member account. C. Set up AWS Organizations and Organizational Units (OU) to connect all AWS accounts of each department. Create a custom IAM Policy to allow or deny the use of certain AWS services for each account. D. Provide access to externally authenticated users via Identity Federation. Set up an IAM role to specify permissions for users from each department whose identity is federated from your organization or a third-party identity provider. ✅ B. Use AWS Organizations and Service Control Policies 🎯 SCPs centrally control AWS service access across multiple accounts and can restrict even root users, unlike IAM policies which only work within individual accounts. ⚠️ A. Cross-account access — Too complex for multiple accounts, more suited for 2-account scenarios ⚠️ C. Custom IAM Policy — IAM policies can't restrict services across accounts, need SCPs not IAM ⚠️ D. Identity Federation — Focuses on authentication, not service-level policy management across accounts 📖 Full Explanation AWS Organizations offers policy-based management for multiple AWS accounts. With Organizations, you can create groups of accounts, automate account creation, and apply and manage policies for those groups. Organizations enables you to centrally manage policies across multiple accounts, without requiring custom scripts and manual processes. It allows you to create Service Control Policies (SCPs) that centrally control AWS service use across multiple AWS accounts. Remember that AWS Organizations does not replace associating IAM policies with users, groups, and roles within an AWS account. Hence, you still need to set up appropriate IAM policies for your root and member accounts. IAM policies let you allow or deny access to AWS services (such as Amazon S3), individual AWS resources (such as a specific S3 bucket), or individual API actions (such as s3:CreateBucket). An IAM policy can be applied only to IAM users, groups, or roles, and it can never restrict the root identity of the AWS account. By contrast, AWS Organizations lets you use service control policies (SCPs) to allow or deny access to particular AWS services for individual AWS accounts, or for groups of accounts within an organizational unit (OU). The specified actions from an attached SCP affect all IAM users, groups, and roles for an account, including the root account identity.

A sports web portal company runs resources across multiple AWS regions including EC2 instances and RDS databases. The IT Security Compliance Officer requires a reliable and durable logging solution to track changes to all EC2, IAM, and RDS resources in all regions. The solution must ensure integrity and confidentiality of log data. Which solution best meets these requirements? A. Create a new trail in AWS CloudTrail with the global services option selected, and create one new Amazon S3 bucket to store the logs. Create IAM roles, S3 bucket policies, and enable Multi Factor Authentication (MFA) Delete on the S3 bucket storing your logs. B. Create three new CloudTrail trails, each with its own S3 bucket to store the logs: one for the AWS Management console, one for AWS SDKs, and one for command line tools. Then create IAM roles and S3 bucket policies for the S3 buckets storing your logs. C. Create a new trail in AWS CloudTrail with the global services option selected, and assign it an existing S3 bucket to store the logs. Create S3 ACLs and enable Multi Factor Authentication (MFA) delete on the S3 bucket storing your logs. D. Create a new trail in CloudTrail and assign it a new S3 bucket to store the logs. Configure AWS SNS to send delivery notifications to your management system. Secure the S3 bucket that stores your logs using IAM roles and S3 bucket policies. ✅ A. CloudTrail with global services, new S3 bucket, IAM roles, and MFA Delete 🎯 Why correct: The IncludeGlobalServiceEvents flag captures IAM events across all regions. A new S3 bucket ensures confidentiality, while MFA Delete protects log integrity and IAM roles provide proper access control. ⚠️ B. Three separate trails Creates unnecessary complexity with three S3 buckets when one trail can capture all API calls regardless of source (console, SDK, CLI). Missing the global services option means IAM events won't be captured properly. ⚠️ C. Existing S3 bucket with ACLs Using an existing bucket compromises confidentiality since it may already have other access permissions. S3 ACLs are less secure than IAM roles and bucket policies for this use case. ⚠️ D. No global services option Without the global services flag, IAM events won't be captured. SNS notifications are nice-to-have but don't address the core logging requirements for multi-region resource tracking.

An IT consulting company uses AWS Organizations with multiple accounts grouped into OUs. Security team discovered an unauthorized third-party account was added to the organization with high-level access privileges . No damage occurred yet, but they need to implement monitoring for organizational changes . Which actions should be taken to set up proper monitoring? (Select TWO.) A. Create a trail in Amazon CloudTrail to capture all API calls to AWS Organizations. Use Amazon EventBridge and SNS to raise events when administrator-specified actions occur. B. Monitor all changes using Systems Manager and use Amazon EventBridge to notify of any new activity. C. Use AWS Config to monitor compliance of AWS Organizations. Set up SNS Topic or Amazon EventBridge for change alerts. D. Configure AWS Control Tower to manage child accounts. Use Amazon Inspector to analyze breaches and notify via SNS. ✅ A and C. CloudTrail + EventBridge/SNS and AWS Config aggregation 🎯 Why correct: CloudTrail captures all Organizations API calls (including unauthorized account additions) while EventBridge can trigger on specific organizational events. AWS Config's multi-account aggregation enables centralized compliance monitoring across the entire organization. ⚠️ B. Systems Manager monitoring Systems Manager is designed for EC2 instances, on-premises servers, and AWS resource configuration management - not for monitoring AWS Organizations structural changes like account additions or OU modifications. ⚠️ D. Control Tower + Inspector While Control Tower can manage accounts, Amazon Inspector is a vulnerability assessment service for workloads and applications, not an organizational event monitoring tool for detecting unauthorized account additions.

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A company has developed a machine learning-based recommendation system designed to personalize content for users. The model has been trained using Amazon SageMaker AI built-in algorithms and a custom dataset, with real-time inference being performed within SageMaker AI. As part of the system, the company also intends to leverage Amazon Comprehend for natural language processing to analyze customer reviews and sentiment, which will further enhance the recommendation engine. To meet strict security and compliance requirements, the company must ensure that both the training and inference environments, as well as all associated services, are deployed within a secure Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). Furthermore, the solution must completely block all access to the internet or any external resources to protect sensitive user data and ensure compliance with regulatory standards. Which of the following will satisfy the given requirements with the LEAST development effort?
correct_text: Activate SageMaker AI network isolation mode to block all external access and establish a VPC endpoint for Comprehend within the same VPC.

When building conversational AI interfaces, when should you choose Amazon Lex over Amazon Comprehend? A. When you need to analyze sentiment in customer reviews B. When you need real-time speech recognition and intent understanding C. When you need to extract entities from documents D. When you need to classify text into categories ✅ B. When you need real-time speech recognition and intent understanding Amazon Lex • Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) • Natural Language Understanding (NLU) • Intent recognition and slot filling • Conversational chatbots and voice interfaces • Real-time dialogue management Amazon Comprehend • Text analysis and insights • Sentiment analysis • Entity extraction • Document classification • Batch processing of text documents 🎯 Decision rule: Choose Lex when building interactive conversational interfaces that need to understand spoken or typed user input in real-time. Choose Comprehend when analyzing existing text content for insights, sentiment, or classification.

Requirements: DNS resolution for internal services , cross-VPC accessibility , no internet exposure , custom domain names , integration with existing VPC peering . Public zones expose to internet, Resolver endpoints are for hybrid connectivity, CloudFront is for content delivery not internal DNS resolution.

A government agency has multiple VPCs in various AWS regions across the United States that need to be linked up to an on-premises central office network in Washington, D.C. The central office requires inter-region VPC access over a private network that is dedicated to each region for enhanced security and more predictable data transfer performance. Your team needs to quickly build this network mesh and minimize management overhead. Which option provides the most secure, highly available, and durable solution for this interconnectivity? A. Utilize AWS Direct Connect Gateway for inter-region VPC access. Create a virtual private gateway in each VPC, then create a private virtual interface for each AWS Direct Connect connection to the Direct Connect gateway. B. Enable inter-region VPC peering which allows peering relationships to be established between VPCs across different AWS regions. C. Implement a hub-and-spoke network topology in each region using AWS Transit Gateway. Route traffic between VPCs and the on-premise network over AWS Site-to-Site VPN. D. Create a link aggregation group (LAG) with AWS Direct Connect Gateway and create public virtual interfaces for each connection. ✅ A. AWS Direct Connect Gateway with private virtual interfaces 🎯 Why correct: Direct Connect Gateway provides dedicated network connections with predictable performance across multiple regions while minimizing management overhead. Private virtual interfaces ensure traffic stays within AWS backbone without traversing public internet, meeting the security and performance requirements. ⚠️ B. Inter-region VPC peering While VPC peering keeps traffic on AWS backbone, it requires extensive manual setup and management overhead to create a functional multi-region network mesh. The connections are not dedicated and don't provide the enhanced performance guarantees required by the government agency. ⚠️ C. Transit Gateway with Site-to-Site VPN Site-to-Site VPN uses internet-based connections rather than dedicated private network connections. This doesn't meet the requirement for dedicated network connectivity and enhanced security that the government agency specifically needs. ⚠️ D. LAG with public virtual interfaces Public virtual interfaces are used for accessing AWS public services, not VPC resources. The scenario requires private connectivity to VPC resources. Additionally, LAG is unnecessary complexity for this use case and doesn't address the core connectivity requirements.

Amazon Athena para consultar la ingestion y un notebook de SageMaker para desplegar el modelo a produccion D. AWS Glue para los pipelines de ingestion de datos y Amazon SageMaker Studio (Classic) para desplegar el modelo

Amazon SageMaker Multi-Model Endpoints B. Amazon SageMaker Automatic Scaling C. Amazon SageMaker Inference Recommender D. Amazon SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning

When should you use NAT Gateway versus VPC Endpoints for private subnet internet access? A. Always use VPC Endpoints as they're more secure than NAT Gateway B. Use NAT Gateway for general internet access, VPC Endpoints for specific AWS services C. VPC Endpoints are cheaper so should be used whenever possible D. NAT Gateway only works with public subnets, VPC Endpoints work with private subnets ✅ B. Use NAT Gateway for general internet access, VPC Endpoints for specific AWS services NAT Gateway • General internet/external API access • ECR image pulls from internet • Third-party service calls • Software updates/packages • Charges for data processing VPC Endpoints • Direct private access to AWS services • S3, DynamoDB (Gateway endpoints) • ECR, ECS, other services (Interface endpoints) • No internet gateway required • No data processing charges 🎯 Decision rule: Use NAT Gateway when tasks need general internet access. Use VPC Endpoints when accessing AWS services privately without internet routing.

category: AIP – Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications
stem: A Generative AI engineering team is developing a supervised image recognition model to accurately identify pandas from a diverse dataset of wildlife photographs. Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth is used to label 1,000 panda images and split the data into training and testing sets, reserving 100 images as a constant test set. Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels is then configured to train a custom image classification model capable of recognizing distinctive panda features such as fur patterns, posture, and environmental background. During the evaluation phase, the engineering team observes that the image classifier misclassifies several test images. A closer analysis reveals that in more than 75% of the misclassified images, the pandas appear upside down, indicating the model’s sensitivity to image orientation. The team must enhance the model’s ability to correctly identify pandas regardless of orientation, without collecting an entirely new dataset or extensively modifying the existing training pipeline. Which approach will most effectively enhance the model’s accuracy in addressing this specific misclassification issue?
correct_text: Expand the existing training dataset by introducing data augmentation techniques such as image rotation, flipping, and scaling.

Object Detection (dibuja cajas y clasifica multiples objetos por imagen) B. Image Classification (asigna una unica etiqueta a la imagen completa) C. Object2Vec (aprende representaciones vectoriales de objetos) D. Semantic Segmentation (clasifica cada pixel de la imagen)

SageMaker vision - un vehiculo autonomo necesita etiquetar a nivel de pixel toda la escena (ej. carretera vs peaton vs cielo), no solo localizar objetos. Que algoritmo integrado corresponde? A. Object Detection - MXNet (dibuja cajas alrededor de objetos) B. Semantic Segmentation (mapa denso que asigna una clase a cada region de la escena) C. Object2Vec (aprende embeddings de objetos discretos) D. Image Classification (asigna una unica etiqueta a la imagen completa)

A media company with a hybrid architecture has 50+ TB of digital videos stored on on-premises tape library. They want to implement automated facial recognition catalog with minimal disruption to existing MAM system and least management overhead . Eventually migrate to AWS. Which solution provides the least ongoing management overhead with minimal disruption? A. Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams for ingestion and Amazon Rekognition for facial recognition processing B. Set up tape gateway appliance and process videos directly from tape gateway using Lambda and Rekognition C. Set up file gateway appliance, use MAM to send files to gateway, process with Lambda and Rekognition from S3 D. Use AWS Snowball to migrate files to S3, install open-source facial recognition on EC2 instance ✅ C. File Gateway with Lambda and Rekognition processing 🎯 Why correct: File Gateway provides seamless integration with existing MAM system while automatically backing files to S3. Rekognition can directly process files from S3 with minimal architectural changes. ⚠️ A. Kinesis Video Streams Requires significant changes to MAM solution to stream files into Kinesis. Designed for real-time streaming, not processing pre-existing archived files from tape library. ⚠️ B. Tape Gateway processing Cannot process videos directly from tape gateway in real-time since it's backed by Glacier storage. Files must be retrieved from archive before processing, adding latency. ⚠️ D. Snowball + open-source tools Requires significant management overhead to maintain open-source facial recognition on EC2. Less accurate than managed Rekognition service and requires custom development.

Imagenes - un modelo de vision pierde accuracy por iluminacion inconsistente y baja calidad de las camaras. Se busca la mejora mas rapida re-creando el dataset de entrenamiento. Que transform de Data Wrangler usar? A. Blur transform para difuminar las imagenes del dataset de entrenamiento B. Grayscale transform para quitar el color y dejar las imagenes en escala de grises C. Enhance image contrast con la opcion Gamma contrast para corregir la iluminacion D. Resize transform para llevar las imagenes a una resolucion mas alta

Which statement about Amazon Rekognition face collections is correct? A. Face collections automatically sync across all AWS regions B. You must create a face collection in a specific region before using IndexFaces operation C. Face collections can only store faces from images, not videos D. Face collections are automatically created when you first use SearchFacesByImage ✅ B. You must create a face collection in a specific region before using IndexFaces operation 🎯 Workflow: First use CreateCollection to create a face collection in your chosen region, then use IndexFaces to detect and store facial features. Collections are region-specific and must be explicitly created. You can then search using SearchFacesByImage , StartFaceSearch (videos), or CreateStreamProcessor (streaming).

category: AIP – Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications
stem: A company is deploying a fraud detection model using Amazon SageMaker AI and Amazon Comprehend in production. The model is designed to analyze transaction data, while Comprehend is used to extract key entities from transaction descriptions. The company wants to monitor the model’s performance over time, especially as fraud patterns evolve, and automatically re-train the model with the newly collected data to improve its accuracy. The company also needs to ensure that this process does not disrupt the production system. Which of the following should be implemented with the LEAST operational overhead?
correct_text: Enable SageMaker Model Monitor with Data Capture on the deployed endpoint to collect input/output data, and use this data for automated model retraining.

Usar SageMaker Model Monitor, habilitar Data Capture en el endpoint y usar esos datos para reentrenar D. Usar SageMaker Model Registry para recolectar datos nuevos y usarlos en el reentrenamiento

Usar EventBridge Scheduler para sondear la Lambda y analizar su salida en busca de drift B. Configurar un job de Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor que compare datos en vivo contra baseline y constraints del entrenamiento C. Which AWS service best addresses this requirement? A. Amazon Rekognition B. Amazon Textract C. Amazon Comprehend D. Amazon Kendra ✅ B. Amazon Textract 🎯 Key trigger: "Extract structured data from scanned documents" maps directly to Textract's AnalyzeExpense API, which is specifically designed for invoice and receipt processing to extract vendor names, amounts, and line items. ⚠️ A. Rekognition - General computer vision, not optimized for structured document data extraction ⚠️ C. Comprehend - Natural language processing for sentiment/entity analysis, not document structure extraction ⚠️ D. Kendra - Enterprise search service, not document data extraction

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A financial services company uses Amazon SageMaker Studio notebooks for data exploration and SageMaker Autopilot to train ML models on customer data stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The dataset contains sensitive financial information, and compliance policies require that all data traffic remain within the AWS private network. During an audit, the security team discovers that SageMaker Studio is accessing S3 over the public internet. The AI developer must reconfigure the environment to ensure that all data transfers between SageMaker and S3 occur securely within AWS’s internal network while maintaining full functionality for Studio notebooks and Autopilot jobs. Which configuration should the developer implement to meet this requirement?
correct_text: Configure SageMaker Studio notebooks to run within a VPC and create a VPC Gateway Endpoint for S3 to ensure all traffic between SageMaker and S3 stays within the AWS private network.

category: AIP – Testing, Validation, and Troubleshooting
stem: An AI developer is tasked with building a generative AI system to summarize patient medical records for physicians. The system uses Amazon SageMaker AI to fine-tune a large language model (LLM) on sensitive clinical notes stored in Amazon S3. Amazon Comprehend Medical is used to extract key medical entities from clinical notes, enriching the dataset for training. After generating summaries, the developer must ensure outputs are clinically relevant, accurate, and compliant with regulatory standards. Due to the high stakes of medical decision-making, a robust process is required to enable healthcare professionals to review and correct AI-generated summaries before full deployment. The solution must scale to handle large volumes of records and integrate seamlessly with existing SageMaker pipelines for smooth retraining and deployment. Which approach will best satisfy these requirements?
correct_text: Use SageMaker Ground Truth Plus to create a human-in-the-loop workflow for expert validation and correction of model-generated summaries. Integrate this workflow with the existing SageMaker pipeline for seamless model retraining and deployment.

Requirements: Cloud contact center with automatic speech recognition , natural language understanding , intent recognition , and ability to maintain conversation context across multiple interactions. Which AWS service meets ALL these requirements for conversational AI? A. Amazon Transcribe B. Amazon Polly C. Amazon Lex D. Amazon Comprehend ✅ C. Amazon Lex 🎯 Why: Amazon Lex provides ASR (speech-to-text), NLU (natural language understanding), intent recognition with slot filling, and context management across conversations. It's specifically designed for building conversational interfaces and chatbots. ⚠️ A. Transcribe: Only provides speech-to-text conversion, lacks NLU, intent recognition, and context management. ⚠️ B. Polly: Only provides text-to-speech synthesis, cannot understand or process incoming speech or text. ⚠️ D. Comprehend: Analyzes text for insights but lacks ASR capabilities and real-time conversational context management.

category: AIP – Implementation and Integration
stem: A data science team at a retail company wants to predict customer churn based on various historical transactional data. The dataset contains 10,000 records, each with 1,500 attributes, such as demographic information, purchasing patterns, and customer service interactions. The team is looking for an automated way to build a model using Amazon SageMaker AI, which can predict whether a customer will churn while also identifying the most relevant features contributing to the prediction. To deepen insights, the team uses Amazon Comprehend to analyze sentiment and key phrases in customer interactions. Which of the following solutions will best fulfill these requirements while minimizing manual effort?
correct_text: Leverage SageMaker Autopilot to automatically train a classification model for forecasting customer churn. Then, utilize insights from SageMaker Clarify to determine which features most significantly influence the predictions.

Hay que quitar duplicados con ML y minima intervencion manual. Que servicio es el mas efectivo? A. Amazon SageMaker Autopilot B. AWS Glue FindMatches transform C. Amazon QuickSight ML Insights D. AWS Glue DataBrew

Amazon Rekognition (analisis de imagenes y video) C. Amazon Comprehend (NLP: sentimiento, entidades, frases clave) D. Amazon SageMaker AI (construir, entrenar y desplegar modelos propios)

A. Transformar al recuperar datos con S3 Object Lambda, integrar SageMaker para el ML y armar dashboards en Amazon CloudWatch B. Ejecutar consultas SQL con AWS Glue DataBrew y conectar los datos a Amazon ElasticSearch para dashboards en tiempo real C. A financial services company stores customer transaction data in S3 and needs to automatically identify credit card numbers, social security numbers, and other PII across terabytes of documents. Which service best addresses this requirement? A. AWS Config B. Amazon Macie C. AWS CloudTrail D. Amazon Inspector ✅ B. Amazon Macie 🎯 Perfect match: Macie uses machine learning to automatically scan S3 buckets and identify sensitive data patterns like credit card numbers, SSNs, and PII. It provides continuous monitoring, classification, and alerting for data security compliance. Config tracks resource configuration changes, CloudTrail logs API calls, and Inspector assesses application security - none perform content-based PII discovery.

A. El transform de normalizacion min-max aplicado sobre las columnas categoricas del dataset B. SageMaker Neo para compilar y optimizar el modelo ya entrenado antes de la inferencia C. El transform de quantile binning para discretizar las columnas numericas en intervalos iguales D. Los encoders integrados (por ejemplo one-hot / ordinal) para transformar datos categoricos en numericos

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A developer is working on an advanced machine learning project using Amazon SageMaker AI. The project involves training a deep learning model using large datasets stored in Amazon S3. Additionally, the developer needs to store model artifacts, logs, and evaluation results back to a different S3 bucket upon completion of the training job. To ensure security and proper access control, the developer must grant the SageMaker notebook instance appropriate permissions to read from and write to the specific S3 buckets. Which approach should be used to securely enable this access?
correct_text: Allow the SageMaker notebook instance to perform s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, and s3:ListBucket operations by attaching a policy to its associated IAM role that grants access to the designated S3 buckets.
