category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A financial services company is developing a machine learning (ML) model in Amazon SageMaker AI to detect real-time fraudulent transactions. The company plans to integrate this model with Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for continuous transaction data ingestion and Amazon DynamoDB for storing transaction metadata. The model must be trained on an extensive historical dataset stored in Amazon S3. The company must ensure that all data is encrypted in transit and at rest, and that access to sensitive data and model results is strictly controlled. AWS Encryption SDK is being considered for additional client-side encryption of sensitive data before uploading it to S3. There’s also a need to track model performance over time to ensure it remains effective and predictions align with business rules. Which solution will secure the ML workflow, control access, and allow for continuous monitoring of model performance?
correct_text: Use SageMaker AI to train the model with data from S3, enable S3 server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) for data at rest, configure IAM roles to control access to the model and data, and use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor model performance metrics and logging.

candidates.full_text: A company receives sensor data every millisecond from manufacturing equipment and needs to detect anomalies in real-time to prevent equipment failure. Which AWS service is best suited for this use case? A. Amazon SQS with Lambda processing B. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Analytics C. Amazon S3 with scheduled EMR jobs D. Amazon RDS with stored procedures ✅ B. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Analytics 🎯 Trigger keywords: "every millisecond" + "real-time anomaly detection" = streaming analytics requirement. Kinesis Data Streams ingests high-frequency sensor data, while Kinesis Analytics runs SQL queries for real-time anomaly detection using sliding windows and statistical functions. SQS + Lambda: SQS has throughput limits and Lambda has execution time limits - not suitable for continuous millisecond data streams requiring real-time processing.

A financial services company stores customer transaction data in S3 and needs to automatically identify credit card numbers, social security numbers, and other PII across terabytes of documents. Which service best addresses this requirement? A. AWS Config B. Amazon Macie C. AWS CloudTrail D. Amazon Inspector ✅ B. Amazon Macie 🎯 Perfect match: Macie uses machine learning to automatically scan S3 buckets and identify sensitive data patterns like credit card numbers, SSNs, and PII. It provides continuous monitoring, classification, and alerting for data security compliance. Config tracks resource configuration changes, CloudTrail logs API calls, and Inspector assesses application security - none perform content-based PII discovery.

A company needs to store and replicate financial transaction data across multiple AWS regions with ACID properties , sub-millisecond latency , and automatic failover capabilities. Which service best addresses this requirement? A. Amazon RDS with Cross-Region Read Replicas B. DynamoDB Global Tables C. Amazon S3 with Cross-Region Replication D. Amazon ElastiCache Global Datastore ✅ B. DynamoDB Global Tables 🎯 Key insight: DynamoDB Global Tables provides single-digit millisecond latency, automatic multi-region replication, and built-in ACID properties for transactions. It's specifically designed for financial and transactional workloads requiring global distribution. ⚠️ A. RDS Cross-Region Replicas only provide read replicas, not multi-master writes, and have higher latency than DynamoDB. ⚠️ C. S3 is object storage, not suitable for transactional data requiring ACID properties. ⚠️ D. ElastiCache is for caching, not persistent transactional storage with ACID guarantees.

Amazon Bedrock, la empresa YA tiene el dataset etiquetado en JSONL y el rol IAM listo. Dado esto, cual es el primer paso RESTANTE del proceso de personalizacion (fine-tuning) del modelo? A. Ajustar hiperparametros y crear el fine-tuning job B. Comprar provisioned throughput para el modelo ajustado C. Analizar resultados revisando metricas de entrenamiento o validacion D. Preparar un dataset etiquetado en formato JSONL con ejemplos de fraude

A company needs to ensure log file integrity for compliance audits, prevent accidental deletion of critical audit logs, and maintain confidentiality of sensitive API call data stored in S3. Which combination of S3 security features best meets ALL requirements? A. S3 Object Lock with Legal Hold and bucket-level public read blocking B. MFA Delete, IAM roles with least privilege, and S3 bucket policies C. S3 versioning with Cross-Region Replication and KMS encryption D. S3 Access Control Lists (ACLs) and CloudWatch monitoring ✅ B. MFA Delete, IAM roles with least privilege, and S3 bucket policies 🎯 MFA Delete prevents accidental deletion (integrity), IAM roles provide fine-grained access control (confidentiality), and bucket policies add an additional layer of access restrictions. Object Lock is overkill for this scenario and doesn't address confidentiality. Versioning alone doesn't prevent deletion. ACLs are less secure than IAM-based controls.

category: AIP – Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications
stem: An AI developer is building a fraud detection model using Amazon SageMaker Autopilot to generate and evaluate candidate models automatically. To further refine model performance, the developer integrates automatic model tuning (AMT) in Amazon SageMaker AI to optimize several hyperparameters related to model learning rate, batch size, and regularization strength. The team also applies canary testing to validate top-performing candidate models before full deployment. During multiple tuning jobs, the developer notices that some training jobs run unnecessarily long when the model’s validation accuracy stops improving early in the process. The tuning configuration must be adjusted appropriately to optimize resource usage and reduce overall tuning time, allowing SageMaker AI to decide automatically when to stop poorly performing training jobs. Which configuration step should be taken to address this requirement?
correct_text: Enable early stopping by setting the TrainingJobEarlyStoppingType parameter to the AUTO value in the tuning job configuration.

Which tuning strategy should be employed to enhance optimization efficiency and expedite hyperparameter search?

stem: A research division is continuously retraining a Generative Forecasting Foundation model pipeline built on Amazon SageMaker AI, where base embedding creation happens in SageMaker Processing, feature encoding is performed inside the SageMaker Feature Store ingestion pipeline, and final supervised regression is trained in SageMaker Training. Last quarter, this same regression model was tuned using SageMaker AI automatic model tuning (AMT), and the results produced a known stable set of high-performing hyperparameters that were saved. A new quarter dataset is now being ingested, and it is larger, has a different distribution, and must be used for the next model update. However, the engineering pillar requires that a new hyperparameter tuning job cannot start from zero because the compute budget is limited. There is also a requirement that if the model’s validation loss does not improve anymore, the tuning must automatically stop without manual intervention. Which hyperparameter tuning job configuration should be used?
correct_text: Start a warm start hyperparameter tuning job using the TRANSFER_LEARNING warm start type to import the previously saved tuning job results. Enable AMT Early Stopping to automatically terminate exploration as soon as validation loss stops improving when training with the new quarterly dataset.

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A social media platform is developing an ML model to moderate user-generated content. The platform stores large volumes of textual and document data in Amazon S3. It uses Amazon Textract to extract text from uploaded PDFs or images, and Amazon SageMaker AI to train custom language models that classify comments based on sentiment, context, and topic relevance. The moderation team aims to enhance safety by detecting toxic or harmful language in real-time, including hate speech, harassment, and explicit threats. The solution must integrate seamlessly with the existing SageMaker AI inference pipeline, handle high throughput, and provide confidence scores for each classification, allowing content flagged as toxic to be reviewed or blocked automatically. Which of the solutions provides a managed solution for detecting toxicity in text to support this ML pipeline with safety classifiers?
correct_text: Utilize Amazon Comprehend toxicity detection to identify abusive or harmful language in text.

candidates.full_text: Servicios AWS de ML - que servicio es el mas adecuado para analizar feedback de clientes (sentimiento e insights de texto) ? A. Amazon Lex (interfaces conversacionales y chatbots) B. Amazon Rekognition (analisis de imagenes y video) C. Amazon Comprehend (NLP: sentimiento, entidades, frases clave) D. Amazon SageMaker AI (construir, entrenar y desplegar modelos propios)

When should you choose Amazon Textract over Amazon Rekognition for document processing? A. When you need to detect faces and objects in images B. When you need to extract structured text, forms, and tables from documents C. When you need to identify inappropriate content in images D. When you need to recognize celebrities in photos ✅ B. When you need to extract structured text, forms, and tables from documents Amazon Textract • Specialized for document text extraction • Handles forms, tables, and structured data • OCR replacement for scanned documents • Invoice and receipt processing • ID document analysis Amazon Rekognition • General computer vision service • Face detection and recognition • Object and scene detection • Content moderation • Celebrity recognition • Basic text detection in images 🎯 Decision rule: Choose Textract when you need to extract and understand structured document content. Choose Rekognition when you need general image analysis, face recognition, or content moderation.

Requirements: Cloud contact center with automatic speech recognition , natural language understanding , intent recognition , and ability to maintain conversation context across multiple interactions. Which AWS service meets ALL these requirements for conversational AI? A. Amazon Transcribe B. Amazon Polly C. Amazon Lex D. Amazon Comprehend ✅ C. Amazon Lex 🎯 Why: Amazon Lex provides ASR (speech-to-text), NLU (natural language understanding), intent recognition with slot filling, and context management across conversations. It's specifically designed for building conversational interfaces and chatbots. ⚠️ A. Transcribe: Only provides speech-to-text conversion, lacks NLU, intent recognition, and context management. ⚠️ B. Polly: Only provides text-to-speech synthesis, cannot understand or process incoming speech or text. ⚠️ D. Comprehend: Analyzes text for insights but lacks ASR capabilities and real-time conversational context management.

A media company has hybrid architecture with Direct Connect. 50TB+ digital videos on on-premises tape library used by Media Asset Management (MAM) system. Want automated catalog with facial recognition, minimal disruption, least management overhead . Eventually migrate to AWS. Which solution uses LEAST ongoing management overhead with MINIMAL disruption? A. Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to set up video ingestion stream with Amazon Rekognition, build face collection. Stream media files from MAM into Kinesis, configure Rekognition to process streamed files. Launch stream consumer for metadata, push to MAM, store files in S3. B. Set up tape gateway on-premises connected to AWS Storage Gateway. Configure MAM to fetch files from archive, push to tape gateway for Glacier storage. Use Rekognition with Lambda function to process video from tape gateway in real-time. C. Integrate local data center file system to AWS Storage Gateway via file gateway on-premises. MAM extracts files and sends to file gateway. Build Rekognition collection, use Lambda to process files from S3 bucket backing file gateway. D. Request AWS Snowball to migrate files to S3. Provision large EC2 instance, install open-source facial recognition tools like OpenFace/OpenCV. Process files for metadata, push to MAM, copy files to another S3 bucket. ✅ C File Gateway with Rekognition 🎯 File Gateway provides seamless integration with existing MAM system while enabling real-time processing with Rekognition. Tape Gateway can't process files in real-time from Glacier. ⚠️ A Kinesis Video Streams — Requires major MAM changes, designed for streaming not archived files ⚠️ B Tape Gateway — Can't process files real-time from Glacier archive ⚠️ D Snowball + EC2 — High management overhead with open-source tools vs managed Rekognition 📖 Full Explanation Amazon Rekognition can store information about detected faces in server-side containers known as collections. You can use the facial information that's stored in a collection to search for known faces in images, stored videos, and streaming videos. Amazon Rekognition supports the IndexFaces operation. You can use this operation to detect faces in an image and persist information about facial features that are detected in a collection. This is an example of a storage-based API operation because the service persists information on the server. To store facial information, you must first create (CreateCollection) a face collection in one of the AWS Regions in your account. You specify this face collection when you call the IndexFaces operation. After you create a face collection and store facial feature information for all faces, you can search the collection for face matches. To search for faces in an image, call SearchFacesByImage. To search for faces in a stored video, call StartFaceSearch. To search for faces in a streaming video, call CreateStreamProcessor. AWS Storage Gateway offers file-based, volume-based, and tape-based storage solutions. With a tape gateway, you can cost-effectively and durably archive backup data in GLACIER or DEEP_ARCHIVE. A tape gateway provides a virtual tape infrastructure that scales seamlessly with your business needs and eliminates the operational burden of provisioning, scaling, and maintaining a physical tape infrastructure. You can run AWS Storage Gateway either on-premises as a VM appliance, as a hardware appliance, or in AWS as an Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance. You deploy your gateway on an EC2 instance to provision iSCSI storage volumes in AWS. You can use gateways hosted on EC2 instances for disaster recovery, data mirroring, and providing storage for applications hosted on Amazon EC2. Hence, the correct answer is: Integrate the file system of your local data center to AWS Storage Gateway by setting up a file gateway appliance on-premises. Utilize the MAM solution to extract the media files from the current data store and send them into the file gateway. Build a collection using Amazon Rekognition by populating a catalog of faces from the processed media files. Use an AWS Lambda function to invoke Amazon Rekognition Javascript SDK to have it fetch the media file from the S3 bucket which is backing the file gateway, retrieve the needed metadata, and finally, persist the information into the MAM solution. The option that says: Request for an AWS Snowball Storage Optimized device to migrate all of the media files from the on-premises library into Amazon S3. Provision a large EC2 instance and allow it to access the S3 bucket. Install an open-source facial recognition tool on the instance like OpenFace or OpenCV. Process the media files to retrieve the metadata and push this information into the MAM solution. Lastly, copy the media files to another S3 bucket is incorrect. This entails a lot of ongoing management overhead instead of just using Amazon Rekognition. Moreover, it is more suitable to use the AWS Storage Gateway service rather than an EBS Volume. The option that says: Set up a tape gateway appliance on-premises and connect it to your AWS Storage Gateway. Configure the MAM solution to fetch the media files from the current archive and push them into the tape gateway to be stored in Amazon Glacier. Using Amazon Rekognition, build a collection from the catalog of faces. Utilize a Lambda function which invokes the Rekognition Javascript SDK to have Amazon Rekognition process the video directly from the tape gateway in real-time, retrieve the required metadata, and push the metadata into the MAM solution is incorrect. Although this solution uses the right combination of AWS Storage Gateway and Amazon Rekognition, take note that you can't directly fetch the media files from your tape gateway in real time since this is backed up using Glacier. Although the on-premises data center is using a tape gateway, you can still set up a solution to use a file gateway in order to properly process the videos using Amazon Rekognition. Keep in mind that the tape gateway in the AWS Storage Gateway service is primarily used as an archive solution. The option that says: Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to set up a video ingestion stream and with Amazon Rekognition, build a collection of faces. Stream the media files from the MAM solution into Kinesis Video Streams and configure the Amazon Rekognition to process the streamed files. Launch a stream consumer to retrieve the required metadata, and push the metadata into the MAM solution. Finally, configure the stream to store the files in an S3 bucket is incorrect. This approach requires significant changes to the existing MAM solution to stream media files directly into Kinesis Video Streams, potentially causing more disruption to the current workflow. Additionally, Kinesis Video Streams is designed for real-time video streaming and processing, which may not be the most efficient approach for processing pre-existing media files stored in a tape library. Lastly, setting up and managing Kinesis Video Streams, configuring Amazon Rekognition integration, implementing a stream consumer, and storing files in S3 introduces additional complexity and management overhead compared to the File Gateway approach.

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: An enterprise is currently leveraging Amazon SageMaker Feature Store for cross-model reusable feature lineage and SageMaker Clarify for model bias monitoring pre-deployment. A new model is now planned to be deployed using a SageMaker AI endpoint. The enterprise security team mandates that all inference traffic must remain inside private subnets, so the SageMaker AI endpoint must use a VPC configuration with no public internet route. Expected request payload sizes are consistently 6 MB to 11 MB, and model inference execution time during operational peak can take 18–22 minutes per request. The finance engineering team also requires that costs must remain minimal while still supporting request/response style inference. Which solution is the most suitable approach to satisfy this requirement?
correct_text: Deploy a SageMaker asynchronous endpoint inside private subnets and include VPC configuration parameters during endpoint creation.

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A global enterprise is building an internal generative AI environment that performs text insights and embedding generation by using Amazon Titan models running on Amazon Bedrock. Multiple engineering divisions intend to integrate these capabilities into various business applications. The organization manages all cloud accounts through AWS Organizations, with distinct organizational units (OUs) representing each department. Executive leadership requires an access framework that enforces the principle of least privilege and restricts interaction with selected foundation models (FMs). The access approach must follow strict role-based access control (RBAC) standards and must integrate seamlessly with the centralized identity provider (IdP) to maintain unified governance across the enterprise environment. Only department-approved development teams must be authorized to invoke specific models, and every model interaction must be recorded for auditing and compliance evaluations. Which action ensures the requirements are met in the most secure manner?
correct_text: Enable SAML federation to AWS IAM Identity Center from the corporate IdP. Build permissions sets for each OU to authorize only designated Bedrock model invocations. Attach an SCP to prevent model usage outside the approved set.

candidates.full_text: An IT consulting company uses AWS Organizations with multiple accounts grouped into OUs. Security team discovered an unauthorized third-party account was added to the organization with high-level access privileges . No damage occurred yet, but they need to implement monitoring for organizational changes . Which actions should be taken to set up proper monitoring? (Select TWO.) A. Create a trail in Amazon CloudTrail to capture all API calls to AWS Organizations. Use Amazon EventBridge and SNS to raise events when administrator-specified actions occur. B. Monitor all changes using Systems Manager and use Amazon EventBridge to notify of any new activity. C. Use AWS Config to monitor compliance of AWS Organizations. Set up SNS Topic or Amazon EventBridge for change alerts. D. Configure AWS Control Tower to manage child accounts. Use Amazon Inspector to analyze breaches and notify via SNS. ✅ A and C. CloudTrail + EventBridge/SNS and AWS Config aggregation 🎯 Why correct: CloudTrail captures all Organizations API calls (including unauthorized account additions) while EventBridge can trigger on specific organizational events. AWS Config's multi-account aggregation enables centralized compliance monitoring across the entire organization. ⚠️ B. Systems Manager monitoring Systems Manager is designed for EC2 instances, on-premises servers, and AWS resource configuration management - not for monitoring AWS Organizations structural changes like account additions or OU modifications. ⚠️ D. Control Tower + Inspector While Control Tower can manage accounts, Amazon Inspector is a vulnerability assessment service for workloads and applications, not an organizational event monitoring tool for detecting unauthorized account additions.

An IT consultancy uses AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts across regional offices. A new account was added to an OU and uses an Amazon ECS Cluster with an attached service-linked role . The solutions architect created a custom SCP to deny certain ECS actions for regulatory purposes, but after applying the policy, the account could still perform the restricted actions. Which of the following is the most likely reason for this problem? A. The default SCP grants all permissions attached to every root, OU, and account. To apply stricter permissions, this policy is required to be modified. B. There is an SCP attached to a higher-level OU that permits the actions of the service-linked role. This permission would therefore be inherited by the current OU, and override the SCP placed by the administrator. C. SCPs do not affect any service-linked role. Service-linked roles enable other AWS services to integrate with AWS Organizations and can't be restricted by SCPs. D. The ECS service is being run outside the jurisdiction of the organization. SCPs affect only the principals that are managed by accounts that are part of the organization. ✅ C. SCPs do not affect any service-linked role 🎯 Why correct: Service-linked roles are special IAM roles that enable AWS services to integrate with Organizations and cannot be restricted by SCPs. This is a fundamental limitation of SCPs - they don't affect service-linked roles regardless of how the SCP is configured. ⚠️ A. Default SCP modification This is incorrect because the scenario already states a custom deny SCP was created. The FullAWSAccess default SCP allows all actions, but explicit deny policies override any allow policies, so modifying the default wouldn't solve this issue with service-linked roles. ⚠️ B. Higher-level OU permissions This misunderstands SCP inheritance. Even if a higher-level OU has an allow policy, a deny SCP at the current level would still block actions for regular IAM users and roles. The issue isn't about inheritance but about service-linked roles being exempt from SCP restrictions entirely. ⚠️ D. ECS outside organization This is technically incorrect because the service-linked role was created within the organization by the root account. The ECS service itself isn't "outside" the organization's jurisdiction - the issue is that service-linked roles have special exemptions from SCP restrictions.

An IT consulting company uses AWS Organizations with multiple accounts grouped into OUs. Security team discovered an unauthorized third-party AWS account was added to the organization with high-level access privileges. No detrimental actions occurred yet. Which actions should the solutions architect take to set up monitoring for changes to AWS accounts ? (Select TWO.) A. Create a trail in Amazon CloudTrail to capture all API calls to your AWS Organizations, including calls from the AWS Organizations console and from code calls to the AWS Organizations APIs. Use Amazon EventBridge and SNS to raise events when administrator-specified actions occur in an organization and send a notification to you. B. Monitor all changes to your organization using Systems Manager and use Amazon EventBridge to notify you of any new activity to your account. C. Use AWS Config to monitor the compliance of your AWS Organizations. Set up an SNS Topic or Amazon EventBridge that will send alerts to you for any changes. D. Configure AWS Control Tower to manage and monitor all child accounts under the organization. Use Amazon Inspector to analyze any possible breach and notify the administrators using AWS SNS. E. Set up a CloudWatch Dashboard to monitor any changes to your organizations and create an SNS topic that would send you a notification. ✅ A & C: CloudTrail + EventBridge/SNS for API calls, AWS Config for compliance monitoring 🎯 CloudTrail captures Organizations API calls, Config aggregates compliance data across accounts - both can trigger EventBridge/SNS for real-time alerts. ⚠️ B: Systems Manager manages EC2/servers, not Organizations structure ⚠️ D: Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, not account changes ⚠️ E: CloudWatch Dashboard visualizes metrics, doesn't monitor Organizations configuration 📖 Full Explanation AWS Organizations can work with CloudWatch Events to raise events when administrator-specified actions occur in an organization. For example, because of the sensitivity of such actions, most administrators would want to be warned every time someone creates a new account in the organization or when an administrator of a member account attempts to leave the organization. You can configure CloudWatch Events rules that look for these actions and then send the generated events to administrator-defined targets. Targets can be an Amazon SNS topic that emails or text messages its subscribers. Combining this with Amazon CloudTrail, you can set an event to trigger whenever a matching API call is received. Multi-account, multi-region data aggregation in AWS Config enables you to aggregate AWS Config data from multiple accounts and regions into a single account. Multi-account, multi-region data aggregation is useful for central IT administrators to monitor compliance for multiple AWS accounts in the enterprise. An aggregator is a new resource type in AWS Config that collects AWS Config data from multiple source accounts and regions.

Requirements: Cloud contact center with automatic speech recognition , natural language understanding , intent recognition , and ability to maintain conversation context across multiple interactions. Which AWS service meets ALL these requirements for conversational AI? A. Amazon Transcribe B. Amazon Polly C. Amazon Lex D. Amazon Comprehend ✅ C. Amazon Lex 🎯 Why: Amazon Lex provides ASR (speech-to-text), NLU (natural language understanding), intent recognition with slot filling, and context management across conversations. It's specifically designed for building conversational interfaces and chatbots. ⚠️ A. Transcribe: Only provides speech-to-text conversion, lacks NLU, intent recognition, and context management. ⚠️ B. Polly: Only provides text-to-speech synthesis, cannot understand or process incoming speech or text. ⚠️ D. Comprehend: Analyzes text for insights but lacks ASR capabilities and real-time conversational context management.

A company has multiple AWS accounts for different departments (finance, HR, engineering). Each account is managed by Systems Administrators with root access. Requirement: centrally manage policies across multiple AWS accounts to allow/deny specific AWS services for individual accounts or groups of accounts. Which is the most suitable solution with the LEAST complexity? A. Connect all departments by setting up cross-account access to each of the AWS accounts of the company. Create and attach IAM policies to your resources based on their respective departments to control access. B. Use AWS Organizations and Service Control Policies to control the list of AWS services that can be used by each member account. C. Set up AWS Organizations and Organizational Units (OU) to connect all AWS accounts of each department. Create a custom IAM Policy to allow or deny the use of certain AWS services for each account. D. Provide access to externally authenticated users via Identity Federation. Set up an IAM role to specify permissions for users from each department whose identity is federated from your organization or a third-party identity provider. ✅ B. Use AWS Organizations and Service Control Policies 🎯 SCPs centrally control AWS service access across multiple accounts and can restrict even root users, unlike IAM policies which only work within individual accounts. ⚠️ A. Cross-account access — Too complex for multiple accounts, more suited for 2-account scenarios ⚠️ C. Custom IAM Policy — IAM policies can't restrict services across accounts, need SCPs not IAM ⚠️ D. Identity Federation — Focuses on authentication, not service-level policy management across accounts 📖 Full Explanation AWS Organizations offers policy-based management for multiple AWS accounts. With Organizations, you can create groups of accounts, automate account creation, and apply and manage policies for those groups. Organizations enables you to centrally manage policies across multiple accounts, without requiring custom scripts and manual processes. It allows you to create Service Control Policies (SCPs) that centrally control AWS service use across multiple AWS accounts. Remember that AWS Organizations does not replace associating IAM policies with users, groups, and roles within an AWS account. Hence, you still need to set up appropriate IAM policies for your root and member accounts. IAM policies let you allow or deny access to AWS services (such as Amazon S3), individual AWS resources (such as a specific S3 bucket), or individual API actions (such as s3:CreateBucket). An IAM policy can be applied only to IAM users, groups, or roles, and it can never restrict the root identity of the AWS account. By contrast, AWS Organizations lets you use service control policies (SCPs) to allow or deny access to particular AWS services for individual AWS accounts, or for groups of accounts within an organizational unit (OU). The specified actions from an attached SCP affect all IAM users, groups, and roles for an account, including the root account identity.

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A global e-commerce company is preparing to train a generative AI model to generate realistic customer reviews for its products. The company collects vast amounts of user-generated content, including reviews, but some of this data contains personally identifiable information (PII). To ensure compliance with privacy regulations, the data scientist must redact any sensitive information while retaining the overall structure and integrity of the content for training the model. The solution must also scale to handle large datasets and automate the process efficiently, allowing for continuous model training without manual intervention. The company utilizes Amazon SageMaker AI for model training and Amazon Comprehend to analyze product reviews. To ensure accurate and compliant data for training the generative AI model, a solution is needed that removes PII while preserving the content’s relevance and structure. The solution must also ensure that no PII is used during model training. Which of the following solutions is the most efficient and scalable option to meet these requirements?
correct_text: Apply Comprehend DetectPiiEntities API to automatically identify and redact PII from the dataset, and store the cleansed data in an Amazon S3 bucket. SageMaker AI can then access the S3 bucket for training the generative AI model.

category: AIP – Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
stem: A multinational digital payments provider is designing a real-time fraud detection platform using Amazon SageMaker AI for training and hosting machine learning models, and Amazon Comprehend for analyzing unstructured transaction descriptions. The AI development team has consolidated years of historical transaction data from multiple regions into a single data lake. Each record in this dataset contains the following fields: client_identifier (string) account_category (integer) payment_value (float) account_duration (integer) operation_status (string) with possible values “legitimate” or “suspicious” Before deploying the model to production, the AI developer must prepare the data to ensure compatibility with SageMaker AI built-in algorithms and maintain a valid label structure for classification. Which preprocessing step should the AI developer perform before training the model in SageMaker AI?
correct_text: Exclude the client_identifier field and encode operation_status into numeric labels, then proceed with launching the model training phase in SageMaker AI.

category: AIP – Testing, Validation, and Troubleshooting
stem: A generative AI developer manages a production generative model endpoint in Amazon SageMaker AI, with Model Monitor and Amazon SageMaker Clarify enabled. The developer recently deployed a newly retrained model to replace an older version, and Model Monitor has been configured to track data quality and distribution drift. SageMaker Clarify continues to provide explainability and bias metrics for the same endpoint. The team also monitors for response drift to detect any unexpected shifts in model output patterns following the retraining. Despite the model being updated and serving new inference traffic based on a more current dataset, the monitoring job continues to show violations. The developer has confirmed that the new dataset is statistically representative of the current traffic, but the violations still persist. Which corrective action should the developer take to resolve the persistent violations in Model Monitor?
correct_text: Perform a baseline job on the new training data and configure Model Monitor to reference the new baseline statistics.

category: AIP – Implementation and Integration
stem: A global broadcasting enterprise, TD Studios, operates an intelligent content-management platform built on Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The platform uses SageMaker to coordinate large-scale data preparation and model-training workflows, enabling automated feature extraction and experimentation across thousands of multimedia assets. At the same time, Bedrock AgentCore serves as the orchestration layer that connects multiple AWS AI services, allowing agents to invoke specialized models and enrich content with generative summaries and metadata for semantic search. The enterprise recently expanded its media repository with several petabytes of newly acquired, unlabeled images, videos, podcasts, and written transcripts stored in Amazon S3. The Research and Curation division, composed primarily of content analysts with limited machine learning expertise, must now enable automatic tagging and indexing of this data to support entity-based search and cross-referencing. The enterprise wants to extend its existing Bedrock AgentCore workflow to handle this new data without performing any model training, manual labeling, or infrastructure provisioning. The solution must deliver accurate tagging across multiple modalities and achieve rapid implementation suitable for a non-specialized research team. Which solution provides the fastest and most effective approach to automatically index and categorize the multimedia assets?
correct_text: Leverage Amazon Comprehend, Amazon Transcribe, and Amazon Rekognition to categorize and tag multimedia content automatically

candidates.full_text: Requirements: Global content delivery , cache static images , handle millions of requests , reduce origin server load , improve mobile app performance worldwide Which service meets ALL requirements for distributing static content? A. Amazon S3 with Transfer Acceleration B. Amazon CloudFront CDN C. Application Load Balancer with multiple regions D. Amazon ElastiCache with Redis clusters ✅ B. Amazon CloudFront CDN 🎯 Why CloudFront wins: Global edge locations (✓), intelligent caching (✓), handles millions of requests (✓), reduces origin load by serving from cache (✓), optimized for mobile with compression and HTTP/2 (✓). Only service meeting ALL requirements. ⚠️ A. S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads but doesn't cache content or reduce origin load for downloads. ⚠️ C. ALB multi-region provides load balancing but no content caching or global edge presence. ⚠️ D. ElastiCache Redis requires application-level integration and doesn't provide global distribution.

A media company requires: global content delivery for images, serverless web hosting with auto-scaling, advanced search capabilities across text content, and 99.99% availability . Which combination of services meets ALL requirements? A. S3 + EC2 Auto Scaling + RDS + Route 53 B. S3 + CloudFront + Elastic Beanstalk + OpenSearch Service C. EFS + Application Load Balancer + Lambda + DynamoDB D. S3 + CloudFront + API Gateway + ElastiCache ✅ B. S3 + CloudFront + Elastic Beanstalk + OpenSearch Service 🎯 Requirements mapping: • Global delivery: CloudFront CDN • Serverless hosting: Elastic Beanstalk with auto-scaling • Advanced search: OpenSearch Service • 99.99% availability: Multi-AZ deployment across all services • Durable storage: S3's 11 9's durability ⚠️ A. EC2 Auto Scaling isn't serverless, RDS doesn't provide search capabilities ⚠️ C. Missing global CDN and advanced search functionality ⚠️ D. ElastiCache is for caching, not search; API Gateway alone doesn't provide web hosting

A tech startup is launching a global mobile marketplace using AWS Amplify . Backend APIs will be deployed to multiple AWS regions to process sales and financial transactions in the region closest to users. Transactions made in one region must be automatically replicated to other regions. Expected to have millions of users across North America, South America, Europe, and Asia. Which is the most scalable, cost-effective, and highly available architecture? A. Create a Global DynamoDB table with replica tables across several AWS regions. Store transactions to a DynamoDB replica table in each local region. B. Use AWS Control Tower and Amazon Connect to launch and centrally manage multiple DynamoDB tables in various AWS Regions. C. Store transactions to a DynamoDB table in each local region. Set up AWS Lambda function to read recent writes and replay data to DynamoDB tables in all other regions. D. Create Amazon S3 buckets in all required regions. Store transactions in local S3 bucket and replicate using S3 Cross-Region Replication. ✅ A. Create a Global DynamoDB table with replica tables across several AWS regions 🎯 Why correct: DynamoDB Global Tables provides fully managed, multi-region, multi-master database with automatic replication. It eliminates the complexity of manual replication and conflict resolution while providing fast local read/write performance for global applications. ⚠️ B. AWS Control Tower and Amazon Connect AWS Control Tower is for multi-account governance and Amazon Connect is a contact center service. Neither service can set up Global DynamoDB tables or handle database replication across regions. ⚠️ C. Lambda function for replication Using Lambda to manually replicate millions of transactions across multiple regions is not scalable. This approach would require significant compute capacity, custom conflict resolution logic, and complex error handling that Global Tables handles automatically. ⚠️ D. S3 Cross-Region Replication Amazon S3 is designed for object storage, not transactional workloads. While S3 Cross-Region Replication works for objects, it's not suitable for real-time transactional data that requires ACID properties and low-latency access.

A tech startup is launching a global mobile marketplace using AWS Amplify. Backend APIs will be deployed to multiple AWS regions for low latency . The system must ensure transactions made in one region are automatically replicated to other regions . Expected to have millions of users across North America, South America, Europe, and Asia. Which is the most scalable, cost-effective, and highly available architecture? A. Create a Global DynamoDB table with replica tables across several AWS regions. Store transactions to DynamoDB replica table in same region. Changes automatically replicated across all tables. B. Use AWS Control Tower and Amazon Connect to launch and manage multiple DynamoDB tables in various regions. Store transactions to DynamoDB replica table in same region. C. Store transactions to DynamoDB table in each region. Set up Lambda function to read recent writes and replay data to DynamoDB tables in all other regions. D. Create S3 buckets in all regions. Store transactions in local S3 bucket. Replicate using S3 Cross-Region Replication. ✅ A. Global DynamoDB table with automatic cross-region replication 🎯 DynamoDB Global Tables provide fully managed, multi-region, multi-master replication with automatic conflict resolution for massive scale. ⚠️ B. Control Tower/Connect — These services don't create Global Tables ⚠️ C. Lambda replication — Not scalable for millions of transactions ⚠️ D. S3 Cross-Region Replication — S3 isn't designed for transactional workloads 📖 Full Explanation Global Tables builds upon DynamoDB's global footprint to provide you with a fully managed, multi-region, and multi-master database that provides fast, local, read and write performance for massively scaled, global applications. Global Tables replicates your Amazon DynamoDB tables automatically across your choice of AWS regions. Global Tables eliminates the difficult work of replicating data between regions and resolving update conflicts, enabling you to focus on your application's business logic. In addition, Global Tables enables your applications to stay highly available even in the unlikely event of isolation or degradation of an entire region. Using Lambda for replication is not scalable for millions of customers. Control Tower and Connect don't create Global Tables. S3 Cross-Region Replication isn't suitable for real-time transactional data.

A BPO startup needs a scalable call center system on AWS that can handle thousands of inbound calls with self-service capabilities (password changes, balance checks) without agents. Requirements: automatic speech recognition (ASR) , natural language understanding , and integration with business applications . Which solution should the Solutions Architect implement? A. AWS Ground Station + Amazon Alexa for Business + Lambda B. Amazon Connect + Amazon Comprehend + Lambda C. Amazon Connect + Amazon Lex + Lambda D. AWS Elemental MediaConnect + Amazon Polly + Lambda ✅ C. Amazon Connect + Amazon Lex + Lambda 🎯 Amazon Connect provides cloud contact center functionality, while Amazon Lex offers both ASR and NLU for conversational chatbots that can handle self-service tasks. ⚠️ A. Ground Station is for satellite communications, not contact centers ⚠️ B. Comprehend analyzes text but lacks ASR/NLU for voice interactions ⚠️ D. MediaConnect is for live video transport, Polly only does text-to-speech 📖 Full Explanation Amazon Connect provides a seamless omnichannel experience through a single unified contact center for voice and chat. Amazon Lex is a service for building conversational interfaces into any application using voice and text. Amazon Lex provides the advanced deep learning functionalities of automatic speech recognition (ASR) for converting speech to text and natural language understanding (NLU) to recognize the intent of the text, enabling you to build applications with highly engaging user experiences and lifelike conversational interactions. By using an Amazon Lex chatbot in your Amazon Connect call center, callers can perform tasks such as changing a password, requesting a balance on an account, or scheduling an appointment without needing to speak to an agent. Amazon Lex uses AWS Lambda functions to query your business applications, provide information back to callers, and make updates as requested.

category: AIP – Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
stem: A startup is training an autonomous vehicle detection model using Amazon SageMaker AI with labeled image data stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The dataset is annotated using SageMaker Ground Truth, which contains thousands of high-resolution images. During model training, the team observes slow startup times and low GPU utilization because the training job downloads data sequentially from S3. The company wants to keep the S3 bucket as the primary data repository, but improve data access performance and training throughput for SageMaker AI without duplicating data or significantly altering the training script. The team reviewed AWS Cost Explorer and observed rising GPU costs due to idle compute time. Which solution should be implemented to optimize SageMaker AI training performance while maintaining the existing S3-based workflow?
correct_text: Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system and connect it to the existing S3 bucket. Update the SageMaker AI training job to access the dataset directly from the FSx mount.

category: AIP – Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications
stem: A global insurance technology company built a claims automation system using Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint and Amazon Rekognition. Rekognition analyzes uploaded vehicle images to detect the severity and type of damage, while SageMaker uses this information, along with other structured features such as vehicle age, mileage, and estimated repair cost, to predict claim approval probability and estimated settlement time. During initial training, the model assigned greater weight to the damage severity score and repair cost estimate as the most influential features for decision-making. However, recent observations suggest that the deployed model on the SageMaker AI endpoint might now be emphasizing vehicle age more heavily than damage severity, resulting in inconsistent predictions and potential policy compliance issues. The data science team must implement a monitoring solution that detects when the feature weight or attribution importance of input variables shifts in production and automatically triggers alerts for investigation. Which of the following should be implemented?
correct_text: Use ModelExplainabilityMonitor class with a SHAP-based baseline to detect feature attribution drift in production. Regularly compare how the model assigns importance to input features against the baseline, and configure Amazon CloudWatch to alert stakeholders when attribution values drift beyond acceptable thresholds.

Configurar un job de Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor que compare datos en vivo contra baseline y constraints del entrenamiento C. category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A financial services company needs to build a predictive model to identify fraudulent transactions using historical customer data, which includes sensitive information such as credit card numbers. The company plans to use Amazon SageMaker AI to train the model and Amazon Comprehend to extract features from the text-based data in the dataset. The company must ensure that all customer data is securely encrypted and that any personally identifiable information (PII), including credit card numbers, is redacted before the data is used for model training. Which solution will meet this requirement?
correct_text: Encrypt customer data with AWS KMS in Amazon S3 before importing it into SageMaker AI. Use AWS Glue to redact credit card numbers from the customer data before using it for model training.

candidates.full_text: A financial services company stores customer transaction data in S3 and needs to automatically identify credit card numbers, social security numbers, and other PII across terabytes of documents. Which service best addresses this requirement? A. AWS Config B. Amazon Macie C. AWS CloudTrail D. Amazon Inspector ✅ B. Amazon Macie 🎯 Perfect match: Macie uses machine learning to automatically scan S3 buckets and identify sensitive data patterns like credit card numbers, SSNs, and PII. It provides continuous monitoring, classification, and alerting for data security compliance. Config tracks resource configuration changes, CloudTrail logs API calls, and Inspector assesses application security - none perform content-based PII discovery.

A telecommunications company is hosting a WordPress website on Amazon ECS Cluster using Fargate launch type . Database credentials must be provided via environment variables , kept secure and not viewable on the cluster. Requirements: dedicated storage with lifecycle management and key rotation . Which solution provides secure credential storage with the least effort? A. Store credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, encrypt with KMS, create IAM role for ECS task execution, reference secrets in container definition B. Migrate to Amazon EKS, use Kubernetes Secrets objects, reference with secretKeyRef, configure automatic rotation C. Store credentials in ECS task definition file encrypted with KMS, store in private S3 bucket with HTTPS, use --cli-input-json parameter D. Store credentials in AWS Secrets Manager, encrypt with KMS, create IAM role for ECS task execution, reference secrets in container definition ✅ D. AWS Secrets Manager with KMS encryption 🎯 Why correct: Secrets Manager provides dedicated secrets storage with built-in lifecycle management and automatic key rotation capabilities, exactly matching the requirement for "dedicated storage with lifecycle management and key rotation." ⚠️ A. Systems Manager Parameter Store While Parameter Store can store encrypted credentials and works with ECS secrets, it doesn't provide dedicated storage with lifecycle management and key rotation features like Secrets Manager does. ⚠️ B. Migrate to Amazon EKS This requires significant migration effort from ECS to EKS, violating the "least effort" requirement. Additionally, Kubernetes doesn't natively support automatic rotation of secrets. ⚠️ C. Store in ECS task definition in S3 Storing sensitive credentials in S3, even encrypted, is not a recommended practice and requires extensive manual configuration. This approach has more overhead than using purpose-built secrets management services.

A company requires: encrypted credential storage , cost optimization , hierarchical organization , and no automatic rotation for their application configuration. Which service meets ALL requirements? A. AWS Secrets Manager B. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store C. Amazon S3 with KMS encryption D. AWS Config ✅ B. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 🎯 Why: Parameter Store provides KMS encryption (security), free tier pricing (cost optimization), hierarchical parameter organization (/app/database/password), and no built-in rotation (meeting the no automatic rotation requirement). It's purpose-built for configuration management. ⚠️ A. Secrets Manager - More expensive and includes automatic rotation features not needed ⚠️ C. S3 with KMS - Lacks hierarchical organization and configuration management features ⚠️ D. AWS Config - Configuration compliance service, not credential storage

category: AIP – Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
stem: A data science team is developing a computer vision model using Amazon SageMaker AI to classify product images that customers upload. In addition to image features, the team plans to integrate Amazon Comprehend to analyze customer feedback text associated with each image. During data preparation, the team noticed that one of the numerical features representing image brightness seemed to affect the model’s convergence rate during training. The lead ML engineer wants to explore how the brightness values are distributed in the dataset before deciding to apply normalization. The engineer uses SageMaker Data Wrangler for feature engineering and data preprocessing. Which actions should the engineer take to best understand the range and distribution of the brightness feature values before transformation?
correct_text: The engineer should use the SageMaker Data Wrangler histogram visualization to inspect the range of values for the brightness feature and identify any outliers.

candidates.full_text: Se quiere elegir el tipo de instancia mas costo-efectivo para desplegar un modelo en tiempo real cumpliendo latencia y throughput. Que feature de SageMaker lo determina? A. Amazon SageMaker Multi-Model Endpoints B. Amazon SageMaker Automatic Scaling C. Amazon SageMaker Inference Recommender D. Amazon SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning

When should you choose Amazon Textract over Amazon Rekognition for document processing? A. When you need to detect faces and objects in images B. When you need to extract structured text, forms, and tables from documents C. When you need to identify inappropriate content in images D. When you need to recognize celebrities in photos ✅ B. When you need to extract structured text, forms, and tables from documents Amazon Textract • Specialized for document text extraction • Handles forms, tables, and structured data • OCR replacement for scanned documents • Invoice and receipt processing • ID document analysis Amazon Rekognition • General computer vision service • Face detection and recognition • Object and scene detection • Content moderation • Celebrity recognition • Basic text detection in images 🎯 Decision rule: Choose Textract when you need to extract and understand structured document content. Choose Rekognition when you need general image analysis, face recognition, or content moderation.

Servicios AWS de ML - que servicio es el mas adecuado para analizar feedback de clientes (sentimiento e insights de texto) ? A. Amazon Lex (interfaces conversacionales y chatbots) B. Amazon Rekognition (analisis de imagenes y video) C. Amazon Comprehend (NLP: sentimiento, entidades, frases clave) D. Amazon SageMaker AI (construir, entrenar y desplegar modelos propios)
