category: AIP – Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
stem: A global wildlife research organization is developing an automated monitoring system to track endangered species using camera trap images collected from remote conservation areas. Image data is uploaded to Amazon S3, and Amazon Rekognition performs an initial scan to identify frames that likely contain animals instead of empty backgrounds. Filtered images are then passed to a custom deep learning model, built using an Amazon SageMaker AI algorithm, to detect and count individual animals within each image accurately. The project requires distinguishing between multiple species, such as elephants, tigers, and rhinos, while also determining the exact position of each animal in the frame. Bounding boxes must be generated for every detected animal to analyze population density and movement patterns over time. The final model will be integrated into an automated analytics pipeline that updates a conservation dashboard used by field researchers and policy teams. Which modeling approach should be implemented in SageMaker AI to both identify animal species and locate each one precisely within the images?
correct_text: Use a SageMaker AI object detection algorithm to accurately identify and localize multiple animal species by generating bounding boxes and associated class labels.

candidates.full_text: SageMaker - se necesita identificar un articulo en una imagen y dar su ubicacion (bounding box) en estanterias en tiempo real. Que algoritmo integrado conviene? A. Random Cut Forest (detecta anomalias en series de tiempo y datos tabulares) B. Object Detection - MXNet (detecta y localiza objetos con bounding boxes) C. K-Means Clustering (agrupa vectores numericos por similitud, no supervisado) D. Object2Vec (aprende embeddings vectoriales de objetos discretos para similitud)

A company receives sensor data every millisecond from manufacturing equipment and needs to detect anomalies in real-time to prevent equipment failure. Which AWS service is best suited for this use case? A. Amazon SQS with Lambda processing B. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Analytics C. Amazon S3 with scheduled EMR jobs D. Amazon RDS with stored procedures ✅ B. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Analytics 🎯 Trigger keywords: "every millisecond" + "real-time anomaly detection" = streaming analytics requirement. Kinesis Data Streams ingests high-frequency sensor data, while Kinesis Analytics runs SQL queries for real-time anomaly detection using sliding windows and statistical functions. SQS + Lambda: SQS has throughput limits and Lambda has execution time limits - not suitable for continuous millisecond data streams requiring real-time processing.

A startup develops IoT pet collars that collect biometric data every second and send it via POST API to a web portal. The portal must provide real-time analytics , trends, and health reports to global pet owners with high durability, availability, and scalability . Which architecture best meets these requirements? A. Use Kinesis Data Streams → Kinesis analytics → S3 → Redshift with backups B. SQS queue → Kinesis analytics → RDS MySQL C. S3 bucket → Data Pipeline daily analysis → Redshift OLAP D. EMR instance → Kinesis analytics → DynamoDB ✅ A. Kinesis Data Streams → analytics → S3 → Redshift 🎯 Kinesis Data Streams handles high-frequency streaming data and enables real-time analytics, perfect for second-by-second biometric collection. ⚠️ B. SQS — Not designed for high-frequency streaming data analytics ⚠️ C. Data Pipeline — Daily batch processing, not real-time ⚠️ D. EMR — Not appropriate for data collection, only processing 📖 Full Explanation Amazon Kinesis Data Streams enable you to build custom applications that process or analyze streaming data for specialized needs. Kinesis Data Streams can continuously capture and store terabytes of data per hour from hundreds of thousands of sources. With the Kinesis Client Library (KCL), you can build applications for real-time dashboards, generate alerts, and emit data to other AWS services like S3, Redshift, EMR, and Lambda. The correct architecture uses Kinesis for streaming collection, real-time analytics, S3 for storage, and Redshift for complex analytics with automated backups. Option B is wrong because SQS queues aren't appropriate for high-frequency streaming data. Option C is wrong because Data Pipeline runs daily batch jobs, not real-time processing. Option D is wrong because EMR instances aren't designed for data collection, only processing.

A data analytics startup will develop a FIFA World Cup statistics system for global access. The system must track game statistics, allow voting for best players/coaches, and handle 10-30 million queries on game days . Requirements: durable storage , high availability , high scalability , and cost-effective . Which is the most cost-effective solution meeting these requirements? A. Multi-AZ RDS + ElastiCache reports + default expire parameters B. Multi-AZ RDS + DynamoDB storage + daily table deletion C. Multi-AZ RDS with Read Replicas + query replicas + daily cleanup D. Multi-AZ RDS with Read Replicas + S3 batch reports + CloudFront CDN with daily TTL ✅ D. Multi-AZ RDS with Read Replicas + S3 batch reports + CloudFront CDN with daily TTL 🎯 Combines scalable database (RDS Multi-AZ + Read Replicas), durable storage (S3), and global distribution (CloudFront) for cost-effective handling of millions of global queries. ⚠️ A. ElastiCache — lacks durable storage and CDN for global distribution ⚠️ B. RDS + DynamoDB — maintaining both databases is not cost-effective ⚠️ C. Read Replicas only — missing durable storage and CDN components 📖 Full Explanation In this scenario, you are required to have the following: A durable storage for the generated reports. A database that is highly available and can scale to handle millions of queries. A Content Delivery Network that can distribute the report files to users all over the world. Amazon S3 is object storage built to store and retrieve any amount of data from anywhere. It's a simple storage service that offers industry leading durability, availability, performance, security, and virtually unlimited scalability at very low costs. Amazon RDS provides high availability and failover support for DB instances using Multi-AZ deployments. In a Multi-AZ deployment, Amazon RDS automatically provisions and maintains a synchronous standby replica in a different Availability Zone. The primary DB instance is synchronously replicated across Availability Zones to a standby replica to provide data redundancy, eliminate I/O freezes, and minimize latency spikes during system backups. Amazon RDS uses the MariaDB, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle, and PostgreSQL DB engines' built-in replication functionality to create a special type of DB instance called a read replica from a source DB instance. The source DB instance becomes the primary DB instance. Updates made to the primary DB instance are asynchronously copied to the read replica. Amazon CloudFront is a web service that speeds up distribution of your static and dynamic web content, such as .html, .css, .js, and image files, to your users. CloudFront delivers your content through a worldwide network of data centers called edge locations. When a user requests content that you're serving with CloudFront, the request is routed to the edge location that provides the lowest latency (time delay), so that content is delivered with the best possible performance. Hence, the following option is the best solution that satisfies all of these requirements: 1. Generate the FIFA reports from MySQL database in Multi-AZ RDS deployments configuration with Read Replicas. 2. Set up a batch job that puts reports in an S3 bucket. 3. Launch a CloudFront distribution to cache the content with a TTL set to expire objects daily. In the above, S3 provides durable storage; Multi-AZ RDS with Read Replicas provide a scalable and highly available database and CloudFront provides the CDN.

A company runs a sports web portal with resources in multiple AWS regions (EC2, RDS, IAM). The IT Security Compliance Officer requires a reliable and durable logging solution to track changes to all resources across all regions. The solution must ensure integrity and confidentiality of log data. Which solution would be the best option? A. Create a new trail in AWS CloudTrail with the global services option selected, and create one new Amazon S3 bucket to store the logs. Create IAM roles, S3 bucket policies, and enable Multi Factor Authentication (MFA) Delete on the S3 bucket storing your logs. B. Create three new CloudTrail trails, each with its own S3 bucket to store the logs: one for the AWS Management console, one for AWS SDKs, and one for command line tools. Then create IAM roles and S3 bucket policies for the S3 buckets storing your logs. C. Create a new trail in AWS CloudTrail with the global services option selected, and assign it an existing S3 bucket to store the logs. Create S3 ACLs and enable Multi Factor Authentication (MFA) delete on the S3 bucket storing your logs. D. Create a new trail in CloudTrail and assign it a new S3 bucket to store the logs. Configure AWS SNS to send delivery notifications to your management system. Secure the S3 bucket that stores your logs using IAM roles and S3 bucket policies. ✅ A. CloudTrail with global services + new S3 bucket + IAM roles + MFA Delete 🎯 Global services flag captures IAM events across regions, new S3 bucket ensures confidentiality, MFA Delete provides integrity protection. ⚠️ B — Creates unnecessary multiple trails without global services flag ⚠️ C — Uses existing S3 bucket (compromises confidentiality) and S3 ACLs instead of IAM roles ⚠️ D — Missing global services flag, won't capture IAM events 📖 Full Explanation For most services, events are recorded in the region where the action occurred to its respective AWS CloudTrail. For global services such as AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), AWS STS, Amazon CloudFront, and Route 53, events are delivered to any trail that includes global services (IncludeGlobalServiceEvents flag). AWS CloudTrail service should be your top choice for the scenarios where the application is tracking the changes made by any AWS service, resource, or API. AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) is integrated with AWS CloudTrail, a service that logs AWS events made by or on behalf of your AWS account. CloudTrail logs authenticate AWS API calls and also AWS sign-in events, and collects this event information in files that are delivered to Amazon S3 buckets. Therefore, the correct answer is: Create a new trail in AWS CloudTrail with the global services option selected, and create one new Amazon S3 bucket to store the logs. Create IAM roles, S3 bucket policies, and enable Multi Factor Authentication (MFA) Delete on the S3 bucket storing your logs. It uses AWS CloudTrail with (includeGlobalServiceEvents flag) Global Option enabled, a single new S3 bucket and IAM Roles so that it has the confidentiality, and MFA on Delete on S3 bucket so that it maintains the data integrity. The option that says: Create a new trail in AWS CloudTrail with the global services option selected, and assign it an existing S3 bucket to store the logs. Create S3 ACLs and enable Multi Factor Authentication (MFA) delete on the S3 bucket storing your logs is incorrect. As an existing S3 bucket is used, it may already be accessed by the user, hence not maintaining the confidentiality, and it is not using IAM roles. The option that says: Create three new CloudTrail trails, each with its own S3 bucket to store the logs: one for the AWS Management console, one for AWS SDKs, and one for command line tools. Then create IAM roles and S3 bucket policies for the S3 buckets storing your logs is incorrect. Although it uses AWS CloudTrail, the Global Option is not enabled, and three S3 buckets are not needed. The option that says: Create a new trail in CloudTrail and assign it a new S3 bucket to store the logs. Configure AWS SNS to send delivery notifications to your management system. Secure the S3 bucket that stores your logs using IAM roles and S3 bucket policies is incorrect. Although it uses AWS CloudTrail, the Global Option is not enabled.

category: AIP – Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications
stem: A digital media company operates a web platform where customers upload high-resolution product and marketing images that require automated text generation for accessibility and search optimization. Each uploaded image can reach up to 60 MB in size, and the platform experiences unpredictable spikes in traffic during global promotional campaigns. All uploaded images are securely stored in an Amazon S3 bucket, which acts as the central repository for incoming media files. The company uses Amazon Rekognition to analyze images, detecting objects, scenes, and other visual features that form the foundation of metadata. The extracted information is passed to Amazon Bedrock, which uses a foundation model to generate detailed natural language captions describing the image content accurately and contextually. The ML workflow automatically starts processing when new images are uploaded to the S3 bucket. The GenAI developer must design a solution that scales automatically to handle fluctuating workloads, maintains high availability during traffic spikes, and operates with minimal infrastructure management overhead. Which solution fulfills these requirements with minimal infrastructure management and operational effort?
correct_text: Deploy an Amazon SageMaker Asynchronous Inference endpoint with a scaling policy that automatically adjusts capacity and processes inference requests for each image in the S3 bucket.

candidates.full_text: A media company has hybrid architecture with Direct Connect. 50TB+ digital videos on on-premises tape library used by Media Asset Management (MAM) system. Want automated catalog with facial recognition, minimal disruption, least management overhead . Eventually migrate to AWS. Which solution uses LEAST ongoing management overhead with MINIMAL disruption? A. Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to set up video ingestion stream with Amazon Rekognition, build face collection. Stream media files from MAM into Kinesis, configure Rekognition to process streamed files. Launch stream consumer for metadata, push to MAM, store files in S3. B. Set up tape gateway on-premises connected to AWS Storage Gateway. Configure MAM to fetch files from archive, push to tape gateway for Glacier storage. Use Rekognition with Lambda function to process video from tape gateway in real-time. C. Integrate local data center file system to AWS Storage Gateway via file gateway on-premises. MAM extracts files and sends to file gateway. Build Rekognition collection, use Lambda to process files from S3 bucket backing file gateway. D. Request AWS Snowball to migrate files to S3. Provision large EC2 instance, install open-source facial recognition tools like OpenFace/OpenCV. Process files for metadata, push to MAM, copy files to another S3 bucket. ✅ C File Gateway with Rekognition 🎯 File Gateway provides seamless integration with existing MAM system while enabling real-time processing with Rekognition. Tape Gateway can't process files in real-time from Glacier. ⚠️ A Kinesis Video Streams — Requires major MAM changes, designed for streaming not archived files ⚠️ B Tape Gateway — Can't process files real-time from Glacier archive ⚠️ D Snowball + EC2 — High management overhead with open-source tools vs managed Rekognition 📖 Full Explanation Amazon Rekognition can store information about detected faces in server-side containers known as collections. You can use the facial information that's stored in a collection to search for known faces in images, stored videos, and streaming videos. Amazon Rekognition supports the IndexFaces operation. You can use this operation to detect faces in an image and persist information about facial features that are detected in a collection. This is an example of a storage-based API operation because the service persists information on the server. To store facial information, you must first create (CreateCollection) a face collection in one of the AWS Regions in your account. You specify this face collection when you call the IndexFaces operation. After you create a face collection and store facial feature information for all faces, you can search the collection for face matches. To search for faces in an image, call SearchFacesByImage. To search for faces in a stored video, call StartFaceSearch. To search for faces in a streaming video, call CreateStreamProcessor. AWS Storage Gateway offers file-based, volume-based, and tape-based storage solutions. With a tape gateway, you can cost-effectively and durably archive backup data in GLACIER or DEEP_ARCHIVE. A tape gateway provides a virtual tape infrastructure that scales seamlessly with your business needs and eliminates the operational burden of provisioning, scaling, and maintaining a physical tape infrastructure. You can run AWS Storage Gateway either on-premises as a VM appliance, as a hardware appliance, or in AWS as an Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance. You deploy your gateway on an EC2 instance to provision iSCSI storage volumes in AWS. You can use gateways hosted on EC2 instances for disaster recovery, data mirroring, and providing storage for applications hosted on Amazon EC2. Hence, the correct answer is: Integrate the file system of your local data center to AWS Storage Gateway by setting up a file gateway appliance on-premises. Utilize the MAM solution to extract the media files from the current data store and send them into the file gateway. Build a collection using Amazon Rekognition by populating a catalog of faces from the processed media files. Use an AWS Lambda function to invoke Amazon Rekognition Javascript SDK to have it fetch the media file from the S3 bucket which is backing the file gateway, retrieve the needed metadata, and finally, persist the information into the MAM solution. The option that says: Request for an AWS Snowball Storage Optimized device to migrate all of the media files from the on-premises library into Amazon S3. Provision a large EC2 instance and allow it to access the S3 bucket. Install an open-source facial recognition tool on the instance like OpenFace or OpenCV. Process the media files to retrieve the metadata and push this information into the MAM solution. Lastly, copy the media files to another S3 bucket is incorrect. This entails a lot of ongoing management overhead instead of just using Amazon Rekognition. Moreover, it is more suitable to use the AWS Storage Gateway service rather than an EBS Volume. The option that says: Set up a tape gateway appliance on-premises and connect it to your AWS Storage Gateway. Configure the MAM solution to fetch the media files from the current archive and push them into the tape gateway to be stored in Amazon Glacier. Using Amazon Rekognition, build a collection from the catalog of faces. Utilize a Lambda function which invokes the Rekognition Javascript SDK to have Amazon Rekognition process the video directly from the tape gateway in real-time, retrieve the required metadata, and push the metadata into the MAM solution is incorrect. Although this solution uses the right combination of AWS Storage Gateway and Amazon Rekognition, take note that you can't directly fetch the media files from your tape gateway in real time since this is backed up using Glacier. Although the on-premises data center is using a tape gateway, you can still set up a solution to use a file gateway in order to properly process the videos using Amazon Rekognition. Keep in mind that the tape gateway in the AWS Storage Gateway service is primarily used as an archive solution. The option that says: Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to set up a video ingestion stream and with Amazon Rekognition, build a collection of faces. Stream the media files from the MAM solution into Kinesis Video Streams and configure the Amazon Rekognition to process the streamed files. Launch a stream consumer to retrieve the required metadata, and push the metadata into the MAM solution. Finally, configure the stream to store the files in an S3 bucket is incorrect. This approach requires significant changes to the existing MAM solution to stream media files directly into Kinesis Video Streams, potentially causing more disruption to the current workflow. Additionally, Kinesis Video Streams is designed for real-time video streaming and processing, which may not be the most efficient approach for processing pre-existing media files stored in a tape library. Lastly, setting up and managing Kinesis Video Streams, configuring Amazon Rekognition integration, implementing a stream consumer, and storing files in S3 introduces additional complexity and management overhead compared to the File Gateway approach.

A media company with a hybrid architecture has 50+ TB of digital videos stored on on-premises tape library. They want to implement automated facial recognition catalog with minimal disruption to existing MAM system and least management overhead . Eventually migrate to AWS. Which solution provides the least ongoing management overhead with minimal disruption? A. Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams for ingestion and Amazon Rekognition for facial recognition processing B. Set up tape gateway appliance and process videos directly from tape gateway using Lambda and Rekognition C. Set up file gateway appliance, use MAM to send files to gateway, process with Lambda and Rekognition from S3 D. Use AWS Snowball to migrate files to S3, install open-source facial recognition on EC2 instance ✅ C. File Gateway with Lambda and Rekognition processing 🎯 Why correct: File Gateway provides seamless integration with existing MAM system while automatically backing files to S3. Rekognition can directly process files from S3 with minimal architectural changes. ⚠️ A. Kinesis Video Streams Requires significant changes to MAM solution to stream files into Kinesis. Designed for real-time streaming, not processing pre-existing archived files from tape library. ⚠️ B. Tape Gateway processing Cannot process videos directly from tape gateway in real-time since it's backed by Glacier storage. Files must be retrieved from archive before processing, adding latency. ⚠️ D. Snowball + open-source tools Requires significant management overhead to maintain open-source facial recognition on EC2. Less accurate than managed Rekognition service and requires custom development.

A print media company wants to migrate their on-premises web application to AWS. The app allows global users to search and retrieve newspaper pages stored as PNG images with OCR-converted text files . Their OCR license expires soon and they need a scalable, durable, highly available AWS architecture. Which is the best option to achieve this requirement? A. Store images in S3, use Amazon Kendra for search, lifecycle policy to Glacier after 3 months with Glacier Select for queries B. CloudFormation with EBS-backed EC2 instances, ALB, NGINX, open source search, EBS volumes with Data Lifecycle Manager C. S3 bucket with CloudFront distribution, Elastic Beanstalk multi-AZ environment, Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Textract for OCR D. S3 Intelligent-Tiering, migrate OCR software to Auto Scaling Spot instances with ALB, Amazon Rekognition for text recognition ✅ C. S3 bucket with CloudFront distribution, Elastic Beanstalk multi-AZ environment, Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Textract for OCR 🎯 Why correct: This solution replaces the expiring OCR license with managed AWS services (Textract), provides scalable storage (S3), high availability (multi-AZ Beanstalk), and robust search capabilities (OpenSearch Service). CloudFront ensures global content delivery performance. ⚠️ A. Amazon Kendra approach Kendra is an enterprise search service for existing content repositories, not designed for OCR text recognition from scanned documents. Moving frequently accessed images to Glacier would severely impact retrieval performance for a global web application. ⚠️ B. EBS-based solution EBS volumes are neither scalable nor durable compared to S3, requiring manual management and creating single points of failure. This approach lacks the cost-effectiveness and automated scaling of managed services. ⚠️ D. Rekognition with existing OCR This solution still relies on the expiring OCR software that needs replacement. Amazon Rekognition is optimized for general image recognition, while Textract is specifically designed for document text extraction.

A media company requires: global content delivery for images, serverless web hosting with auto-scaling, advanced search capabilities across text content, and 99.99% availability . Which combination of services meets ALL requirements? A. S3 + EC2 Auto Scaling + RDS + Route 53 B. S3 + CloudFront + Elastic Beanstalk + OpenSearch Service C. EFS + Application Load Balancer + Lambda + DynamoDB D. S3 + CloudFront + API Gateway + ElastiCache ✅ B. S3 + CloudFront + Elastic Beanstalk + OpenSearch Service 🎯 Requirements mapping: • Global delivery: CloudFront CDN • Serverless hosting: Elastic Beanstalk with auto-scaling • Advanced search: OpenSearch Service • 99.99% availability: Multi-AZ deployment across all services • Durable storage: S3's 11 9's durability ⚠️ A. EC2 Auto Scaling isn't serverless, RDS doesn't provide search capabilities ⚠️ C. Missing global CDN and advanced search functionality ⚠️ D. ElastiCache is for caching, not search; API Gateway alone doesn't provide web hosting

A graphics design startup stores high-resolution media files in multiple Amazon S3 buckets . After partnering with a media company, they share digital resources. The media company performs multiple object retrievals daily , significantly increasing the startup's data transfer costs . What should you do to help the startup lower their operational costs? A. Advise the media company to create their own S3 bucket and sync objects using aws s3 sync command B. Enable the Requester Pays feature in all of the startup's S3 buckets C. Create a new billing account for the media company using AWS Organizations with SCPs D. Provide cross-account access for the media company to access S3 bucket contents ✅ B. Enable the Requester Pays feature in all of the startup's S3 buckets 🎯 Why correct: With Requester Pays buckets, the requester (media company) pays for data transfer and request costs instead of the bucket owner (startup). The bucket owner only pays for storage costs, solving the cost problem directly. ⚠️ A. AWS S3 sync approach This would actually increase costs significantly because the startup would be charged for all data transfer during the sync process. Additionally, maintaining duplicate datasets creates ongoing synchronization complexity and storage costs. ⚠️ C. AWS Organizations with SCPs AWS Organizations provides consolidated billing, not separate billing accounts for each member. All charges still roll up to the master account, so this doesn't shift costs to the media company. ⚠️ D. Cross-account access only Cross-account access alone doesn't change billing responsibility. Unless Requester Pays is enabled, the bucket owner (startup) continues to pay for all data transfer and request costs regardless of who makes the requests.

category: AIP – Implementation and Integration
stem: A data science team is running an anti-financial crime workload using Amazon SageMaker Training and SageMaker Feature Store. The team stores transactional features inside the Feature Store offline store, and those features are periodically retrieved and consumed by SageMaker model training jobs inside a scheduled retraining pipeline. The binary classifier is used for real-time fraud detection involving regulated payment flows, but the team is consistently observing a very high count of false negatives, even though the overall model accuracy is greater than 96%. The core issue is the severe class imbalance condition, where fraud transactions represent less than one-half of one percent of the entire dataset, and historical fraud samples remain extremely limited. The goal is to increase the model’s ability to correctly detect fraudulent cases. The team wants to directly correct this imbalance problem before running the next retraining cycle. Which solution will increase the fraudulent case detection performance?
correct_text: Integrate a preprocessing step that applies the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) on the minority fraudulent transaction class only before the training run begins.

category: AIP – Implementation and Integration
stem: A financial services organization has built a custom machine learning (ML) model designed for real-time fraud detection. The model, which is hosted on the company’s on-premises infrastructure, is less than 5 GB in size and processes up to 50 concurrent requests simultaneously. The company is exploring AWS services to migrate its model to the cloud while minimizing infrastructure management. The development team is familiar with Amazon Rekognition for image-based analysis and Amazon Textract for document analysis, and is now looking for the best service to deploy the fraud detection model. Which of the following will meet the given requirements with the least operational overhead?
correct_text: Create a model configuration within Amazon SageMaker AI, then deploy the custom fraud detection model on a serverless SageMaker endpoint.

candidates.full_text: Hosting - un modelo de fraude near real-time y baja latencia pesa menos de 1 GB, recibe como maximo 10 peticiones concurrentes y hoy corre on-premises. Configurar el modelo como SageMaker AI Model y servirlo en un endpoint serverless de SageMaker AI B. Configurar el modelo como SageMaker AI Model y usar batch transform para inferencia C. Construir un contenedor del modelo y desplegarlo con Amazon ECS sobre AWS Fargate D. Importar el modelo a Amazon Comprehend Custom Classification y usar su API en tiempo real

A media company has hybrid architecture with Direct Connect. 50TB+ digital videos on on-premises tape library used by Media Asset Management (MAM) system. Want automated catalog with facial recognition, minimal disruption, least management overhead . Eventually migrate to AWS. Which solution uses LEAST ongoing management overhead with MINIMAL disruption? A. Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to set up video ingestion stream with Amazon Rekognition, build face collection. Stream media files from MAM into Kinesis, configure Rekognition to process streamed files. Launch stream consumer for metadata, push to MAM, store files in S3. B. Set up tape gateway on-premises connected to AWS Storage Gateway. Configure MAM to fetch files from archive, push to tape gateway for Glacier storage. Use Rekognition with Lambda function to process video from tape gateway in real-time. C. Integrate local data center file system to AWS Storage Gateway via file gateway on-premises. MAM extracts files and sends to file gateway. Build Rekognition collection, use Lambda to process files from S3 bucket backing file gateway. D. Request AWS Snowball to migrate files to S3. Provision large EC2 instance, install open-source facial recognition tools like OpenFace/OpenCV. Process files for metadata, push to MAM, copy files to another S3 bucket. ✅ C File Gateway with Rekognition 🎯 File Gateway provides seamless integration with existing MAM system while enabling real-time processing with Rekognition. Tape Gateway can't process files in real-time from Glacier. ⚠️ A Kinesis Video Streams — Requires major MAM changes, designed for streaming not archived files ⚠️ B Tape Gateway — Can't process files real-time from Glacier archive ⚠️ D Snowball + EC2 — High management overhead with open-source tools vs managed Rekognition 📖 Full Explanation Amazon Rekognition can store information about detected faces in server-side containers known as collections. You can use the facial information that's stored in a collection to search for known faces in images, stored videos, and streaming videos. Amazon Rekognition supports the IndexFaces operation. You can use this operation to detect faces in an image and persist information about facial features that are detected in a collection. This is an example of a storage-based API operation because the service persists information on the server. To store facial information, you must first create (CreateCollection) a face collection in one of the AWS Regions in your account. You specify this face collection when you call the IndexFaces operation. After you create a face collection and store facial feature information for all faces, you can search the collection for face matches. To search for faces in an image, call SearchFacesByImage. To search for faces in a stored video, call StartFaceSearch. To search for faces in a streaming video, call CreateStreamProcessor. AWS Storage Gateway offers file-based, volume-based, and tape-based storage solutions. With a tape gateway, you can cost-effectively and durably archive backup data in GLACIER or DEEP_ARCHIVE. A tape gateway provides a virtual tape infrastructure that scales seamlessly with your business needs and eliminates the operational burden of provisioning, scaling, and maintaining a physical tape infrastructure. You can run AWS Storage Gateway either on-premises as a VM appliance, as a hardware appliance, or in AWS as an Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance. You deploy your gateway on an EC2 instance to provision iSCSI storage volumes in AWS. You can use gateways hosted on EC2 instances for disaster recovery, data mirroring, and providing storage for applications hosted on Amazon EC2. Hence, the correct answer is: Integrate the file system of your local data center to AWS Storage Gateway by setting up a file gateway appliance on-premises. Utilize the MAM solution to extract the media files from the current data store and send them into the file gateway. Build a collection using Amazon Rekognition by populating a catalog of faces from the processed media files. Use an AWS Lambda function to invoke Amazon Rekognition Javascript SDK to have it fetch the media file from the S3 bucket which is backing the file gateway, retrieve the needed metadata, and finally, persist the information into the MAM solution. The option that says: Request for an AWS Snowball Storage Optimized device to migrate all of the media files from the on-premises library into Amazon S3. Provision a large EC2 instance and allow it to access the S3 bucket. Install an open-source facial recognition tool on the instance like OpenFace or OpenCV. Process the media files to retrieve the metadata and push this information into the MAM solution. Lastly, copy the media files to another S3 bucket is incorrect. This entails a lot of ongoing management overhead instead of just using Amazon Rekognition. Moreover, it is more suitable to use the AWS Storage Gateway service rather than an EBS Volume. The option that says: Set up a tape gateway appliance on-premises and connect it to your AWS Storage Gateway. Configure the MAM solution to fetch the media files from the current archive and push them into the tape gateway to be stored in Amazon Glacier. Using Amazon Rekognition, build a collection from the catalog of faces. Utilize a Lambda function which invokes the Rekognition Javascript SDK to have Amazon Rekognition process the video directly from the tape gateway in real-time, retrieve the required metadata, and push the metadata into the MAM solution is incorrect. Although this solution uses the right combination of AWS Storage Gateway and Amazon Rekognition, take note that you can't directly fetch the media files from your tape gateway in real time since this is backed up using Glacier. Although the on-premises data center is using a tape gateway, you can still set up a solution to use a file gateway in order to properly process the videos using Amazon Rekognition. Keep in mind that the tape gateway in the AWS Storage Gateway service is primarily used as an archive solution. The option that says: Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to set up a video ingestion stream and with Amazon Rekognition, build a collection of faces. Stream the media files from the MAM solution into Kinesis Video Streams and configure the Amazon Rekognition to process the streamed files. Launch a stream consumer to retrieve the required metadata, and push the metadata into the MAM solution. Finally, configure the stream to store the files in an S3 bucket is incorrect. This approach requires significant changes to the existing MAM solution to stream media files directly into Kinesis Video Streams, potentially causing more disruption to the current workflow. Additionally, Kinesis Video Streams is designed for real-time video streaming and processing, which may not be the most efficient approach for processing pre-existing media files stored in a tape library. Lastly, setting up and managing Kinesis Video Streams, configuring Amazon Rekognition integration, implementing a stream consumer, and storing files in S3 introduces additional complexity and management overhead compared to the File Gateway approach.

A media company with a hybrid architecture has 50+ TB of digital videos stored on on-premises tape library. They want to implement automated facial recognition catalog with minimal disruption to existing MAM system and least management overhead . Eventually migrate to AWS. Which solution provides the least ongoing management overhead with minimal disruption? A. Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams for ingestion and Amazon Rekognition for facial recognition processing B. Set up tape gateway appliance and process videos directly from tape gateway using Lambda and Rekognition C. Set up file gateway appliance, use MAM to send files to gateway, process with Lambda and Rekognition from S3 D. Use AWS Snowball to migrate files to S3, install open-source facial recognition on EC2 instance ✅ C. File Gateway with Lambda and Rekognition processing 🎯 Why correct: File Gateway provides seamless integration with existing MAM system while automatically backing files to S3. Rekognition can directly process files from S3 with minimal architectural changes. ⚠️ A. Kinesis Video Streams Requires significant changes to MAM solution to stream files into Kinesis. Designed for real-time streaming, not processing pre-existing archived files from tape library. ⚠️ B. Tape Gateway processing Cannot process videos directly from tape gateway in real-time since it's backed by Glacier storage. Files must be retrieved from archive before processing, adding latency. ⚠️ D. Snowball + open-source tools Requires significant management overhead to maintain open-source facial recognition on EC2. Less accurate than managed Rekognition service and requires custom development.

A company receives sensor data every millisecond from manufacturing equipment and needs to detect anomalies in real-time to prevent equipment failure. Which AWS service is best suited for this use case? A. Amazon SQS with Lambda processing B. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Analytics C. Amazon S3 with scheduled EMR jobs D. Amazon RDS with stored procedures ✅ B. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Analytics 🎯 Trigger keywords: "every millisecond" + "real-time anomaly detection" = streaming analytics requirement. Kinesis Data Streams ingests high-frequency sensor data, while Kinesis Analytics runs SQL queries for real-time anomaly detection using sliding windows and statistical functions. SQS + Lambda: SQS has throughput limits and Lambda has execution time limits - not suitable for continuous millisecond data streams requiring real-time processing.

The department of education is building a learning portal in AWS to supplement their on-premises network . They need a highly available cloud infrastructure with multiple Availability Zones . Requirements: aggregate logs , automate log analysis for errors , and immediately notify IT Operations when errors breach thresholds . Which solution BEST meets these requirements? A. Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus on-premises → AWS Lambda for metrics → CloudWatch Alarm B. Amazon Kinesis agent on-premises → CloudWatch Logs → metric filter → QuickSight monitoring C. CloudWatch agent on-premises → EventBridge → metric filter → Athena monitoring D. CloudWatch agent on-premises → CloudWatch Logs → metric filter → CloudWatch Alarm ✅ D. CloudWatch agent → CloudWatch Logs → metric filter → CloudWatch Alarm 🎯 Why correct: CloudWatch agent is the proper service for collecting on-premises logs and sending to CloudWatch Logs. Metric filters convert log data to numerical metrics, and CloudWatch Alarms provide immediate notifications when thresholds are breached. ⚠️ A. Prometheus + Lambda approach Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is designed for container metrics, not general log processing. Creating custom Lambda functions for log processing is unnecessary complexity when CloudWatch already provides this functionality natively. ⚠️ B. Kinesis agent approach Kinesis agent is for streaming data ingestion, not log collection from on-premises servers. QuickSight is a business intelligence tool, not designed for real-time alerting and monitoring compared to CloudWatch Alarms. ⚠️ C. EventBridge destination Logs should go to CloudWatch Logs, not EventBridge which is for event routing. Athena is for querying data, not real-time monitoring and alerting like CloudWatch Alarms.

stem: A team of AI engineers is developing a churn prediction model using Amazon SageMaker AI. The team imports customer interaction and billing data into SageMaker Data Wrangler for data preparation and feature engineering. During exploratory data analysis, the team discovered that only about 8% of customers in the dataset have churned, causing a significant class imbalance. The team plans to launch a SageMaker training job using an XGBoost model to predict churn. However, initial training results show that the model consistently predicts the majority “non-churn” class, leading to poor recall for churned customers. The data scientist must address the imbalance to improve model performance and ensure the training dataset adequately represents both classes. Which approach should the team take to resolve this issue before starting the SageMaker training job?
correct_text: Perform the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) in SageMaker Data Wrangler to rebalance the churn dataset before running the SageMaker training job.

category: AIP – Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
stem: A global market research firm stores thousands of recorded analyst briefings in Amazon S3. The data science division uses Amazon SageMaker AI JumpStart to experiment with pretrained NLP models for text classification and Amazon Polly to synthesize sample voice outputs for model validation. Before processing, the team uses AWS Glue Data Quality to validate and standardize incoming audio metadata and transcript outputs to ensure consistency across all recordings. The next project phase requires grouping all recorded discussions by the conversation themes, such as equity strategy, macroeconomic policy, and currency trends. The AI developer must choose an approach that automatically categorizes these recordings by topic, while minimizing custom development effort. Which solution will meet this requirement most efficiently?
correct_text: Configure Amazon Transcribe jobs to process all recordings into text, followed by an Amazon Comprehend topic detection job that identifies and clusters conversation topics.

candidates.full_text: Requirements: Cloud contact center with automatic speech recognition , natural language understanding , intent recognition , and ability to maintain conversation context across multiple interactions. Which AWS service meets ALL these requirements for conversational AI? A. Amazon Transcribe B. Amazon Polly C. Amazon Lex D. Amazon Comprehend ✅ C. Amazon Lex 🎯 Why: Amazon Lex provides ASR (speech-to-text), NLU (natural language understanding), intent recognition with slot filling, and context management across conversations. It's specifically designed for building conversational interfaces and chatbots. ⚠️ A. Transcribe: Only provides speech-to-text conversion, lacks NLU, intent recognition, and context management. ⚠️ B. Polly: Only provides text-to-speech synthesis, cannot understand or process incoming speech or text. ⚠️ D. Comprehend: Analyzes text for insights but lacks ASR capabilities and real-time conversational context management.

Servicios AWS de ML - que servicio es el mas adecuado para analizar feedback de clientes (sentimiento e insights de texto) ? A. Amazon Lex (interfaces conversacionales y chatbots) B. Amazon Rekognition (analisis de imagenes y video) C. Amazon Comprehend (NLP: sentimiento, entidades, frases clave) D. Amazon SageMaker AI (construir, entrenar y desplegar modelos propios)

A company wants to build an Interactive Voice Response (IVR) system where customers can speak naturally to check account balances and update personal information without speaking to agents. Which AWS service combination is specifically designed for this use case? A. Amazon Polly + Amazon Transcribe B. Amazon Connect + Amazon Lex C. Amazon Comprehend + Amazon Translate D. AWS Alexa for Business + Amazon Rekognition ✅ B. Amazon Connect + Amazon Lex 🎯 This is the exact use case Amazon Connect and Lex were designed for. Amazon Connect handles the contact center infrastructure, while Amazon Lex provides the conversational AI with built-in ASR and NLU to understand natural speech and execute self-service tasks. ⚠️ A. Polly + Transcribe: Polly only does text-to-speech, Transcribe only does speech-to-text. Neither provides intent understanding or dialogue management needed for IVR interactions. ⚠️ C. Comprehend + Translate: These are for text analysis and translation, not real-time voice interactions or contact center operations. ⚠️ D. Alexa for Business + Rekognition: Alexa for Business is for workplace productivity, Rekognition is for image analysis - neither addresses contact center or IVR requirements.

Amazon Transcribe para transcribir el audio, y Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases con Titan Embeddings G1 para crear embeddings y buscar semanticamente en una base vectorial C. Amazon Rekognition para analizar los audios, extraer metadatos automaticamente y guardarlos en Amazon S3 para su consulta posterior D. Amazon Transcribe para transcribir el audio, Amazon Comprehend para extraer frases clave, y guardar los resultados en Amazon DynamoDB para consultarlos por clave

An IT consulting company uses AWS Organizations with multiple accounts grouped into OUs. Security team discovered an unauthorized third-party account was added to the organization with high-level access privileges . No damage occurred yet, but they need to implement monitoring for organizational changes . Which actions should be taken to set up proper monitoring? (Select TWO.) A. Create a trail in Amazon CloudTrail to capture all API calls to AWS Organizations. Use Amazon EventBridge and SNS to raise events when administrator-specified actions occur. B. Monitor all changes using Systems Manager and use Amazon EventBridge to notify of any new activity. C. Use AWS Config to monitor compliance of AWS Organizations. Set up SNS Topic or Amazon EventBridge for change alerts. D. Configure AWS Control Tower to manage child accounts. Use Amazon Inspector to analyze breaches and notify via SNS. ✅ A and C. CloudTrail + EventBridge/SNS and AWS Config aggregation 🎯 Why correct: CloudTrail captures all Organizations API calls (including unauthorized account additions) while EventBridge can trigger on specific organizational events. AWS Config's multi-account aggregation enables centralized compliance monitoring across the entire organization. ⚠️ B. Systems Manager monitoring Systems Manager is designed for EC2 instances, on-premises servers, and AWS resource configuration management - not for monitoring AWS Organizations structural changes like account additions or OU modifications. ⚠️ D. Control Tower + Inspector While Control Tower can manage accounts, Amazon Inspector is a vulnerability assessment service for workloads and applications, not an organizational event monitoring tool for detecting unauthorized account additions.

category: AIP – Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications
stem: A global e-commerce platform utilizes Amazon SageMaker AI to implement a real-time recommendation system that provides personalized product suggestions. The model is developed using SageMaker Studio. Once trained, the model is hosted on a SageMaker endpoint, enabling it to deliver inferences in real time. Additionally, the company employs Amazon Comprehend to analyze customer feedback and sentiment derived from reviews and product ratings. This analysis helps the company better understand customer preferences and enhance its recommendations. As the business prepares for major sales events, the operations team observes that increased customer activity results in significant delays when retrieving product recommendations, ultimately leading to a poor user experience. To address this issue, there is a need to adjust the target tracking scaling policy on the SageMaker endpoint. The goal is to ensure effective scaling during high-traffic periods, preventing latency from adversely affecting the customer experience. Which solution will best optimize the scaling of the SageMaker inference endpoint?
correct_text: Configure a scheduled scaling policy to increase the capacity of the SageMaker inference endpoint before the sales events begin.
